summary: Associates continental climate with lack of ocean/sea moderation, hot summers, cold winters and large daily and annual fluctuations. It contains no grape biochemistry or Serbian station comparison.
notes: The page is marked as a stub; lower weight than German metric definitions and primary climate data.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Континентална клима
summary: Describes cold winters and comparatively dry summers and gives temperature thresholds, but does not define continentality indices, grape physiology or Serbian regional maxima.
notes: The article explicitly has no cited sources; assigned low reliability despite local language.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Континентальный климат
provenance: Requested Wikipedia edition; general climate article
summary: Links temperate continental climates to large annual amplitude and significant daily change, hot summers, cold winters and large land influence. It offers no grape mechanism or Serbian ranking.
notes: The article is flagged for missing inline citations and disputed reliability; substantive but lower trust than German metric and primary studies.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Kontinentalna klima
provenance: Requested Wikipedia edition; short climate article
summary: Gives cold-winter and warm-summer ranges for continental climate but neither a formal continentality metric nor viticulture/Serbian station evidence.
notes: Marked as lacking sources; ranked below English, German, Hungarian and Russian coverage.

title: English Wikipedia — Diurnal temperature variation
provenance: Largest requested Wikipedia edition; meteorology and viticulture overview
summary: Defines daily maximum–minimum range and lists water bodies, soil/cover, wind, cloud, vapour and ground moisture as controls; repeats the wine-literature idea that cool nights can preserve acid but does not rank Serbia.
notes: Viticulture paragraph is secondary and simplified; primary berry-acid studies take precedence.

title: Journal of Experimental Botany — elevated temperature and organic-acid degradation in ripening grape
summary: Shows that elevated temperature alters malate degradation during veraison/ripening and that day and night heating produce stage-dependent metabolic effects; it does not make tartaric acid or aroma/freshness follow the same simple rule.
notes: Direct physiology evidence; no Serbian cultivar or sensory panel.

title: Scientific Reports — low night temperature at veraison in Corvina
summary: Low night temperature affected Corvina anthocyanin and transcript responses at veraison, while similar post-veraison treatment was ineffective; the study and review context emphasise genotype, phenological stage and temperature-regime dependence.
notes: Primarily anthocyanin rather than aroma-precursor evidence; counters a universal cool-night rule.

title: PLOS One/PMC — vineyard canopy versus standard weather-station temperature
summary: Daily maximum/minimum temperatures within the canopy and around clusters differed significantly from a standard weather station during late spring to early fall, with exposure and canopy height/position affecting differences and model uncertainty.
notes: Measures air around clusters rather than every berry tissue temperature; stations remain valid for regional climatology.

title: Serbian wine-region zoning — station bioclimatic indices
provenance: Published Serbian wine-geography regulation with 1961–2010 station indices
summary: Provides temperature-derived indices including cool-night values for stations across wine regions, but not one homogeneous national ranking of daily maximum–minimum range; thus it cannot verify the stated two maxima.
notes: Strong official regional source; CI is not the same as mean diurnal range or continentality index.

title: Weather Atlas — Palić monthly climate
summary: Reports monthly mean maxima and minima for Palić/Subotica; warm-season differences are roughly 9.5–12.0 °C and nights average about 14–18 °C from June through September, not categorically cold.
notes: Secondary database with unclear exact normal period; used only as indicative, not as proof of a Serbian maximum.

title: Negotin 1991–2020 normals republished from RHMZ
provenance: Engineering document reproducing official RHMZ station table
summary: For Negotin, mean daily maximum minus mean daily minimum is about 12.4 °C annually and about 12.4–13.5 °C from June through September, confirming substantial range but not a national maximum.
notes: Secondary republication of official data; the original RHMZ table should replace it in final editorial sourcing if a stable direct URL is obtained.

title: wein.plus Lexicon — Cool Climate Winegrowing
summary: Presents a trade-oriented continental-climate shorthand of hot days, cold nights and frosty winters; other public entries attribute acidity/aroma intensity to day–night differences, but provide no experiment, Serbian comparison or compound-specific mechanism.
notes: Public unobscured text only; ranked below peer-reviewed physiology and climate normals.

title: SerbianWine.rs — regional climate search
summary: Uses unsourced summaries such as Župa's large day–night swings and Negotin's continental climate, but offers no station method, national comparison, acid experiment or canopy-temperature measurement.
notes: Useful for identifying claims needing verification, not for confirming maxima or biochemical causality.

title: Košava (wind)
provenance: wikipedia-en; article now cites the two principal International Journal of Climatology studies
summary: Defines a cold squally SE wind, northwest Danube/Iron Gates route and jet effect, northern/southern reach, summer occurrence, pressure-system trigger and gap-flow mechanism. It does not supply the Turkish etymology, unique-gap claim, vineyard effect, full foehn asymmetry or Negotin fine-snow duration.
notes: Highest Wikipedia priority, but several opening details still trace to the old AMS glossary rather than to the newer papers.

title: Košava
provenance: wikipedia-de; short article citing Encyclopedia of World Climatology
summary: Supports cold E–SE wind, Iron Gates valley nozzle effect, Banat-to-Niš reach and possible Russian snow. It contains no relevant detail on Ukraine–Moldova parcel path, unique Carpathian breach, Subotica maximum, etymology, summer frequency, vineyards, foehn-side asymmetry or multi-day fine snow.
notes: Independent encyclopedia citation, but much narrower than EN and SR.

title: Szél — named-winds list, Kosava entry
provenance: wikipedia-hu; general wind article, no dedicated Košava page
summary: The sole relevant line calls Kosava a SE wind passing through the Iron Gates toward eastern Serbia and Vojvodina. It has no relevant material for the detailed route, uniqueness, acceleration metric, southern-Banat maximum, etymology, seasonal/viticultural effects, foehn asymmetry or snow duration.
notes: Lower evidentiary weight because the entry is one unspecialised list item.

title: Кошава
provenance: wikipedia-sr; local-language article citing Serbian climatology and the peer-reviewed trend study
summary: Supports Carpathian SE wind, dry/cold but sometimes warm variants, autumn–winter prevalence, Subotica reach, Ukraine/Mediterranean pressure pattern, greatest strength at Iron Gates entrance, explicit summer Košava and multi-day persistence. It gives no etymology, vineyard study or full foehn/windward explanation.
notes: Valuable local geography; part of the text overlaps EN/AMS and therefore is not wholly independent.

title: Кошава (ветер)
provenance: wikipedia-ru; unreviewed current version with weak references
summary: Supports a dry dusty Carpathian wind in the middle/lower Danube, October–March prevalence, Ukrainian-anticyclone/Adriatic-low mechanism, Subotica reach and greatest force at the Iron Gates entrance. It has no relevant etymology, vineyard effect, summer discussion, foehn asymmetry or local fine-snow duration.
notes: Rank below EN/DE/SR because the article itself relies partly on outdated popular pages and personal blogs.

title: Košava
provenance: wikipedia-hr; text closely follows Hrvatska enciklopedija
summary: Supports the Turkish koş + hava derivation, dry SE–S wind, cold-season prevalence, southern Hungary/Podunavlje/Banat/Pomoravlje range and Mediterranean-low/NE-Europe-high mechanism. It contains no relevant Iron Gates route, acceleration, unique breach, exact maximum, summer/vineyard effects, foehn asymmetry or fine snow.
notes: Do not count separately from Hrvatska enciklopedija for etymological consensus.

title: International Journal of Climatology — Contributing factors to Koshava wind characteristics
summary: Finds Košava usually in the cold part of the year across much of Serbia and nearby countries; a strong Eurasian anticyclone is the main trigger, Mediterranean cyclone usually co-occurs, and across-mountain pressure difference dominates the gap-flow characteristics. It does not support a fixed Ukraine–Moldova air-parcel route or an exclusively gorge/foehn narrative.
notes: Abstract is public; full methods/results should be consulted before extracting station-level rankings.

title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — The Danube Limes (Romania), Iron Gates component
summary: Calls Iron Gates the last and most important 130-km mountain breach between the South Carpathians and Balkans, from Golubac toward the Timok mouth; it does not call it the sole major rupture of the complete Carpathian arc.
notes: Supports «major breach», refutes the unsupported superlative «only».

title: BBC News na srpskom via Danas — Košava i mitovi
provenance: BBC interview with University of Belgrade climatology professor Vladan Ducić, republished intact
summary: Explains the Ukraine/Carpathian anticyclone and Mediterranean cyclone, Iron Gates-to-Vojvodina/Morava route, maximum intensity in southeastern Banat, warm and cold variants, and the recurrent windward cloudy/precipitating Timok versus leeward warming/drying pattern described as foehn/katabatic.
notes: Expert explanation, not a peer-reviewed event climatology; use conditional language for regime frequency.

title: Municipality of Negotin — Location, climate and population
summary: Describes Košava as a frequent cold eastern winter wind in Negotin, weaker than gornjak, that can cause several days of fine snow; also notes earlier snow cover under moist cold waves from east or northeast.
notes: Old and poorly translated municipal text without observations table; supports local description, not national generalisation.

title: RTS/RHMZ forecasts — southern Banat gusts and Timok weather contrast
provenance: RTS republication of Republic Hydrometeorological Service warning
summary: During a January 2026 Košava episode, RHMZ warned of storm to hurricane SE gusts in southern Banat while Timočka Krajina was cold, overcast and subject to freezing rain or granular snow; other RTS/RHMZ reports document May Košava and the same Banat/Timok contrast.
notes: Event evidence, not long-term causality; May report: https://www.rts.rs/lat/vesti/srbija-danas/5441688/olujna-kosava-u-vrscu.html .

title: Agricultural and Forest Meteorology — prevailing wind, canopy asymmetry and fruit-zone irradiance
summary: Prevailing growing-season wind shortened windward shoots by 26–29%, displaced shoot tips, produced canopy asymmetry and changed the timing and distribution of fruit-zone irradiance, with potential unequal berry ripening.
notes: Not a Serbian or Košava vineyard; establishes plausible wind mechanisms, not local effect size.

title: Grapes Extension — Wind Damage to Grapevines
provenance: University/extension viticulture guidance reviewed by Cornell and Texas A&M specialists
summary: Documents spring/early-summer shoot breakage, leaf damage and photosynthesis loss, fruit rubbing, trellis risk and possible flowering/fertilisation effects under heavy persistent wind.
notes: General strong-wind evidence; no attribution of any specific Serbian vineyard outcome to Košava.

title: Hrvatska enciklopedija — košava
provenance: Leksikografski zavod Miroslav Krleža national encyclopedia
summary: Gives the conventional Turkish koş «fast» + hava «air» etymology and defines Košava as a dry squally SE–S wind blowing predominantly in the cold season, not exclusively within fixed calendar months.
notes: Croatian Wikipedia closely reproduces this entry and is not an independent second source.

title: International Journal of Climatology — Long-term trends of the Koshava wind, 1949–2010
summary: Defines Košava as a strong SE-quadrant wind over Serbia/Bulgaria/Romania and analyses 1949–2010 at five stations where the wind is fully developed; the public abstract does not establish an October–April hard limit or a national southern-Banat superlative.
notes: Already used in earlier Košava audit; retained here because the current block makes new seasonal and maximum claims.

title: wein.plus public lexicon and Wine Guide — Košava search
provenance: User-requested public wine lexicon/search; unobscured content only
summary: No relevant public Košava climate entry or Serbian vineyard-specific effect evidence was found; search hits for similar strings concern wine names rather than this meteorological regime.
notes: No Premium text, blurred content or access restriction was bypassed.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Košava and vineyard search
summary: No relevant public article defining Košava, its foehn asymmetry, or quantified effects on Serbian vineyards was found in site search; winery/event pages do not test the book's meteorological claims.
notes: No new missing winery, region or wine object arose from this topic search, so no gaps record was added.

title: Albedo; related Mosel and Wachau wine-region articles
provenance: wikipedia-en; most detailed requested-language optical treatment
summary: Defines albedo as reflected fraction, tabulates open ocean 0.06, bare soil 0.17 and green grass 0.25, and explains low/medium-incidence water reflectivity, grazing-angle increase and locally specular glint. The Mosel article says river reflection maximises sunlight at best sites, while Wachau says the Danube moderates climate. It gives no measured Serbian winter footprint, universal kilometre threshold, Danube-ice series or forest-frost drainage test.
notes: Related pages: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosel_%28wine_region%29 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wachau_wine . The Mosel line cites a general wine atlas, not a site radiometry experiment.

title: Albedo; Mosel (Weinanbaugebiet)
provenance: wikipedia-de; technically useful general optics page
summary: Explains that smooth surfaces such as water have a substantial specular component and that albedo depends strongly on incidence angle. The German Mosel wine-region article does not provide the book's quantitative 3–8% vineyard calculation, a universal reflection-distance result, Serbian Danube winter buffering/ice measurements or the forest-frost mechanism.
notes: Related page checked: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosel_%28Weinanbaugebiet%29 . Its climate description is not a radiometric validation of reflected light on vines.

title: Albedó
summary: Defines albedo/reflected-radiation ratio but supplies no relevant detailed water-angle geometry, Mosel/Douro vineyard-reflection assessment, Serbian Danube frost footprint or ice climatology, or forest/windbreak cold-air drainage evidence for these claims.
notes: No dedicated Hungarian Wikipedia treatment of the combined river–vineyard–forest mechanism was found.

title: Албедо
provenance: wikipedia-sr; local language but very short physics coverage
summary: Gives the basic albedo definition but no relevant numerical river-water range and angular/specular vineyard geometry, no measured Danube-side frost distance or modern ice frequency, and no vineyard forest/windbreak cold-air-flow analysis.
notes: Local-language priority does not compensate for the absence of Serbian field measurements in the article.

title: Вода — оптические свойства; Альбедо
provenance: wikipedia-ru; quantitative line is weakly sourced
summary: The water article says water reflects about 5% of solar rays, consistent with the book's order of magnitude, but does not state the applicable angle, spectrum, surface condition or vineyard geometry. The Russian albedo material adds no relevant Mosel/Douro test, Danube winter footprint/ice climatology or forest-frost drainage analysis.
notes: The 5% line cites a generic ocean-optics web item and ranks below peer-reviewed angular albedo measurements.

title: Albedo
summary: Defines albedo as the ratio of reflected to incident radiation but contains no relevant detailed water reflectance/angle comparison, vineyard reflection measurement, Serbian Danube frost footprint or ice history, or forest-controlled cold-air drainage evidence.
notes: No Croatian Wikipedia article found that independently tests the book's river-vineyard optical claims.

title: Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans — Albedo of a water surface
provenance: Peer-reviewed aircraft, mast and ship irradiance measurements
summary: Shows that water-surface albedo varies with spectral band, atmospheric transmittance/cloudiness, solar altitude and wind; it reports agreement with classic angle-dependent measurements but deviations at high Sun and below 20° altitude, precluding a universal 3–8% constant or sunset-only threshold.
notes: The public abstract does not provide a Mosel/Danube slope irradiance calculation.

title: Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans — Observation and Parameterization of Broadband Sea Surface Albedo
summary: Finds broadband sea-surface albedo changes little under high Sun in clear sky, rises strongly with solar zenith angle at low Sun, is much less angle-dependent under cloud, and also varies with wind/waves and water-vapour pressure.
notes: Sea observations establish physics but not the effect size for a narrow freshwater river and opposing vineyard slope.

title: NOAA NESDIS — Sunglint
summary: Defines sunglint as sunlight reflected from water at the same angle at which a sensor receives it, confirming directional/specular geometry; the receiving direction changes with source, observer and surface orientation rather than being universally sideways.
notes: Satellite viewing geometry is analogous to a slope receiver but does not quantify grape-canopy irradiance.

title: NASA Earth Observatory — Moselle River Gorge, Germany
provenance: NASA landscape caption citing Ronald Jackson's Wine Science and contemporary Wikipedia
summary: Explicitly states that reflected light from the Moselle surface is known to help vines on favoured slopes. This documents the narrative and conflicts with a categorical physical dismissal, but it is a secondary caption rather than an instrumented vineyard radiative-budget study.
notes: Keep evidentiary weight below direct logger/radiometer work; the caption's references do not report a site-specific effect size.

title: Sustainability — Cooling Effect of an Urban River: mobile measurement study
provenance: Peer-reviewed mobile transect measurement beside the Yangtze in Wuhan
summary: On one hot humid summer day, measured daytime cooling reached 3.55°C and an inferred influence distance of 1,741 m, with humidity and heat-stress effects also extending beyond one kilometre; nighttime effects were weaker. It directly disproves a universal sub-kilometre rule but is not winter vineyard evidence.
notes: Urban morphology and a roughly 2-km-wide river limit transfer to the Serbian Danube; use only to establish context dependence.

title: Water — Numerical Study on the Influence of Rivers on Urban Microclimate
provenance: Peer-reviewed numerical case study in Chengdu
summary: Models temperature/humidity differences over 0–50 m bands and shows bank side, wind passage through woods/road/river and surrounding form alter the effect, illustrating that short footprints also occur and that no fixed universal distance follows from water alone.
notes: Urban summer model, not direct winter-vineyard validation.

title: Scientific Reports via AWI — Vanishing river ice cover in the lower Danube basin
provenance: Research-institute summary linking the peer-reviewed long record
summary: Danube Commission records at Tulcea show near-annual ice before the mid-twentieth century but only ten freezing winters from 1951–2016; warmer winters and human heat/wastewater inflows have made extended freezing rare.
notes: Lower-Danube station history does not describe every Serbian reach; DOI 10.1038/s41598-018-26357-w.

title: Government of Serbia — navigation reopened after 2017 Danube ice
provenance: Official Serbian Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure release
summary: Reports more than a month of Serbian and Hungarian icebreaker operations against Danube ice jams at Apatin, Dalj, Đerdap, Surduk, Novi Banovci, Grocka and Smederevo, with navigation closed from 8 January to 10 February 2017.
notes: Confirms extensive ice and disruption, not necessarily a continuous bank-to-bank freeze at every named location.

title: BC Wine Grape Council — Site Selection
summary: States that large water bodies moderate surrounding temperatures and separately stresses slope, aspect, heat accumulation, frost pockets and cold-air drainage, supporting a first-order buffer while showing the full site effect cannot be reduced to water proximity alone.
notes: Lake-oriented Canadian guidance; no Danube distance or winter frost-effect measurement.

title: BC Wine Grape Council — Frost Protection
summary: Explains radiative versus advective frost, downslope cold-air drift and pooling; warns that windbreaks can help in advective freezes but often worsen radiative frosts by slowing drainage and ponding cold air uphill, with barrier placement and pruning critical.
notes: Natural forest is not identical to a designed windbreak, but both can act as porous flow barriers.

title: University of Georgia — Vineyard Frost Protection
summary: Cold air follows drainage pathways like water and pools at the bottom of sloped or concave terrain in radiation frost; exposed convex sites can be safer then but more vulnerable during advective freezes, confirming the regime-dependent reversal.
notes: Southeastern US guidance; mechanism is general but local thresholds require Serbian measurements.

title: Ecology and Evolution — Frequent and strong cold-air pooling drives temperate forest composition
summary: Finds cold-air pooling in 19–43% of seasonal observations and strong spatial complexity; fine topography and forest canopy may shelter inversions from solar heating and wind mixing, supporting forest modulation without a universal protective sign.
notes: New England forests, not Serbian vineyards; use for mechanism and variability only.

title: Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology — Cold-Air Pooling in the Upper Douro Valley
provenance: Peer-reviewed seven-year high-frequency vineyard weather-station study
summary: Identifies 834 cold pools (32% of nights) near the Douro, mostly in winter/early spring, and explains that pools can prolong fog/frost or sometimes benefit phenology/heat stress. The authors explicitly say the Douro water body's exact winter effect on cold pools is unknown and note increased winter fog after dams.
notes: Strongest selected vineyard-valley microclimate source; it does not isolate forest-barrier effects or reflected solar irradiance.

title: wein.plus public lexicon — river, albedo, frost and windbreak search
provenance: User-requested public wine lexicon/search; unobscured content only
summary: No public entry was found that quantifies a Danube frost-buffer footprint, validates the 3–8% water-to-vine irradiance calculation, sets a kilometre cutoff or tests Serbian forest-controlled cold-air drainage; general regional entries are descriptive rather than experimental.
notes: No Premium text, blurred content or access restriction was bypassed.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Danube vineyard microclimate and reflection search
summary: Public pages identify Danube slopes, viewpoints and nearby wineries but provide no measured river-frost distance, water albedo or vineyard irradiance, modern ice climatology, or forest/windbreak cold-air-flow test. Topic search returned objects already present in the book or prior gaps audit, so no new gap was added here.
notes: Marketing proximity/view language must not be treated as physical causality; no text was copied into the book.

title: English Wikipedia — cold-air pool, lapse rate and Toplica cross-check
provenance: Largest Wikipedia edition; cross-checked with Lapse rate, Inversion (meteorology), Toplica (South Morava) and Aleksandrovac
summary: Defines cold-air pooling as accumulation of dense cooled air in depressions, explains nocturnal downslope flow and frost risk, and the lapse-rate article states that temperature normally decreases with height but the environmental rate varies and can invert. The Toplica article places its central depression between Jastrebac and the southern mountains and notes grapes; Aleksandrovac supplies no comparable Župa climate analysis.
notes: No relevant material on Serbian register altitude percentages, variety-specific elevation preference, Župa season length or the speed of seasonal transitions.

title: German Wikipedia — Inversionswetterlage and Aleksandrovac cross-check
provenance: Large German-language general encyclopedia; cross-checked with Kaltluftsee and Aleksandrovac
summary: Defines an inversion as warmer air above cooler air, says topography makes inversions more frequent in mountains and describes extreme nocturnal ground inversions produced by cold-air inflow into small basins. Aleksandrovac is identified with the Župa wine area but no local climate mechanism is quantified.
notes: No relevant material on the three varieties' altitude distributions, Serbian vineyard-height totals, harvest delay, protected-season length or transition speed.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Inverzió (meteorológia) cross-check
provenance: Hungarian-language general encyclopedia; verified article version
summary: Defines inversion as higher temperature aloft, gives the usual average decrease of 0.65 °C per 100 m and explains clear calm nocturnal surface cooling. It does not describe cold-air drainage in Serbian wine basins or any variety/elevation dataset.
notes: No relevant Župa/Toplica geography, altitude percentages, growing-season length, harvest timing or seasonal-transition material was found.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Топлица (река) and basin cross-check
provenance: Serbian-language general encyclopedia; related Toplica region page and site search checked
summary: Describes the Toplica as a composite valley alternating gorges and basins and locates its basin relief between named mountains. No standalone Serbian inversion article or vineyard-height statistical treatment relevant to the book's figures was found.
notes: No relevant material on Župa enclosure, temperature moderation, growing-season extension, cultivar altitude shares or rapid seasonal transitions.

title: Russian Wikipedia — температурная инверсия and Toplica cross-check
provenance: Large Russian-language general encyclopedia; cross-checked with Топлица (река)
summary: Defines temperature inversion and explicitly says that on clear calm nights cold air can descend slopes and collect in valleys, leaving them colder than locations 100–200 m above. The Toplica article locates the river among Kopaonik/Radan relief but does not supply the fuller vineyard-basin or climate claims.
notes: No relevant cultivar-height statistics, Župa geography, season-length measurement or transition-speed definition.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Temperaturna inverzija cross-check
provenance: Croatian-language general encyclopedia; article draws partly on Hrvatska enciklopedija
summary: Defines inversion as temperature increasing with altitude and explains radiative inversion after clear nights when the ground and near-surface air cool strongly. It does not discuss Serbian vineyard statistics or local Župa/Toplica climate.
notes: The page is partly derivative of Hrvatska enciklopedija and provides no independent support for cultivar shares, mountain protection, season length or transitions.

title: CEVVIN — Виноградарство и винарство Србије (2019), section 3.5 Topographic factors
provenance: CEVVIN analysis of Ministry of Agriculture Viticultural Register data; 19,208 registered vineyard parcels
summary: Reports 39.54% of parcels above 100–200 m, 27.32% above 200–300 m and 26.80% above 300 m, with source attribution to MPŠV/CEVVIN and the 2019 register. It describes altitude, slope and aspect as indirect topographic controls through microclimate and soil.
notes: The prose reports parcel counts, not the exact vineyard-area share within 100–400 m; the plotted higher bins are not numerically transcribed in the accessible text.

title: CEVVIN — Prokupac cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar and register profile
summary: Classifies Prokupac as ripening between epochs III and IV and states that its largest registered vineyard-area altitude bin is above 300–400 m at 43.80%. The accessible profile does not state that 22% lies above 400 m.
notes: Observed planting distribution is not evidence of an innate altitude preference; the page does not state the register snapshot date or full altitude table.

title: CEVVIN — Vranac cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar and register profile
summary: Places Vranac ripening in epoch III and reports its largest registered vineyard-area altitude bin above 300–400 m at 60.80%, matching the rounded 61% in the book.
notes: The page reports a descriptive distribution, not a controlled biological site-preference test.

title: CEVVIN — Smederevka cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar and register profile
summary: Calls Smederevka very late-ripening (epoch IV) and states that its largest registered vineyard-area altitude bin is above 200–300 m at 37.11%, directly conflicting with the book's 50% at 100–200 m.
notes: A different historical snapshot or denominator could explain the conflict only if explicitly documented; none was found in the selected corpus.

title: Plants — Alpine Viticulture and Climate Change: Environmental Resources and Limitations for Grapevine Ripening in Valtellina, Italy
provenance: Peer-reviewed multi-site and multi-season vineyard analysis
summary: Uses a general temperature decrease of roughly 0.45–0.65 °C per 100 m but shows that aspect and site radiation can make lower sites cooler and that the highest vineyard need not finish ripening latest. Higher/cooler sites often ripen later, but altitude is not a deterministic harvest clock.
notes: Italian Alpine vineyards, not Serbia; appropriate for mechanism, not local harvest dates.

title: Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology — Cold-Air Pooling in the Upper Douro Valley
provenance: Peer-reviewed seven-year high-frequency vineyard weather-station study
summary: Identifies 834 cold-air pools on 32% of nights and shows that valley bottoms can be colder than slopes during stable nocturnal conditions. The events depend on season, wind and topography and can affect frost, fog and phenology.
notes: Douro measurements confirm the mechanism and variability but cannot supply Župa or Toplica frequency or growing-season length.

title: Vino & Fino / Association of Winemakers and Winegrowers of Serbia — Vinograde čuvaju planine: Toplički rejon
provenance: Regional profile published with the Serbian national winegrowers' association
summary: Places Toplica vineyards at 250–400 m and describes them as protected from harsh weather by Veliki/Mali Jastrebac, Vidojevica and Pasjača, with warm sunny days and fresh nights.
notes: Descriptive trade press without station comparisons, frost dates or a test of reduced extremes and longer season.

title: Fragaria Winery — Župa vineyard location and microclimate
provenance: Primary producer description of its Lukarevina site in Župa
summary: States that the vineyard is surrounded by Kopaonik, Željin, Goč and Jastrebac and characterises its site as mild and protected from winter frost and cold wind.
notes: Promotional single-site statement; it does not establish conditions across all Župa or quantify extremes, frost-free days or season length.

title: wein.plus public wine-region and lexicon search — Serbia altitude and basin climate
provenance: User-requested specialist database; public and unobscured material only
summary: The public Serbia guide lists West Morava/Župa and Southern Morava among nine growing regions but does not publish the Serbian register altitude bins, cultivar-specific percentages, local inversion frequency, mountain-induced growing-season extension or transition metrics.
notes: No Premium text, blurred content or access restriction was bypassed; no new missing object beyond already audited regional/winery gaps was exposed in this block.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Toplica, Župa, altitude and harvest search
provenance: User-requested Serbian public wine-tourism and educational site
summary: The Toplički Vinogradi page uses general favourable-microclimate language, while the harvest guide gives broad region and high-altitude harvest windows. Neither supplies the register percentages, local inversion measurements, mountain-protection effect size, season length or transition speed.
notes: Toplički Vinogradi and its missing portfolio are already recorded in prior gaps G0315–G0316; no duplicate gap was added.

title: English Wikipedia — autochthon concept and grape usage cross-check
provenance: Largest Wikipedia edition; cross-checked with Autochthon (ancient Greece), Gringet and multiple grape pages
summary: Glosses an autochthon in nature as an indigenous plant or animal; grape pages use «autochthonous» for varieties native or unique to a region even when exact historical origin is uncertain. It supplies no Serbian local-versus-international area comparison or objective test of regional character.
notes: The general page is a disambiguation rather than a viticulture standard; specialist evidence carries greater weight.

title: German Wikipedia — Autochthon terminology cross-check
provenance: Large German-language general encyclopedia; related grape-variety pages checked
summary: Defines autochthon as native, indigenous or originated here and describes autochthonous biological species as long present without human introduction. German grape pages apply the term to a cultivar's home region, not merely long residence after introduction.
notes: No relevant Serbian vineyard-area table or test that local cultivars explain regional style.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — local/international Serbian grape classification search
provenance: Hungarian Wikipedia site search and related wine/grape pages checked
summary: No Hungarian Wikipedia article was found that defines autochthonous grape cultivars, quantifies Serbian local versus international vineyard area or evaluates the regional-character proposition.
notes: Individual grape pages using őshonos do not provide a controlled terminology standard for this claim.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — аутохтоне сорте and Serbian variety-area search
provenance: Serbian Wikipedia site search and grape/wine pages checked
summary: No Serbian Wikipedia page was found that formally separates autochthonous, regional, traditional and introduced grape cultivars or gives a national area balance between them.
notes: Scattered use of «аутохтона сорта» is descriptive and does not validate the book's expanded definition.

title: Russian Wikipedia — автохтонный сорт винограда usage cross-check
provenance: Russian-language general encyclopedia; terminology and Serbian-area search checked
summary: Uses «автохтонный» for a cultivar presented as Armenian and locally endemic, consistent with native-origin usage, but provides no general definition and no Serbian local/international area data.
notes: The Areni page is not a terminology authority and some of its sourcing is weak; it is not used to verify Serbian cultivars.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — autohtone sorte vinove loze and Serbian area search
provenance: Croatian Wikipedia site search and wine/grape pages checked
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia article was found that supplies a formal grape-specific definition, a Serbian planted-area split or an evidence-based regional-character test.
notes: Ordinary adjectival use of autohton does not distinguish native origin from long-established imported material.

title: CEVVIN — Виноградарство и винарство Србије (2019), varietal structure
provenance: CEVVIN analysis of Ministry Viticultural Register data
summary: Reports that the ten leading cultivars account for 69.85% of commercial area and that, apart from Prokupac and the domestic-bred Župljanka, the leaders are predominantly international; it separately groups autochthonous and regional varieties and notes that Graševina is regional even when presented with international varieties.
notes: The study does not publish one complete autochthonous-versus-international percentage split, and its categories must not be silently collapsed.

title: Life — Analysis of Wine-Producing Vitis vinifera Biotypes, Autochthonous to Crete
summary: Explicitly defines autochthonous cultivars as indigenous—native to the origin where they were found—and distinguishes old/autochthonous, widespread non-autochthonous and locally selected hybrids. It also stresses genetic typing because synonyms, homonyms and presumed origins are uncertain.
notes: Greek case study, but the terminology and identification problem are directly transferable.

title: OIV — Ancient variety and cultivated variety terminology
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine resolution on old grapevine diversity
summary: Uses «ancient variety» for old grape cultivars whose human selection history does not fit botanical variety or a single identified modern cultivar breeder, demonstrating that great age and uncertain selection history have their own terminology rather than automatically proving autochthony.
notes: The resolution does not itself define autochthonous; it is complementary terminological evidence.

title: wein.plus Serbia region table — current cultivar hectares
provenance: User-requested specialist wine database; public and unobscured regional table
summary: Its 2023 table lists Cabernet Sauvignon 2,111 ha, Welschriesling/Graševina 2,037, Merlot 1,968, Chardonnay 1,455 and Riesling 1,361 before Prokupac 916, strongly supporting international/regional cultivar area dominance. It does not define autochthonous or prove that local varieties determine regional character.
notes: The table mixes Welschriesling/Graševina, which CEVVIN calls regional, with clearly international cultivars; no Premium text was used.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Serbian Indigenous Grape Varieties guide
provenance: User-requested Serbian public wine-tourism and educational site
summary: Presents indigenous cultivars as carriers of regional identity and lists regions and style claims, supporting that this framing is common in Serbian wine communication. It does not define autochthonous rigorously or quantify the planted-area split.
notes: Several cultivar-history and descriptor statements on the page require separate fact checks in their own blocks; all named core varieties already occur in the book, so no new gap is added here.

title: English Wikipedia — Prokupac
provenance: Largest Wikipedia edition; concise cultivar article
summary: Defines Prokupac as a Serbian red wine grape, lists Kamenicarka and Rskavac as synonyms, gives only broad freshness and dark-fruit character, and identifies Three Moravas, Toplica, Šumadija and Leskovac as major planting areas, with additional plantings elsewhere. It does not provide the card's detailed tannin, phenology or tertiary-descriptor profile.
notes: Highest Wikipedia priority, but the short article is less detailed than Serbian specialist and professional tasting sources.

title: German Wikipedia — Prokupac
summary: Lists Kamenicarka/Kamenicharka and Rskavac as synonyms, describes Prokupac as late ripening with thick berry skin, and characterises its wine only broadly as fruity and spicy. It does not establish the detailed body, tannin, named fruit, age-development or Serbian regional list.
notes: The synonym list cites the VIVC identity tradition; broad fruit/spice wording cannot validate every descriptor.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Prokupac, Rskavac, Kameničarka
summary: No standalone Hungarian article or comparable Hungarian-language profile was found for Prokupac synonyms, phenology, structure, descriptors, ageing or Serbian planting geography.
notes: Hungarian Wikipedia contributes no evidence to the card-level consensus.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Прокупац
summary: Provides brief local agronomic context for the vigorous, productive cultivar but no comparable detailed sensory profile, age-development sequence or quantitative regional planting account for this card. Its information is supplemented rather than replaced by CEVVIN.
notes: The Serbian CEVVIN profile is more detailed and authoritative for ampelography and registered areas.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Прокупац, Рскавац, Каменичарка
provenance: Russian Wikipedia search and Serbian-wine overview check
summary: No standalone Russian Prokupac article with the card's synonymy, ampelography, sensory descriptors or regional geography was found; the Russian wine-in-Serbia overview only supplies general national cultivar context.
notes: Russian Wikipedia contributes no detailed definition or descriptor consensus.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Prokupac, Rskavac, Kameničarka
summary: No standalone Croatian article or comparable Croatian-language profile was found for Prokupac synonymy, phenology, sensory descriptors, ageing or Serbian regional distribution.
notes: Croatian Wikipedia contributes no evidence to the card-level consensus.

title: CEVVIN — Prokupac cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar and register profile
summary: Lists Kameničarka and Rskavac among synonyms; describes medium round berries with thick blue-black skin, ripening between epochs III and IV, and refreshing red/ruby wine. It states that longer pomace contact extracts tannin and can make the wine astringent, and identifies Three Moravas, Toplica and Leskovac as leading regions, with Župsko vinogorje the largest named area in its register snapshot.
notes: The profile's area list is a register snapshot and does not make the book's three-region list exhaustive; Šumadija is supported independently.

title: VIVC passport 9734 — Prokupac
provenance: Vitis International Variety Catalogue, Julius Kühn-Institut
summary: Canonical international cultivar-identity record for Prokupac; direct automated retrieval was refused in this pass, while the record identifier and Rskavac/Kameničarka synonymy are reproduced by the EN/DE Wikipedia articles and specialist databases.
notes: Used only as an identity anchor, not as direct support for sensory or regional claims.

title: wein.plus public glossary — Prokupac
provenance: User-requested specialist wine database; public unobscured glossary entry
summary: Lists Kameničarka and Rskavac among the many Prokupac synonyms and cautiously locates origin in the Balkans, possibly Serbia. The accessible entry does not supply the detailed sensory and ageing profile in the book.
notes: No Premium, blurred or otherwise access-controlled content was extracted or reconstructed.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Serbian Indigenous Grape Varieties
summary: Describes Prokupac as medium-bodied and juicy, with sour cherry, plum, wild herbs, silky tannins and vivid acidity, and names Župa, Three Moravas, Nišava-Toplica and Šumadija. This supports the broad modern style and geography but not every detailed descriptor or an invariant tannin level.
notes: Tourism-facing editorial overview, lower than CEVVIN for ampelography and lower than blinded research for causal sensory claims; text is paraphrased.

title: Foods — Procyanidins and Anthocyanins in Young and Aged Prokupac Wines
provenance: Peer-reviewed comparison of selected young and aged Prokupac wines and salivary-protein reactivity
summary: Reports greater acidity and astringency in the studied young Prokupac and improved tannin quality in the aged wine; sensory and chemical differences show that age and matrix alter perceived structure. The experiment concerns selected wines and does not prove that every young wine is coarse or that leather, tobacco and forest floor arise universally with age.
notes: More probative for structural change than descriptive marketing, but not a population-wide cultivar survey.

title: JancisRobinson.com — Made in Serbia
provenance: Professional comparative tasting report by Julia Harding MW
summary: Across multiple Prokupac wines, the report records cherry-family fruit, raspberry, plum, violet, pepper, herbal notes, tobacco and forest-floor character. The descriptors are independently useful as a range, but each belongs to one or more particular wines rather than every expression of the cultivar.
notes: All observations are paraphrased and kept below quotation limits; the report does not isolate ageing as the sole cause of tertiary notes.

title: Vino Budimir — Prokupac Boje Lila
provenance: Official page for a Župa Prokupac aged in oak
summary: Describes a medium-plus-bodied wine with pleasant tannins and cherry, raspberry, mint, plum-jam, cedar, leather and vanilla notes after extended oak ageing. It confirms that these notes occur in a specific mature example, not that they are cultivar constants.
notes: Producer is primary for its own wine and technology but interested for general varietal claims; text is paraphrased.

title: Vinarija Marko — Doajen Prokupac
provenance: Official product page with technology and analysis
summary: Describes a medium-bodied Prokupac with fresh acidity, soft tannins and cherry, plum, violet, spice, earth, pepper and tobacco after French-oak and amphora ageing. It supports occurrence in one wine and demonstrates that oak and vessel history confound a simple age-only explanation.
notes: Producer copy is paraphrased and not treated as an independent blinded tasting.

title: Vinarija Aleksandrović — Prokupac
summary: Names ripe cherry and sweet-cherry-like fruit together with currant, clove, cinnamon and vanilla for a barrel-aged Prokupac. It is direct evidence that a sweet-cherry reading occurs for a specific wine, but not proof that generic English cherry should always be translated as черешня.
notes: Product-specific producer evidence; additional spice and oak notes are useful omissions for later editorial review, not universal cultivar descriptors.

title: English Wikipedia — Tamjanika
provenance: Largest Wikipedia edition; short cultivar-family article
summary: Places Tamjanika in the Muscat family and treats it as a probable descendant/expression of Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains; describes very strong grape aroma and gives elder, cinnamon and basil for white wine. It does not rank Serbian whites, isolate sweetness perception, give Župa primacy or recommend a service temperature.
notes: The article mixes dark and white Tamjanika forms, so colour/accession context is essential.

title: German Wikipedia — Tamjanika Crna
summary: Covers only dark Tamjanika Crna/Rosenmuskateller, not the white Tamjanika card; its red-grape ampelography, rose-spice profile and sweet-wine context cannot be transferred to white Tamjanika.
notes: Useful mainly as a warning that the shared name spans distinct colour forms.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Tamjanika white Muscat Župa
summary: No Hungarian article was found that identifies white Tamjanika, gives its Serbian descriptor profile, Župa geography, sweetness-perception mechanism or service temperature.
notes: Hungarian Wikipedia contributes no card-level consensus.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — Тамјаника Жупа мускат
summary: No standalone Serbian article with comparable white-Tamjanika ampelography, descriptors, sweetness science, Župa distribution or service guidance was found.
notes: SerbianWine.rs and the national wine association are more informative, but are not Wikipedia.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Тамьяника Жупа мускат
summary: No Russian Wikipedia profile was found for white Tamjanika, its Serbian descriptors, sweetness-perception mechanism or serving temperature.
notes: Russian Wikipedia contributes no card-level evidence.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Tamjanika bijeli muškat Župa
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia article was found that covers the white Serbian Tamjanika card, its descriptors, perceived sweetness or service range.
notes: Croatian muscat material does not establish the Serbian local-name identity without an accession link.

title: wein.plus public glossary — Tamjanika
provenance: User-requested specialist wine lexicon; public unobscured entry
summary: Places Tamjanika/Tamyanka among country and local names associated with Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, while a separate Tamjanika Bela entry illustrates unresolved or inconsistent nomenclature.
notes: No Premium or blurred material was used; identity of a specific Serbian accession still requires genetic documentation.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Tamjanika: Serbia’s Aromatic White Wine
summary: Describes white Tamjanika as an intensely aromatic Serbian expression of Muscat Blanc, commonly fresh and dry, with jasmine, elderflower, orange blossom, lemon peel, mandarin, grape, peach and herbs. It explains that strong floral-fruit aroma can suggest sweetness despite low residual sugar.
notes: Editorial wine guide rather than a genetic database or controlled sensory study; all wording is paraphrased.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Župa & the Three Moravas Wine Route
summary: Highlights Tamjanika alongside Prokupac in Župa and the wider Three Moravas wine route, supporting the region's central cultural and commercial association with the cultivar.
notes: Tourism framing is not a national planted-area ranking; Tamjanika also occurs outside Župa.

title: Union of Winemakers and Winegrowers of Serbia — I’m picking grapes, I’m choosing Tamjanika
provenance: Serbian national wine association educational article
summary: Calls fruit and floral aromas dominant and lists citrus plus incense, basil and cinnamon among subtler notes; confirms Tamjanika's pronounced aromatic character but publishes no comparison ranking every Serbian white cultivar.
notes: Industry overview supports typicality, not a measured superlative.

title: Food Chemistry — effects of wine volatiles on taste and astringency perception
summary: Finds that wine volatiles can alter taste judgments and that perceived sweetness in dry wine is closely associated with congruent fruit aroma even without corresponding sugar addition.
notes: The experiment does not isolate Tamjanika or muscat terpenes; residual sugar, alcohol and acidity remain relevant to sweetness.

title: BalkanWines — Tamjanika Bellucci
provenance: Public technical page for a dry still Tamjanika
summary: Recommends serving the dry, steel-aged Tamjanika at 8–12 °C.
notes: One wine outside Župa; service advice is style-specific rather than a universal rule for all Tamjanika categories.

title: Frug — Tamjanika
provenance: Official page for a fresh dry Tamjanika
summary: Recommends 8–10 °C for its dry, steel-aged Tamjanika, independently fitting inside the book's 8–12 °C range.
notes: Does not establish service for sparkling, sweet, orange or oak-aged Tamjanika.

title: English Wikipedia — Tamjanika
provenance: Largest Wikipedia edition; brief family article
summary: Calls red Tamjanika rare and aromatic and places Tamjanika traditions in Serbia and neighbouring Balkan countries, but gives no exact Rosenmuskateller identity, Negotin production frequency, polusuvarak stage or dehydration mechanism.
notes: Its mixing of white and red forms makes specialist identity sources necessary.

title: German Wikipedia — Tamjanika Crna
provenance: Most detailed Wikipedia edition for this cultivar
summary: Identifies Tamjanika Crna with the very rare Balkan Rosenmuskateller/Moscato Rosa complex and describes intensely rose- and spice-scented wines, often sweet in its South Tyrolean context. It does not establish Negotin harvest frequency or the Serbian polusuvarak terminology.
notes: South Tyrolean style information cannot automatically describe Serbian dry and sweet examples.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Crna Tamjanika Rosenmuskateller Negotin
summary: No Hungarian article was found defining Crna Tamjanika identity, Negotin association, late harvest, partial raisining or aroma-concentration mechanism.
notes: Hungarian Wikipedia contributes no card-level consensus.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — Црна тамјаника Неготин презрело грожђе
summary: The Serbian corpus gives only broad Tamjanika context and no standalone sourced treatment of Rosenmuskateller identity, harvest frequency, polusuvarak or on-vine dehydration effects.
notes: Local technical and producer sources carry more detail but are evaluated separately.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Црна тамьяника Неготин поздний сбор
summary: No Russian Wikipedia material was found for the cultivar's exact identity, Negotin practice, partial raisining or dehydration-driven aroma claim.
notes: Russian Wikipedia contributes no card-level evidence.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Crna Tamjanika Muškat Ruža Negotin
summary: No Croatian article was found that ties the Serbian name and Negotin practices to Muškat Ruža/Rosenmuskateller or defines the claimed dehydration stage and effect.
notes: The Croatian genetically identical name is documented by specialist databases, not this Wikipedia search.

title: VIVC passport 8057 — Tamjanika Crna
provenance: Vitis International Variety Catalogue, Julius Kühn-Institut
summary: Canonical identity record for Tamjanika Crna, red berry colour and Balkan origin; linked synonym traditions associate it with Rosenmuskateller/Moscato Rosa.
notes: Automated direct retrieval may be refused; used only for identity, not sensory or harvest-practice claims.

title: wein.plus public glossary — Tamjanika Crna / Rosenmuskateller
provenance: User-requested specialist wine lexicon; unobscured public text
summary: States that Tamjanika Crna and Krajinska Tamjanika Crna are synonyms of Rosenmuskateller and lists Moscato Rosa and Croatian Muškat Ruža Porečki in the same identity complex; origin is Balkan, possibly Dalmatian.
notes: No Premium or blurred text was used; the entry does not establish Negotin late-harvest frequency.

title: Frontiers in Plant Science — genetic characterization of old Serbian grapevines
summary: Treats Tamjanika Crna as old Balkan germplasm and documents Serbian/Srem historical references from 1816 and 1873, supporting long regional continuity but not exclusive Serbian origin or Negotin-only distribution.
notes: Genetic identity cannot by itself date the origin of cultivation.

title: Slow Food Ark of Taste — Black Tamjanika Wine
summary: Documents rare traditional Black Tamjanika wine in Negotinska Krajina and its pronounced aromatic character, supporting regional preservation significance.
notes: Heritage narrative is not a production-frequency survey or grape-dehydration experiment.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Winery Raj d.o.o Rajac
summary: Lists Crna Tamjanika among the current wines of a Rajac/Negotin Valley producer, independently confirming continuing regional production.
notes: The page contains an internally inconsistent reference to Ub in its prose, so only the explicit address/region and product listing are used.

title: Vinoteka Beograd — Matalj Crna Tamjanika 2017
provenance: Dated retail technical page reproducing wine production details
summary: Describes one Matalj Crna Tamjanika as late-harvest wine from overripe grapes and says the berries dehydrate rapidly on the vine, concentrating the must; it supplies residual sugar, acidity and vineyard information for that vintage.
notes: Commercial secondary source and one wine/vintage; it does not use the exact term polusuvarak or establish that the practice is frequent across the cultivar.

title: Matalj Vinarija — Crna Tamjanika
summary: Documents a sweet, fresh, structured and strongly flavoured 100% Crna Tamjanika from Negotin; together with the dated technical archive it confirms a concentrated sweet interpretation but not a universal harvest rule.
notes: Current page lacks the full older production narrative, so specific dehydration wording is not attributed to it.

title: OENO One — sequential harvests based on berry sugar accumulation
provenance: Peer-reviewed grape ripening and wine sensory study
summary: Shows that late-season berry dehydration can raise juice sugar concentration without increasing sugar amount per berry and that later-harvest wine aroma development is not explained directly by sugar concentration alone.
notes: Study cultivars are Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon, not Crna Tamjanika; the physiology is transferable but cultivar response may differ.

title: Horticulturae — volatile profiles during on-vine grape dehydration
summary: Finds that water-loss concentration, biosynthesis and degradation all occur during on-vine dehydration, significantly modifying multiple free and bound aroma compounds rather than merely increasing every aroma uniformly.
notes: Vidal dessert-wine grapes are an analogue, not a Crna Tamjanika trial.

title: English Wikipedia search — Bagrina / Braghina Rosie / Crvena Dinka
summary: No standalone English article or comparable source was found for Bagrina identity, reddish berries, Matalj descriptors, the 2023 microvinification programme or sample-level sensory variation.
notes: Search results can confuse Bagrina with Portuguese red Baga through overlapping synonym strings; they are not the same cultivar.

title: German Wikipedia search — Bagrina Braghina Rosie Crvena Dinka
summary: No German Bagrina profile was found; the article Baga describes an unrelated Portuguese red cultivar and must not be used for this Serbian/Romanian white variety.
notes: A misleading Bagrina Crvena synonym appears under Baga; specialist genetics and CEVVIN take priority for identity.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Bagrina Vörös Dinka Törökdinka
summary: No Hungarian article was found linking local Dinka names to Bagrina or covering its Serbian sensory and research profile.
notes: The Hungarian-language corpus contributes no card-level verification.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — Багрина црвена динка Неготин
summary: No standalone Serbian Wikipedia article was found with the cultivar identity, sensory descriptors or 2023 research details.
notes: CEVVIN is the strongest Serbian source but is not Wikipedia.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Багрина црвена динка Неготин
summary: No Russian Bagrina article or comparable material was found for synonymy, berry colour, descriptors, microvinification results or variability.
notes: Russian Wikipedia contributes no card-level evidence.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Bagrina Crvena Dinka Braghina
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia profile was found that resolves Bagrina identity or supplies the Serbian product and research details in the card.
notes: Specialist sources list Croatian synonym usage, but Wikipedia does not provide a comparable article.

title: CEVVIN — Bagrina cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar and register profile
summary: Lists Bagrina crvena/Bagrina rošie among synonyms, describes an old Balkan cultivar grown in Serbia, Romania and Bulgaria, states that the berries are reddish and that the largest Serbian commercial area is in Negotinska Krajina.
notes: It does not say Bagrina is darker than all other white cultivars or provide the card's sensory profile.

title: wein.plus public glossary — Bagrina
provenance: User-requested specialist lexicon; unobscured public entry
summary: Defines Bagrina as a white cultivar of the Romania–Serbia/old Yugoslavia–Hungary border and historical Banat and lists Crvena Dinka/Červená Dinka and Braghina forms among roughly 60 synonyms.
notes: No Premium or blurred content was used; the public entry supplies no tasting descriptors.

title: Frontiers in Plant Science — genetic characterization of old Serbian grapevines
summary: Identifies Serbian-collected Bagrina samples as Braghina Rosie and reports fifteen such accessions, supporting the synonym/identity link and the cultivar's place in wider Balkan germplasm.
notes: Genetic identity does not establish the exact origin or a sensory profile.

title: Darko Jakšić, ed. — Sorta vinove loze Bagrina
provenance: CEVVIN, Niš, 2023, 164 pp., ISBN 978-86-912489-3-2; cited sensory section pp. 130–147
summary: The monograph reports 21 2022 microvinifications and sensory work involving CREA-VE Asti; its descriptor set includes apple, peach, flowers and occasional honey, mint and spice, with sample differences in acidity, bitterness and overall expression.
notes: The public catalogue confirms the book; exact sensory details are page-attributed to the print/PDF monograph rather than inferred from marketing copy.

title: Vino.rs — Bagrina kakvu nismo poznavali
provenance: On-site report from the 2023 Bagrina project conclusion and tasting
summary: Reports inspection of 13,110 vines, selection of 21 plants/genotypes, CEVVIN microvinifications and CREA-VE involvement. It records wide aroma and acidity ranges; fruit, floral, citrus and some herbal notes dominated, with honey in the local panel, and only three or four samples showing serious all-round potential.
notes: Journalistic report, not the full data table; particularly useful as public corroboration of method and range.

title: JUG deli — Matalj Bagrina Bukovska 2021
provenance: Retail card reproducing a detailed Matalj tasting note
summary: For the 2021 wine, lists apricot, fresh quince, hay, wildflowers, rosemary, sage and chamomile, moderately full body, juiciness and a mineral/tense palate impression.
notes: Text is producer-derived and bottle-specific, not an independent cultivar consensus; wording is paraphrased.

title: Vinoteka Beograd — Matalj Bagrina Bukovska vintage archive
provenance: Dated retail technical archive reproducing producer data
summary: Selected Matalj vintages list apricot, mango, sage, hay, jasmine and white tea, with full body, creamy texture, firmness and minerality. Vintage pages differ between steel and reported barrique ageing, demonstrating a changing wine rather than one stable profile.
notes: Commercial/producer-derived evidence; no consistent explicit toast note is visible, and current 2024 information gives steel ageing.

title: SerbianWine.rs — current indigenous-grape overview, Bagrina entry
provenance: User-requested Serbian public wine guide, current opened page
summary: The current page correctly calls Bagrina a rare local white variety linked to Negotin whose berries can develop reddish skins; it supplies no tasting profile, Matalj vintage details or 2023 microvinification results.
notes: A stale search-engine snapshot exposed an older materially incorrect red-teinturier text; the audit uses the currently opened page and does not preserve the stale content as the current site position.

title: English Wikipedia search — Začinak, Teinturier, Prokupac and Serbian wine
provenance: Largest Wikipedia edition and linked articles
summary: There is no standalone Začinak article. Serbian wine merely lists Začinak among indigenous red grapes; Teinturier defines coloured flesh/juice and colour-focused blending, while Prokupac assigns Negotinsko Crno and Zachinok-like forms to Prokupac, creating a nomenclatural conflict rather than a Začinak profile.
notes: The English edition is highest-priority among the requested Wikipedias but is not reliable enough here to resolve the local cultivar/wine-name collision without Serbian technical and genetic sources.

title: German Wikipedia search — Začinak, Färbertraube and Prokupac
provenance: German Wikipedia and linked technical/cultivar articles
summary: No standalone Začinak article was found. Färbertraube defines dark-red flesh and pigment-bearing juice and says such grapes generally form under 5% when used for colour, but the Prokupac article also lists Negotinsko Crno and Zachinok forms under Prokupac.
notes: The under-5% statement describes teinturiers in general, not a measured distribution of Začinak blends; it cannot override actual 25–30% Bukovski Cuvée recipes.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Začinak / Negotinsko Crno / festőszőlő
summary: No Hungarian Wikipedia article or comparable entry was found for Začinak identity, local names, geography, technical profile, blend practice or Matalj descriptors.
notes: The Hungarian edition contributes no card-level verification.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — Зачинак / Зачињак / Неготинско црно
summary: No Serbian Wikipedia cultivar or wine article was found covering Začinak, its must colour, synonym problem, blending use or the Matalj wine.
notes: CEVVIN and Serbian peer-reviewed/technical sources are substantially stronger than the empty Serbian Wikipedia result.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Зачинак and generic teinturier material
provenance: Russian Wikipedia search and Alicante Bouschet article
summary: No Začinak article was found. The Alicante Bouschet article supplies only the generic rule that a teinturier has coloured juice and flesh and is used to strengthen red-wine colour; it gives no Začinak geography, names, wine or descriptors.
notes: Useful for Russian terminology, not cultivar verification.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Začinak / Negotinsko crno / bojadiser
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia article was found for Začinak or its technical and sensory profile.
notes: Croatian official variety registers do list Začinak, but that evidence is outside Croatian Wikipedia and is treated separately from this requested-language check.

title: CEVVIN — Začinak cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar and vineyard-register profile
summary: Defines Začinak/Začinjak/Negotinsko crno as an autochthonous cultivar, calls its must partly coloured and therefore bojadiser, gives must and wine analysis ranges, very dark red-black colour, much extract, slight astringency and colour-correction use. Current registered commercial area is only 0.08 ha, concentrated most in Negotinska Krajina and Tri Morave.
notes: Its partly coloured must directly contradicts «light juice»; region data distinguish current commercial concentration from historical Šumadija mentions.

title: wein.plus public glossary — Začinak
provenance: User-requested specialist wine lexicon; unobscured public entry
summary: Lists Krajinsko Crno and Negotinsko Crno among Začinak synonyms, calls the cultivar probably Serbian and very late ripening, and describes strongly coloured spicy red wines used mainly as a teinturier in blends.
notes: No Premium or blurred material was used. Its very broad synonym set conflicts with genetic and Prokupac nomenclature and therefore cannot turn each name into an unambiguous monovarietal-wine label.

title: Bešlić et al. — Genetic characterization and relationships of traditional grape cultivars from Serbia
summary: SSR work treats Prokupac and Začinak as distinct old Serbian varieties, places Začinak mainly in eastern Serbia/Timok and reported no synonym or homonym match for the tested Začinak profile in the consulted databases.
notes: This does not invalidate every later local synonym, but it warns against merging Začinak with Prokupac solely through similar names such as Zachinok or Negotinsko Crno.

title: Matalj Vinarija — Začinak Bukovski 2017
provenance: Official producer technical and tasting page
summary: Documents a 100% Začinak 2017 at 13.0% alcohol and 1.2 g/L sugar. The producer note gives muted purple colour, sour cherry, pomegranate, blueberry and mint; a very fresh concentrated nose; soft moderately full fresh-fruity palate; persistent polished tannins balanced by lively acids; light chocolate and a moderately long fruity finish.
notes: Producer-authored and vintage-specific; it is not independent evidence for a universal cultivar profile and gives no maceration duration.

title: NIN — Serbian wine map: Začinak commentary by Darko Jakšić Petrović
provenance: National news magazine interview with Serbian viticulture expert
summary: Characterizes Začinak/Začinjak as an old Serbian cultivar strongly tied to Negotin, rarely seen alone and traditionally blended there, including with Gamay.
notes: Interview evidence supports practice and geography, not exact blend percentages or product descriptors.

title: Vino & Fino — Narodne istine su uglavnom ispravne
provenance: Serbian specialist wine magazine and producer interview
summary: Defines historical Negotinsko crno as a powerful regional blend of Prokupac, Začinak and Četereška/Kadarka, describes its revival in Bukovski Cuvée 2021, and reports plans for tiny experimental pure-Začinak quantities.
notes: Historical composition is transmitted through modern specialist reporting and producer knowledge rather than a digitized original cellar record.

title: Vino.rs — Konačno pravi Bukovski Cuvée na Grand Tastingu
summary: Reports Bukovski Cuvée 2021 as Prokupac 68%, Začinak 25% and Četereška, explicitly framed as revival of the traditional Negotinsko crno blend.
notes: One vintage cannot establish the population average, but it disproves treating single-digit percentages as a safe recipe for this prominent modern example.

title: SerbianWine.rs — current indigenous-grape overview
provenance: User-requested Serbian public wine guide, current opened page
summary: The current page has entries for Prokupac, Tamjanika, Smederevka, Grašac Beli, Bagrina and Morava but no Začinak section, so it provides no identity, process or descriptor verification for this card.
notes: A stale search-engine snapshot showed different page content; only the currently opened public page is used here. No obscured or Premium content was used.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Pimnica Perić winery listing
summary: Lists Začinjak among the top products of Pimnica Perić at Rajačke pimnice, supporting a current regional label/presence but supplying no varietal composition, vintage, technical data or tasting descriptors.
notes: The winery is already recorded separately as gap G0281; the product name alone is insufficient to infer a 100% Začinak wine.

title: Vinogradar, vinogradar–rasadničar, podrumar — Začinak profile
provenance: Digitized Yugoslav viticulture and cellar manual
summary: Calls Začinak a Krajina cultivar with coloured juice and its wine very dark, somewhat astringent and around 5–7‰ acidity, used in small additions to correct the colour of Prokupac and Skadarka wines.
notes: The manual predates current precise area and product data; its analytical acidity cannot be translated automatically into the sensory word «sour» or a universal exact percentage.

title: Croatian vineyard-register regulation — Začinak / Negotinsko crno
provenance: Official Croatian legal gazette variety table
summary: The official table lists Začinak with Negotinsko crno as a synonym, confirming real regional synonym use while not resolving the conflicting Prokupac and historical-blend uses.
notes: This is Croatian law, not Croatian Wikipedia; it is used only as a separate authoritative nomenclature source.

title: Serbian wine — Kreaca entry
summary: The article lists Kreaca among indigenous Serbian white grapes and explicitly gives Banatski Rizling as another name. It supplies no Temišvarka, Vršac-only origin, phenology, sugar, technical wine profile, 1983 document, current blend recipe or tasting descriptors.
notes: Useful as the largest-edition overview, but CEVVIN, scientific literature and the official product page are stronger for all detailed claims.

title: Liste von Rebsorten/K — Kreaca
provenance: German Wikipedia list derived principally from VIVC
summary: The list identifies Kreaca as Serbian Vitis vinifera for white wine/table use and records Banat Riesling, Banati Rizling and Banatski Rizling among its synonyms. Temišvarka and every technical or current-wine descriptor are absent.
notes: The list is a secondary pointer to VIVC and does not establish sensory facts, trademark status or current product composition.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Kreaca / Bánáti rizling
summary: No Hungarian Wikipedia article or comparable detailed entry was found for Kreaca identity, Temišvarka, technical profile, historical regulation or the Drašković wine.
notes: The absence is notable despite historical Hungarian use of Bánáti rizling; non-Wikipedia specialist registries are used separately.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — Креаца / Банатски ризлинг
summary: No Serbian Wikipedia cultivar or wine article was found that verifies the Kreaca card, its synonyms, technical properties, the 1983 list or the modern Banatski Rizling blend.
notes: The local-language gap is filled by current CEVVIN, Serbian scientific papers and producer/specialist sources.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Креаца / Банатский рислинг
summary: Russian Wikipedia has no relevant Kreaca profile. Its Welschriesling material concerns a different cultivar and cannot be transferred to either Kreaca or the seven-variety Banatski Rizling wine.
notes: A separate Russian ampelographic website is recorded only to expose a ripening-time conflict; it is not Russian Wikipedia.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Kreaca / Banatski rizling
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia article was found for Kreaca, its technical profile, names, current blend or descriptors.
notes: Croatian Vinopedia gives late-ripening regional context outside Wikipedia and is treated as a lower-priority specialist source.

title: CEVVIN — Kreaca cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar/register profile
summary: Defines Kreaca as an autochthonous/regional Balkan white cultivar, describes a soft juicy neutral berry, late ripening, lower sugar accumulation and harmonious drinkable wine in the better-quality mass-wine group. It ranks 31st in commercial plantings and places 67% of the area in South Banat.
notes: The current page provides comparative rather than fixed sugar values and does not list Temišvarka or Banatski Rizling among its displayed synonyms.

title: wein.plus public glossary — Kreaca / Bánáti Rizling
provenance: User-requested specialist wine lexicon; unobscured public entry
summary: Calls Kreaca an old white Balkan cultivar, lists Banat Riesling/Banatski Rizling/Bánáti Riesling and numerous Creată forms, reports proposed Coarnă Alba parentage and warns that it is not Riesling despite those names. Temišvarka is absent.
notes: No blurred or Premium material was used. The companion public synonym page at https://glossary.wein.plus/banati-rizling explicitly points to Kreaca.

title: Vitis International Variety Catalogue — Kreaca passport
provenance: Julius Kühn-Institut VIVC, reflected in linked catalogue lists
summary: The current registry identity is Kreaca and the published synonym set includes Banat Riesling, Banati Rizling and Banatski Rizling; Temišvarka is not present in the accessible catalogue-derived lists.
notes: Direct automated access returned a restriction; identity and synonym forms are cross-checked through the German Wikipedia list and wein.plus. Absence of a folk name is not absolute proof, but multiple specialist corpora agree.

title: Rakonjac et al. — The cluster analysis of clones obtained from autochthonous cultivar Kreaca
summary: Treats Kreaca as an autochthonous Banat cultivar, names Kreazer and Banatski rizling locally, describes colourless soft juicy flesh with neutral taste and reports trials on 28 Gudurica clones. Clone mean sugars ranged 17.6–22.6%, yearly means 18.7–20.8%, showing meaningful variation; the paper also says blending can make a more complete wine.
notes: The paper studies selected clones over 2006–2008, not every planting or present vintage. It does not support Temišvarka.

title: Vinogradar, vinogradar–rasadničar, podrumar — Kreaca profile
provenance: Lazar Avramov et al., Zadružna knjiga, Belgrade, 1964, digitized technical manual
summary: Places Kreaca chiefly in South Banat and in the third ripening epoch, gives 18–20% sugar in must, 10–12% alcohol and 5–6‰ acidity in wine, and calls the wine drinkable, harmonious and characteristically varietal in aroma. It rates the wine better than Plovdina, Ružica and Slankamenka despite placing the section under weaker whites.
notes: Dated Yugoslav-era values use the source's percent/promille conventions and cannot be applied as present legal specifications.

title: Commission Regulation (EEC) No 1224/83 of 6 May 1983
provenance: Official Journal of the European Communities via EUR-Lex
summary: The replaced Yugoslavia chapter prints «BANATSKI RIZLING, KREACA» together and associates the accepted synonym Zackelweiss with the entry.
notes: This is a naming table for wine description/presentation, not a genetic or sensory study.

title: Swisslion-Takovo — Banatski rizling 1L
provenance: Current official group product page for Vinarija Drašković
summary: Identifies the product as dry white wine from Drašković vineyards, lists Italian Riesling, Rhine Riesling, Župljanka, Kreaca, Smederevka, Rkatsiteli and Chasselas, and gives 11.5% alcohol.
notes: The page uses Banatski Rizling as the product name but does not prove legal trademark registration and contains no tasting note or blend percentages.

title: Vino.rs — Legendarna vina: Banatski rizling
provenance: Dated specialist report and direct tasting with Drašković chief oenologist, 2020
summary: Documents the enduring commercial label, seven-variety blend and minimum-50% Grašac historical recipe statement. Its tasted modern wine had pleasant fruit and unexpected tropical aroma, slight butteriness, solid body, well-balanced acidity, some crispness and a deliberately not-long finish.
notes: The sensory profile and 12% figure belong to the tasted release in 2020; they must not override the current official 11.5% page or become universal cultivar descriptors.

title: Vino & Fino — Renesansa na Vršačkom bregu
provenance: Independent Serbian wine magazine visit and tasting
summary: Calls Banatski Rizling a formerly mass everyday white-wine brand now revived as a clean, fresh and precise seven-variety blend, with citrus and yellow-fruit character, lively presentation, decent length and structure.
notes: The note is dated and bottle-specific; it supports broad consensus on fruit, citrus and freshness, not every aroma in other retail notes.

title: RTV — Sinonim za grožđe Kreaca je banatski rizling
provenance: Radio Television of Vojvodina report with local growers and winery executive
summary: Reports Banatski rizling as a Kreaca synonym and as the name source of the wine brand, links the cultivar to Gudurica/Vršac and describes its white wines as harmonious, drinkable and without a strong aroma.
notes: Interview statements are valuable local evidence but do not prove legal trademark registration; «without strong aroma» is compatible with a subtle characteristic varietal aroma.

title: SerbianWine.rs — public catalogue search for Kreaca / Banatski Rizling
provenance: User-requested Serbian wine and tourism directory
