provenance: Serbian viticulture-centre cultivar monograph and 2019 inventory
summary: Profiles Kreaca as a South Banat-associated traditional cultivar with comparatively low sugar accumulation and a late-ripening classification; approximately two thirds of the recorded 31.69 ha were in South Banat.
notes: Its late-ripening classification conflicts with another secondary ampelographic account and does not establish a late harvest for every Vršac grape.

title: Vinski vodič — Vršački vinogradi
provenance: Serbian directory preserving historical large-estate assortment data
summary: Lists Italian Riesling as more than half of the former estate assortment and includes Kreaca among Vršac white cultivars.
notes: The denominator is the old Vršački vinogradi company, not all current vineyards of Vršac or South Banat.

title: Power of Terroir: Case study of Grašac at the Fruška Gora wine region
provenance: Open Geosciences peer-reviewed comparison of two sites, three chemical vintages and seven sensory vintages
summary: Finds lighter, more primary-fruited young Grašac at Sremski Karlovci and fuller, more complex development with age at Neštin, demonstrating substantial variation within Fruška Gora itself.
notes: The study contains no Vršac comparator, so it cannot establish that Fruška Gora is generally riper or fuller than Vršac.

title: Grape must quality and mesoclimatic variability in Fruška Gora wine-growing region
provenance: University of Novi Sad vineyard study, Terclim 2022 proceedings
summary: Reports directional and cultivar variation in harvest timing and must chemistry across Fruška Gora and finds Grašac the most chemically stable of the monitored cultivars, without comparing it to Vršac wines.
notes: Must composition and harvest day do not directly establish finished-wine body.

title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources, fourth edition
summary: Defines the high-clay shrink–swell behaviour of Vertisols relevant to smonica terminology, while not predicting a regional harvest date or wine style from the soil name alone.
notes: Actual thermal and water behaviour depends on profile moisture, drainage, structure, cover and management.

title: Long-term trends of the Koshava wind during the period 1949–2010
provenance: International Journal of Climatology study using five synoptic stations
summary: Characterises Košava frequency and speed as a strong southeast-sector wind but does not study grape ripening, berry acids or wine acidity.
notes: The presence of a wind regime cannot alone establish beneficial acid retention.

title: Soil-related terroir factors: a review
summary: Explains that ripening and wine outcomes arise from interacting soil, water, temperature, cultivar and management factors rather than a single soil label or isolated climate feature.
notes: It is general evidence and does not replace local Vršac measurements.

title: English Wikipedia — Tamjanika, Muscat Ottonel, Gewürztraminer and Aleksandrovac search
provenance: Requested English Wikipedia cultivar, region, aroma-chemistry and night-temperature search
summary: Identifies Tamjanika as an aromatic Muscat-related grape and provides generic context for the two alternatives, but does not prove Župa planting leadership, local cool nights or preservation of volatiles during ripening and processing.
notes: The article cannot establish the book's causal explanation or make aroma independent of site.

title: German Wikipedia — Gewürztraminer, Muskat-Ottonel and Aleksandrovac search
provenance: Requested German Wikipedia cultivar, Serbian-region and aroma-preservation search
summary: Strongly supports Gewürztraminer's aromatic identity and generic Muscat Ottonel context, but contains no evidence for current Serbian regional availability or the Župa night-temperature mechanism.
notes: It also shows that ripeness and acidity affect expression, contrary to an absolute place-independent formula.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Tramini and Muscat search; no Župa climate material
provenance: Requested Hungarian Wikipedia cultivar, region and temperature-effect search
summary: Provides general aromatic Traminer context but no detailed Tamjanika/Župa distribution, Vršac product evidence or night-temperature data.
notes: The absence of local material is recorded, not treated as counterevidence.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Александровац and Tamjanika search
provenance: Requested Serbian Wikipedia place, cultivar, aroma and climate search
summary: Places Aleksandrovac in a basin between mountain spurs but has no sufficiently sourced Tamjanika profile, planting statistics, vineyard night series or volatile-compound mechanism.
notes: A basin description does not establish its nocturnal thermal regime.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Гевюрцтраминер, Мускат and Aleksandrovac search
provenance: Requested Russian Wikipedia cultivar, place and aroma-temperature search
summary: Describes Gewürztraminer as highly aromatic and clarifies Traminer naming, but offers no direct evidence for the Serbian alternatives, Župa planting rank or local volatile retention.
notes: No cross-language encyclopedia supplies the missing local measurements.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Traminac and Serbian Tamjanika/Župa search
provenance: Requested Croatian Wikipedia cultivar, region and aroma-preservation search
summary: Supports Traminac as a very aromatic wine-grape type but does not establish Fruška Gora availability, Vršac Muscat Ottonel, Župa cool nights or processing effects.
notes: Regional product and scientific records are required for the Serbian claims.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Tamjanika: Aromatic White Wine and Where to Taste It
provenance: Dated 4 August 2026 Serbian national wine guide
summary: Calls Tamjanika Serbia's intensely aromatic Muscat Blanc expression, closely associates it with Župa/Aleksandrovac and lists jasmine, elderflower, orange blossom, citrus, grape, peach and herbs.
notes: The guide explicitly says vineyard setting contributes to Serbian expression and therefore does not support aroma being independent of place.

title: Union of Winemakers and Winegrowers of Serbia — I'm picking grapes, I'm choosing Tamjanika
provenance: Serbian national wine-association technical and market overview
summary: States that Tamjanika's revival began in Župa, reports the greatest plantings there and 69.59 ha in Tri Morave, identifies it as an aromatic Muscat and gives a 22–24% sugar and 5–7 g/L acid profile with floral, fruit, citrus and spice notes.
notes: The association also says final authenticity comes from both variety and terroir, contradicting «independent of place».

title: Bikicki — Moma Traminac crveni 2024
provenance: Current Fruška Gora winery technical and sensory sheet
summary: Documents a 2024 Traminac crveni white wine from Banoštor, Fruška Gora, with strong floral, pineapple, honey and rose-water aromas and exact analytical and production details.
notes: The page names Traminac crveni; it should not be silently converted to a different Traminer form without registry evidence.

title: Drašković winery — Vršac varieties
summary: Lists Muscat Ottonel among the white grapes/wines of current Vršac production and confirms the area's white-wine emphasis.
notes: The page establishes availability, not a representative sensory score for every Muscat Ottonel bottle.

title: Terpenoids and their role in wine flavour: recent advances
provenance: Australian Journal of Grape and Wine Research open-access review by Australian Wine Research Institute authors
summary: Explains that grape monoterpenes and other terpenoids may occur in free volatile or sugar-bound forms and that only a subset makes an important contribution to wine aroma.
notes: It supports an intrinsic grape contribution but not independence from climate, site, maturity or processing.

title: Riesling aroma composition in light of changing global temperatures — effects of warmer nights
provenance: Charles Sturt University/National Wine and Grape Industry Centre field study, GiESCO proceedings
summary: Across four monitored sites, warmer ripening nights were associated at harvest with lower concentrations of specific terpenes including linalool and alpha-terpineol.
notes: The experiment concerns Riesling in Australia, not Tamjanika in Župa, so it supports mechanism plausibility only and cannot prove the local claim.

title: Pre-processing Cooling of Harvested Grapes Induces Changes in Berry Composition and Metabolism
provenance: Frontiers in Nutrition controlled Vermentino pre-cooling study
summary: Shows that cooling harvested grapes at 4 or 10°C before processing altered berry and wine volatile profiles, with treatment-specific increases in sesquiterpenes and other compositional effects.
notes: Active pre-cooling after harvest is technologically distinct from naturally cool vineyard nights, and effects cannot be assumed for Tamjanika without testing.

title: Vinarija Mozaik — Podneblje Župe
provenance: Župa producer's regional geography and climate page
summary: Describes Župa as a basin between Kopaonik, Željin, Goč and Jastrebac and provides qualitative regional climate context.
notes: It provides no vineyard night-temperature series and cannot establish the thermal premise of the book's volatile-retention explanation.

title: English Wikipedia — Kadarka, Subotica Sands and Prokupac search
provenance: Requested English Wikipedia regional, cultivar, soil, structure and ageing search
summary: Confirms Kadarka identity and Central European/Balkan distribution but describes medium-dark or dark, full and deeply aromatic wine; it gives no Serbian Subotica recommendation, sandy-soil mechanism, Župa bottle guidance or fixed ageing window.
notes: Its sensory paragraph is weakly sourced and should not override current Serbian primary records or controlled enology.

title: German Wikipedia — Kadarka and Prokupac search
provenance: Requested German Wikipedia cultivar, colour, soil and ageing search
summary: Directly describes very thin-skinned Kadarka berries but says successful varietal wines can be dark, tannic, extract-rich and age well; it does not isolate skin thickness as the cause of colour or support a universal two-to-three-year rule.
notes: No specific evidence is supplied for Subotica-Horgoš, Župa Prokupac or the causal effect of sand.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Kadarka and sandy-site style search
provenance: Requested Hungarian Wikipedia cultivar, sand, structure and ageing search
summary: Contrasts thinner, fresher Kadarka on loose sand with fuller wine on bound and loess soils and notes low colour under some harvest conditions, but gives no Serbian matched-site experiment and does not prove the book's water-and-nutrient mechanism.
notes: The traditional contrast is relevant evidence but conflicts with diverse wines from the same Subotica sandy vineyards and cannot establish determinism.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Kadarka, Prokupac, Subotica and Župa search
provenance: Requested Serbian Wikipedia local-region, cultivar, style and ageing search
summary: Presents Kadarka as an elegant, light, harmonious, cherry-led wine with moderate acidity and separately places Prokupac strongly in Župa; it does not substantiate the sandy-soil causal chain, conspicuous tannin or an exact ageing window.
notes: The Prokupac material is broader than the linked Kadarka page and was checked as part of the same language search.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Кадарка and Прокупац search
provenance: Requested Russian Wikipedia cultivar, region, soil and ageing search
summary: Confirms thin-skinned Kadarka berries and Serbian cultivation but gives almost no sensory, soil, tannin or ageing analysis and no practical Subotica or Župa recommendation.
notes: Its sparse sourcing cannot prove that thinness causes pale wine or that sand makes the style light.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Kadarka and north Bačka search
provenance: Requested Croatian Wikipedia cultivar, Subotica, structure and ageing search
summary: Credits Tonković with reviving Kadarka in northern Bačka and describes ruby, medium-bodied, soft and fresh wine without overpowering tannin; it does not demonstrate the soil mechanism and only says ageing potential is limited in general terms.
notes: The page supports current regional association more strongly than the claim that tannin is routinely conspicuous.

title: CEVVIN — Skadarka
provenance: Serbian Center for Viticulture and Winemaking national variety profile
summary: Identifies Subotica among the largest present Serbian areas, says Skadarka was formerly the leading local indigenous variety there, reports compact bunches, drought resistance and aromatic wine from both sand and bound soil.
notes: The profile does not describe berry skin thickness, exact tannin intensity or a two-to-three-year drinking window.

title: Vinarija Tonković — Fantasy Kadarka
provenance: Current Subotica-Horgoš producer technical and sensory page
summary: Documents Kadarka from Bački Vinogradi on the Subotica-Horgoš sands as ruby, elegant, soft, fresh and medium-bodied with balanced tannins, 13.53% alcohol, pH 3.53 and 5.21 g/L total acidity; the producer claims at least ten years of bottle life.
notes: Producer ageing language is bottle-specific and promotional; it contradicts a universal two-to-three-year window rather than setting a new universal rule.

title: Vinarija Tonković — Rhapsody Kadarka
provenance: Current technical page for a second Kadarka from the same Subotica-Horgoš vineyard base
summary: Describes Kadarka from Bački Vinogradi as fuller-bodied and denser after ageing in new 300-litre oak, with 13.51% alcohol, pH 3.53 and 5.11 g/L total acidity.
notes: It shows that a sandy regional label does not force a light wine; fruit selection and élevage differ from the base Fantasy.

title: Maurer — Vineyards in the Subotica wine region
provenance: Current winery page documenting historic Kadarka parcels and local soil profiles
summary: Records two old Kadarka vineyards near Subotica and specifies that surface sand extends to about half a metre above clayey calcareous loess, demonstrating a layered rather than uniformly deep sandy profile.
notes: One producer's parcels do not define every site in the regional designation.

title: Ivanović Winery — current wine catalogue
provenance: Current Aleksandrovac winery storefront and portfolio
summary: Lists a standard red Prokupac at 1,440 RSD alongside more expensive and differently styled wines, providing a concrete current Župa-direction bottle rather than an undefined category alone.
notes: Price and availability are time-sensitive, and «standard» does not itself establish a Kadarka-like light sensory profile.

title: Ivanović Winery — About us
provenance: Current Aleksandrovac producer vineyard and vinification profile
summary: Places the winery in Aleksandrovac, locates its own and contracted vineyards across Župa and identifies Prokupac as one of the two foundations of production; red wines are traditionally vinified and then aged twelve months in 500-litre oak.
notes: The cellar's standard Prokupac is not necessarily a no-oak, very light entry wine; the label and vintage still require checking.

title: CEVVIN — Prokupac
provenance: Serbian Center for Viticulture and Winemaking national variety profile
summary: Places the greatest Prokupac area in the Three Moravas region and describes drinkable refreshing red or ruby wine, while warning that longer pomace contact makes it astringent and stating that ageing can improve quality.
notes: The region-level profile supports Župa direction but also shows why «basic» and lightness must be defined by vinification and bottle.

title: FAO Soils Portal — Management of Sandy Soils
provenance: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization soil-management reference
summary: Defines generally sandy profiles as coarse-textured to 50 cm and states that they retain few nutrients and have low water-holding capacity.
notes: This establishes the physical premise only; it does not predict Kadarka body, colour, acidity or tannin at Subotica.

title: Influence of non-irrigation and seasonality on wine colour, phenolic composition and sensory quality of Callet
provenance: OENO One field study and literature synthesis on vine water deficit
summary: Reports that water deficit can reduce berry weight, increase skin-to-pulp ratio and raise concentrations of anthocyanins and other phenolics, while cultivar, timing and season modify the response.
notes: The experiment concerns Callet in a Mediterranean climate, not Kadarka in Subotica, so it demonstrates non-determinism rather than the local outcome.

title: Magyar Bor — Kadarka
provenance: Official Hungarian Wine communication portal, freshly checked cultivar profile
summary: Attributes Kadarka's pale colour to low anthocyanins and describes light-to-medium body, bright acidity and restrained or low tannins; it recommends the latest vintages within one or two years for the fresh light style because the wine oxidises relatively quickly.
notes: The recommendation is style-specific and cannot exclude longer-lived selected or oak-aged bottles.

title: Fermentation temperature and duration effect on the quality and anthocyanin content of Kadarka wine produced in the Miniș wine region
summary: Shows that Kadarka wine anthocyanin content and colour respond to fermentation temperature and maceration duration, with different tested regimes producing different extraction outcomes.
notes: It does not measure skin thickness as an isolated cause and concerns a Romanian region rather than Subotica.

title: English Wikipedia — Negotin
provenance: Required English Wikipedia geographic, climate and wine-context check
summary: Places Negotin in eastern Serbia and provides current climate normals, including hot July and August means, but does not establish a canonical three-grape blend, a regional style comparison, vineyard drainage or a flatland Vertisol wine style.
notes: The climate table is useful context; specialist regulation, OIV and current wine records carry the detailed findings.

title: German Wikipedia — Negotin
provenance: Required German Wikipedia geographic and wine-context check
summary: Provides broad geographic and historical orientation for Negotin without the bottle-specific composition, comparative Vranac style or soil-drainage evidence needed for this block.
notes: Not used as evidence for a sensory or causal rule.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Negotin targeted check
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia targeted geographic and wine search
summary: No sufficiently specific material was available for the recommended wines, the proposed comparative style or the slope, drainage and Vertisol causal chain.
notes: Absence of detail is recorded as a search result, not counter-evidence.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Неготин
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local geographic, climate and wine-context check
summary: Supplies local geographic and general climate context but no representative sample proving that all dense reds follow the proposed varietal, alcohol, slope or flatland pattern.
notes: The state regional specification has priority for legal geography, soils and topography.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Неготин
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia geographic and wine-context check
summary: Provides only basic orientation and does not verify the named wines, blend interpretation, Vranac comparison or terroir-to-style mechanism.
notes: Not counted as an independent specialist source.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Negotin
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia geographic and wine-context check
summary: Offers minimal geographic context and no adequate evidence for the recommended blend reading, regional weight comparison, measured drainage or a flatland smonica style.
notes: Specialist and primary sources are required for the substantive conclusions.

title: Pravilnik o rejonizaciji — Negotinska Krajina and Knjaževac
provenance: Serbian wine-region regulation consolidated with amendments through Službeni glasnik RS 18/2024
summary: Separates Negotinska Krajina from the Knjaževac region and Potrkanje subarea; for Negotin it records 1961–2010 bioclimatic data, principal vineyard soils including Vertisol, eutric Cambisol and sand, elevations mainly 100–270 m, generally moderate-to-gentle vineyard slopes and mainly southern, southeastern and eastern exposures.
notes: The text does not overlay Vertisol exclusively with flat terrain, measure drainage by site or prescribe a resulting wine style.

title: Municipality of Negotin — Location, climate and population
provenance: Official municipal geographic and climate profile
summary: Describes the local continental climate, pronounced seasonal variation and hot summers, corroborating the broad ripening background used in the guide.
notes: Municipal prose does not describe every vineyard mesoclimate or quantify grape sugar.

title: OURS — Matalj Kremen Kamen 2021
provenance: Current Serbian specialist retail technical and stock card
summary: Lists a currently stocked Negotin 2021 dry red made from Cabernet Sauvignon, aged in oak, at 14% ABV and describes it as intense, layered, full and firmly structured.
notes: A retailer's sensory description supports one concrete recommendation, not a universal regional style.

title: Vinoteka Beograd — Matalj Bukovski Cuvée 2021
provenance: Current Serbian retailer product record retained for the named vintage and composition
summary: Identifies Bukovski Cuvée 2021 as a Negotinska Krajina blend of 68% Prokupac, 25% Začinak and 7% Četereška, directly showing that the local Začinak route is not the proposed Cabernet-Vranac-Začinak trio.
notes: The retailer catalogue is transitioning to a newer vintage, so the percentages here are explicitly tied to the displayed 2021 record.

title: Decanter — Matalj Bukovski Cuvée, Negotin 2021
summary: Records a dry oaked 2021 Negotin red at 12.5% ABV and medium body, with Prokupac, Začinak and Kadarka; it supplies an immediate counterexample to treating ripe Negotin red as necessarily high-alcohol or heavy.
notes: Its submitted percentages differ slightly from current retailer data, but both sources agree on the three varieties and the 12.5% wine identity.

title: Vino.rs — Bukovski Cuvée: Decanterovo zlato rođeno u vinogradu
provenance: Dated report from the winery's July 2025 presentation of Bukovski Cuvée 2021
summary: Attributes fruit to Prokupac, freshness and structure to Začinak and spice to Kadarka in the actual local blend, supporting functional use of Začinak without a Cabernet or Vranac requirement.
notes: Producer comments reported by specialist media are bottle-specific, not a general blend law.

title: OURS — Jović Vranac Potrkanjski 2022
provenance: Current Serbian specialist retail technical, stock and sensory card
summary: Lists the 2022 varietal Vranac from Jović in Potrkanje at 15% ABV, aged in oak and full on the palate, contradicting a safe promise of lesser weight outside Negotinska Krajina.
notes: The card's Tri Morave region field conflicts with official zoning and its own Potrkanje/Knjaževac producer location, so it is not used for regional classification.

title: Svet vina — Prvi dobitnici nagrade Ljubičasta plaketa
provenance: Serbian wine-origin labelling report listing initial geographic-designation recipients
summary: Places Jović and Vranac Potrkanjski under Knjaževački rejon with the Knjaževac/Potrkanje designation, independently resolving retailer region-field errors.
notes: The source establishes origin, not a sensory comparison with Negotinska Krajina.

title: OURS — Todorović Opus Vranac 2019
provenance: Current Serbian specialist retail technical and stock card
summary: Lists a currently stocked 2019 varietal Vranac from Potrkanje in the Knjaževac region at 14% ABV, oak-aged and full in character.
notes: One retailer profile cannot establish a regional mean, but a second full-bodied example weakens the lighter-style promise.

title: OURS — Aleksić Amanet Vranac 2019
provenance: Current Serbian specialist retail technical and stock card
summary: Lists a Vranje-region 2019 varietal Vranac at 14.5% ABV and describes it as powerful, full and juicy, showing that a genuinely southeastern example is not reliably light either.
notes: This is a single Vranje bottle and cannot substitute for a comparative regional sample.

title: OIV — Evaluation by refractometry of sugar concentration and potential alcoholic strength
provenance: OIV official analytical resolution OIV-OENO 466-2012, currently in force
summary: Defines the linear conversion between must sugar concentration and potential alcoholic strength and labels the calculated value as potential rather than guaranteed final wine ABV.
notes: The method does not make heat the sole cause of sugar or predict fermentation outcome and final style.

title: FAO Soils Portal — Management of heavy cracking clays
provenance: FAO technical overview of Vertisols and other heavy cracking clays
summary: Explains that heavy cracking clays often have poor internal drainage and very slow hydraulic conductivity when wet, while dry cracks can rapidly admit water; drainage behaviour is therefore profile- and moisture-dependent.
notes: The global soil-management page does not map Negotin's Vertisol, terrain position or wine style.

title: English Wikipedia — Prokupac
provenance: Required English Wikipedia cultivar, region, style, agronomy and label-context check
summary: Identifies Prokupac as Serbian, links major plantings to Three Moravas and Šumadija and describes freshness and dark fruit; it notes abundant harvests even on skeletal soil but does not establish medium body as universal, mandatory crop thinning, empty wine without canopy work or Serbian GI market shares.
notes: Its skeletal-soil statement comes from an older regional monograph and is not a comparative vigour trial.

title: German Wikipedia — Prokupac
provenance: Required German Wikipedia cultivar, style and agronomy check
summary: Describes medium-to-strong shoot growth, high yields and spicy fruit aromas, but also generally alcohol-rich wine and no compulsory thinning, canopy recipe, label-law analysis or GI production share.
notes: Broad cultivar prose cannot identify the origin of a particular bottle.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Prokupac, Župa and Oplenac
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia targeted cultivar, region and origin-label search
summary: No dedicated Prokupac article or sufficiently specific evidence was found for the regional recommendation, management chain, label interpretation or GI statistics.
notes: The negative search result is not evidence against the claims.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Прокупац
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local cultivar and agronomy check
summary: Calls Prokupac very vigorous and highly productive, recommends short pruning and permeable, loose, stony-gravelly, moderately fertile warm soils and describes broad wine character. It does not prove that omitted thinning and canopy work create empty wine or that town names alone establish origin.
notes: The agronomic text overlaps popular Serbian material, limiting independence.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Прокупац, Жупа and Oplenac
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia targeted cultivar, region and label search
summary: No dedicated article or sufficiently specific Russian-language evidence was found for the style, vineyard-management mechanism, official label names or current GI share.
notes: General Russian soil or appellation articles cannot establish Serbian local practice.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Prokupac and Župa
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia targeted cultivar, region and label search
summary: No dedicated Prokupac treatment or adequate evidence was found for the block's regional, sensory, agronomic, legal or statistical statements.
notes: Absence is recorded without treating it as contradiction.

title: Pravilnik o rejonizaciji — Župa, Šumadija and Oplenac
provenance: Serbian wine-region regulation consolidated with amendments through Službeni glasnik RS 18/2024
summary: Names Župsko vinogorje/Župa under Tri Morave and Oplenačko vinogorje/Oplenac under Šumadija; Aleksandrovac and Topola occur as municipalities or cadastral localities within the respective boundaries rather than as the listed vinogorje names.
notes: A town name may still appear as a producer address; label function must be checked in context.

title: Vinarija Aleksandrović — Prokupac
provenance: Current official product, vineyard, soil and food-pairing page
summary: Lists a currently sold 100% Prokupac from Oplenac/Šumadija as fruity, spicy and structured with soft tannins; it names clove and cinnamon, several meat and cheese pairings, and a low-humus clay site with sand and stone where low yields are achieved.
notes: Producer attribution supports one wine and site; it cannot prove that stones alone reduce vigour or that all Šumadija Prokupac is medium-bodied.

title: OURS — Ivanović Prokupac 2024
provenance: Current Serbian specialist retail technical and stock card
summary: Lists a stocked 2024 dry red led by Prokupac from Ivanović in Aleksandrovac/Župa, Tri Morave, with fresh ripe-red-fruit aroma and an easy-drinking character.
notes: The card labels the wine as a blend category despite showing only Prokupac in the variety field; exact percentages require a producer technical sheet.

title: CEVVIN — Prokupac
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking national cultivar and register profile
summary: Calls Prokupac very vigorous, supports short pruning, says reduced yields favour suitable must sugar and names loose, permeable, gajnjača, calcareous smonica, gravelly, deluvial, moderately fertile and warm soils; it also places major area in Tri Morave and documents broad red and rosé styles.
notes: The page does not prescribe universal thinning or canopy operations and does not compare shoot growth on stony versus non-stony plots.

title: Prokupac Day — Enjoying Prokupac
provenance: Serbian cultivar-focused educational and gastronomy campaign
summary: Explicitly distinguishes easy-drinking fruit-forward, lush full-bodied, medium-bodied fruit-and-spice, and Bordeaux-blended Prokupac styles and pairs the medium-bodied version with beef ribs in red-wine sauce.
notes: Campaign material is promotional and does not test vineyard-management causality.

title: PSSS agronomist — Kakav je prokupac kao grožđe, a kakav kao vino
provenance: Serbian Agricultural Advisory and Expert Service author published by Dobro Jutro
summary: Describes Prokupac as medium-to-strong in vigour and productive at 15–20 t/ha, recommends short pruning and repeats the preference for permeable, loose, stony-gravelly and moderately fertile soils.
notes: It does not state that thinning and canopy work are always required or that their absence produces an empty wine; its source base overlaps Serbian cultivar summaries.

title: Impact of Cluster Thinning on Wine Grape Yield and Fruit Composition: A Review and Meta-Analysis
provenance: 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis of 78 wine-grape studies
summary: Finds an average yield reduction from cluster thinning but non-universal composition responses that vary with cultivar, rootstock and thinning intensity; only moderate thinning showed consistent effects for some metrics.
notes: The meta-analysis has no Prokupac-specific subgroup and does not assess the undefined descriptor empty.

title: Ministry of Agriculture of Serbia — Deklarisanje vina
provenance: Serbian Ministry of Agriculture wine-labelling guidance
summary: States that Serbian labelling rules are aligned with EU requirements, places responsibility on the producer and prohibits geographic indications on wines without geographical origin.
notes: A place name printed solely as an address must not be silently read as the wine's protected origin.

title: WIPO Lex — Law on Wine of Serbia
provenance: WIPO Lex English reproduction of Serbia's Wine Law and geographical-indication categories
summary: Separates wine without geographical indication from PGI and PDO categories and defines origin requirements, including at least 85% grapes from the named unit for regional wine and exclusive origin for the stricter controlled category.
notes: Protected origin certifies compliance with a specification, not an identical tasting score for every bottle.

title: Euronews Srbija — Vina iz 112 vinarija sa oznakom geografskog porekla
provenance: 4 January 2025 report citing the Serbian Chamber of Commerce and current producer register
summary: Reports 497 registered market wine producers in 2024, of which 112 held geographical-origin designations covering 450 wines.
notes: The counts show GI holders are a minority of producers but do not give the total number of distinct non-GI labels or a 2026 volume share.

title: Blic Biznis — Wine Register production structure in 2021
provenance: 18 January 2023 report reproducing Serbian Wine Register figures
summary: Reports that wine without geographical origin accounted for 87% of Serbian registered wine production in 2021 and wine with GI, KPK or KGPK for 13%.
notes: This is a 2021 production-volume snapshot reproduced by media, not a live 2026 statistic or count of labels.

title: English Wikipedia — Bermet
provenance: Required English Wikipedia geography, style, composition, alcohol and recipe check
summary: Presents Bermet as a Fruška Gora dessert-wine speciality in red or white forms, usually 16–18% alcohol, made with about 20 herbs and spices, with exact recipes held by some Sremski Karlovci families.
notes: It supports the Serbian centre and broad profile but does not prove more than 20 components, universal wormwood bitterness, an exclusive Karlovci origin or the international production claim.

title: German Wikipedia — Bermet
provenance: Required German Wikipedia cross-border geography, composition and recipe-variation check
summary: Describes a long Bermet tradition in Serbia and Croatia, current family production in Sremski Karlovci, Fruška Gora monasteries and Samobor, non-standardised producer-specific recipes, up to 20 herbs, spices and fruits including wormwood, 16–18% alcohol and a lightly bitter base.
notes: Its suggestion of a monastic origin is explicitly uncertain, and its up-to-20 count conflicts with a universal more-than-20 formula.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Bermet bor
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia targeted Bermet search
summary: No dedicated Hungarian Bermet article or sufficiently specific evidence was found for the block's geography, style, recipe, ingredient count or historical claim.
notes: The negative search result is recorded without treating absence as contradiction.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Бермет
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language style, geography and recipe check
summary: Calls Bermet a traditional Karlovci sweet aromatised wine, usually 16–18% alcohol, made from red or white Fruška Gora grapes with medicinal plants; it places production across the Srem wine area and describes recipes as varying by house, with wormwood among characteristic botanicals.
notes: It does not provide a representative commercial ingredient census, prove perceptible wormwood bitterness in every wine or establish Karlovci as the sole place of origin.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Бермет вино
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia targeted Bermet search
summary: No dedicated Russian Bermet article or sufficiently specific treatment of the recommendation was found.
notes: Unrelated name and place results cannot support or contradict the wine claims.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Bermet
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia cross-border Bermet tradition check
summary: Treats Bermet broadly as an aromatised wine or wine-based drink with wormwood and other botanicals, documents production in Srijem and north-western Croatia and gives a Croatian alcohol figure around 15–16% with aperitif and digestif uses.
notes: The page centres Croatian forms and therefore counters exclusive Karlovci wording but cannot define the usual strength or ingredient count of Serbian commercial Bermet.

title: Gorjanović et al. — Serbian aromatized wine “Bermet”: antioxidant activity
provenance: Journal of the Serbian Chemical Society 85(4), 517–529 (2020), DOI 10.2298/JSC190404139G
summary: Defines Fruška Gora Bermet as red or white aromatised wine, describes production since the fifteenth century, analyses ten commercial Bermets from several localities and records producer-dependent recipes and extraction, usual 16–18% alcohol and an experimental 46-herb formulation containing wormwood.
notes: The experimental 46-herb mixture is not a census of commercial recipes, and the undisclosed commercial formulas cannot establish universal wormwood bitterness or a uniform ingredient count.

title: Vinarija Vinum — Bermet crveni
provenance: Current official product page of Vinarija Vinum, Sremski Karlovci
summary: Lists a current sweet red aromatised Frankovka-based Bermet and describes a combination of 22 kinds of fruit and spices with dried-plum, fig, orange-peel, dried-grape, cinnamon and clove aromas.
notes: The six named items are presented as aromas, not a complete ingredient declaration, and one producer's 22-part description cannot define every Bermet.

title: Vinarija Veritas Ćuković — Bermet
provenance: Current official Veritas Ćuković product page
summary: Calls its red Bermet a sweet aromatised wine enriched with more than 20 medicinal herbs and spices and describes dried-fruit, cinnamon, clove, anise, vanilla and dark-chocolate aromas.
notes: The page supports more than 20 for this label, not a universal Bermet rule, and its dried-fruit wording is a sensory description rather than a full recipe.

title: Tourist Organisation of Sremski Karlovci — Bermet
provenance: Official municipal tourism organisation's food-and-wine profile
summary: Presents Bermet as one of the primary associations of Sremski Karlovci and as a traditional aromatic dessert wine produced in the area for centuries.
notes: Local promotion establishes Karlovci's centrality and continuity but not sole invention or exclusive survival there.

title: European Commission — Aromatised wine
provenance: European Commission Directorate-General for Agriculture and Rural Development

notes: The page directly supports production traditions in multiple countries; it does not address the Serbian legal status of Bermet.

title: City of Samobor tourism — Gastronomy: Samoborski bermet
provenance: Official City of Samobor tourism portal
summary: Describes Bermet as a centuries-old Samobor tradition made from red wine, fruit and herbs; it says each producing family has a specific method and that examples vary in bitterness and sweetness.
notes: This is evidence for a distinct Croatian tradition and recipe variation, not a definition of Serbian Bermet's usual alcohol or ingredient count.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on recognition of designations for still wines
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 121/2012, 102/2014, 78/2015, 94/2017, 48/2022 and 18/2024
summary: Provides the current designation procedure and states that one controlled geographical designation simultaneously receives K.P.K. and K.G.P.K., while the category used for a given production year depends on the sensory score in control; its final provisions replaced the relevant 1980 Serbian republican wine-and-rakia origin rules.
notes: The site reproduces the consolidated Gazette text but is not itself the official Gazette; statutory claims are cross-checked against the Wine Law and sensory rulebook.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024
summary: Requires Serbian domestic quality terms G.I., K.P.K. or K.G.P.K. and explicitly permits the additional English expressions protected geographical indication / PGI and protected designation of origin / PDO beside the corresponding Serbian term.

title: EUR-Lex — Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013, current consolidated wine GI definitions
provenance: Current consolidated EU common market organisation regulation, Article 93
summary: Defines wine PDO by exclusive grape origin and production in the named area and wine PGI by at least 85% grape origin and production in the area, alongside the required geographical quality or reputation link.
notes: The EU regulation defines EU categories; their Serbian mapping depends on the separate Serbian law and labelling rulebook.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on procedures and methods of sensory evaluation of wine
summary: Requires wines with geographical origin to be assessed by an official sensory commission of at least three trained assessors, normally five or more, with independent scoring and a calculated final result.
notes: The rulebook establishes who evaluates; the recognition rulebook establishes that the resulting score selects K.P.K. or K.G.P.K. for the production year.

provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Articles 6 and 35

title: Balenović et al. 2021 — Factors Influencing Wine Purchasing by Generation Y and Older Cohorts on the Serbian Wine Market
provenance: Peer-reviewed primary survey conducted in Serbia from June to December 2020
summary: Among 1,438 wine consumers, 2.1% selected no extra payment for quality wine with controlled geographical origin, while 39.6% selected a 10–20% premium; geographical-origin information was important to online purchase. Recruitment used university staff emails and snowball sampling.
notes: Measures stated willingness to pay in a non-probability, education-heavy sample, not observed retail prices or equal mark incidence across price bands.

title: Ćirić et al. 2023 — Consumer attitudes and habits about products with geographical indication in Serbia
provenance: Peer-reviewed primary Serbian consumer survey of 399 respondents
summary: Reports that about 70% of respondents were willing to pay a higher price for products with geographical indications in Serbia.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on recognition of designations for still wines
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 121/2012 through 18/2024

title: Serbia — Rulebook on production methods and quality of table wines and wines with geographical origin
provenance: Reproduction of Official Gazette RS 87/2011 with 73/2024 cross-amendment
summary: Defines current categories including stono wine without geographical origin and the regional, kvalitetno/K.P.K. and vrhunsko/K.G.P.K. levels; sets regional-wine yields at 4.5/4 kg per vine or 13.5/16 t per hectare and controlled-quality yields at 2.5/2 kg or 7.5/8 t; sensory minima are 59, 79 and 89 respectively on a 100-point scale.
notes: The words stono, kvalitetno and vrhunsko remain operative legal category language; higher official scores are certification thresholds, not proof that every consumer will prefer the wine.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Article 6
summary: Requires K.P.K. or K.G.P.K. for the corresponding Serbian controlled categories and permits protected designation of origin/PDO beside either; country-of-origin labelling alone is not one of these category terms.

title: Serbia Ministry of Finance — Law on Excises, consolidated through Official Gazette 109/2025
provenance: Ministry of Finance consolidated text in force in 2026, Articles 2, 12, 12a and 18
summary: Taxes defined alcoholic beverages and requires control excise marks for covered products, but the definition comprises spirits, specified low-alcohol mixed drinks and beer rather than plain grape wine; wine appears as a possible ingredient of a low-alcohol drink, not as an independently excisable category.
notes: This conclusion concerns statutory wine itself, not every beverage or aromatised mixture that may contain wine.

title: Mondo / Beta — Nova klasifikacija vina u Srbiji
provenance: 2010 Beta report quoting Ministry of Agriculture adviser Darko Jakšić at introduction of the marks
summary: States that the Banknote Printing Institute would print evidenciona markica and that the marks guarantee a stated quality category and region; also identifies their number, category abbreviation and vintage.
notes: Useful for the printer identity at launch, but not a substitute for a current binding rule and not evidence of a separate current number register at the institute.

title: English Wikipedia — Serbian language
provenance: Required English Wikipedia two-script and alphabet comparison
summary: Describes active Serbian digraphia, interchangeable Cyrillic and Latin orthographies, one-to-one correspondence, Latin predominance in general retail packaging and a 30-letter table. It does not provide a wine-shelf sample, Russian-reader study, wine-label letter frequencies or the specific Despotika, Janko and Vinum findings.
notes: Its general packaging statement cannot by itself establish the frequency of scripts on Serbian wine bottles.

title: German Wikipedia — Serbische Sprache
provenance: Required German Wikipedia two-script and alphabet comparison
summary: States that both Cyrillic and Latin are used in daily life and supplies both 30-letter alphabets, including Ј/J, Љ/Lj, Њ/Nj, Ћ/Ć, Ђ/Đ and Џ/Dž. It contains no representative wine-label frequency, Russian comprehensibility test or evidence for the named winery examples.
notes: Useful secondary agreement on the writing systems, not a source for individual bottle appearance.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia targeted two-script and wine-label search
summary: No retrievable Hungarian Wikipedia passage was recovered that establishes script frequency on Serbian wine labels, Russian-reader comprehension, distinctive-letter frequency or the Despotika, Janko and Vinum bottle examples.
notes: The targeted corpus result is recorded for coverage only; absence does not contradict the Serbian language rulebook or producer photographs.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Српски језик
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language digraphia check
summary: Characterises Serbian by двоазбучност and names Serbian Cyrillic and Serbian Latin as its two scripts. It does not measure script use on the wine shelf or verify the named labels, Russian readability or letter frequency.
notes: Current Serbian wine regulations and first-party producer material determine the label-specific conclusions.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Сербский язык
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia two-script and Russian-reading comparison
summary: States that Serbian uses two 30-letter alphabets with one-to-one correspondence, gives Ј/J approximately as Russian й and lists the six Serbian Cyrillic characters absent from the Russian alphabet by comparison. Its general usage figures do not establish wine-shelf frequency or near-dictionary-free comprehension.
notes: The article's 2014 population poll is broader than packaging and cannot validate a claim about which special letter occurs most often on wine labels.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Srpski jezik
summary: Records the historical and current standard use of Cyrillic and Latin for Serbian and says modern Serbian orthographies treat both as standard scripts. It supplies no Serbian wine-shelf census, Russian-reader test, letter-frequency corpus or first-party support for the winery examples.
notes: Several historical assertions on the page are marked as lacking citations, so only the broad cross-Wikipedia agreement is used.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Article 7
summary: Requires the mandatory information in Articles 5–6 to appear in Serbian and expressly permits either Cyrillic or Latin script.
notes: The rule establishes permissibility, not the observed market share of either script.

title: Jung and Kim 2023 — Coexistence of Multiple Writing Systems: Classifying Digraphia in Post-Socialist Countries
provenance: Peer-reviewed comparative sociolinguistic article, Serbian case section
summary: Reports prior Serbian research concluding that roughly two-thirds of public and private texts use Latin and one-third Cyrillic, and describes free switching with different functions and prestige.
notes: The evidence concerns texts broadly, not a probability sample of wine packages; it supports Latin predominance only with that limitation.

title: UNGEGN — UN Romanization of Serbian for Geographical Names
provenance: UNGEGN Working Group report, version 4.0, Serbian table based on UN resolution III/11
summary: Provides an unambiguous, automatic and reversible 30-letter mapping, including Ђ/đ, Ј/j, Љ/lj, Њ/nj, Ћ/ć and Џ/dž; the table directly converts суво, црвено and винарија to their Latin forms.
notes: Romanization preserves the Serbian lexical item and pronunciation but does not erase visual, accessibility or sociolinguistic differences between scripts.

title: Vinarija Despotika — official homepage and wine photograph
provenance: First-party winery site and linked photograph of Despotika wines
summary: Places the winery in north-eastern Šumadija, presents the Serbian site in Cyrillic and shows three bottles whose prominent front-label and capsule branding is Cyrillic.
notes: The photograph supports visible front design; it is not sharp enough to prove that every item of mandatory fine print and every back label is exclusively Cyrillic.

title: Vinarija Janko — official wines, press excerpt and contact page
provenance: First-party winery website with product photography, quoted 2014 label description and current contact address
summary: Lists Janko wines, reproduces a description of Stari Zavet as having a Cyrillic label and identifies the winery at Rudnička 8, Smederevo.
notes: The page supports the Cyrillic example and physical location; the separate legal geography source explains why the wine area may still be called Beogradski rejon.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on recognition of designations for still wines
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 121/2012 through 18/2024, annex of controlled-origin names
summary: Lists Smederevsko vinogorje / Smederevo inside Beogradski rejon / Beograd.
notes: The regulated rejon name must not be confused with a claim that the winery's street address is in the city of Belgrade.

title: Vinarija Vinum — Bermet crveni 2023
provenance: First-party current product listing and linked bottle photograph
summary: Identifies the producer in Sremski Karlovci and the product as aromatised sweet red wine; its current front photograph visibly uses Latin Bermet crveni, AROMATIZOVANO CRVENO VINO and VINUM wording, with no registration mark visible on the shown neck or front.
notes: A front photograph cannot rule out an unseen mark elsewhere on a bottle, so the specific absence is not asserted; it only fails to verify the book's claimed neck mark.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on the appearance, content and display of the registration mark for wine with geographical origin
provenance: Reproduction of Official Gazette RS 67/2010, Articles 7–12
summary: Prescribes Cyrillic words and category codes on all three mark types and requires the mark on each original package of wine with geographical origin, visibly placed without requiring the neck as the only location.
notes: This general legal design does not prove that the photographed aromatised Vinum Bermet has such a mark.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Шумадия
provenance: Russian-language usage check for the Serbian geographic name Шумадија
summary: Uses the established Russian form Шумадия for the central Serbian historical region.
notes: Together with the letter mapping, it supports the example as conventional Russian usage rather than a universal transcription rule for every context.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Ракия
provenance: Russian-language usage check for South Slavic ракија / rakija
summary: Uses the established Russian beverage name ракия and includes South Slavic forms with intervocalic j/ј.
notes: The page confirms usage; the UNGEGN table supplies the underlying Serbian Ј/j correspondence.

title: English Wikipedia — Serbian wine
provenance: Required English Wikipedia current Serbian label-percentage and sensory-system check
summary: Gives broad history and regional reform context but no current rules for a named variety, vintage or smaller geographical unit, no historical 51% exception and no official sensory scale or category thresholds.
notes: Primary Serbian rulebooks determine every numeric conclusion in these blocks.

title: German Wikipedia — Weinbau in Serbien
provenance: Required German Wikipedia current Serbian label-percentage and sensory-system check
summary: Describes Serbian viticulture through an older regional frame and does not supply the operative 85% and 100% label rules, the obsolete 51% exception or the national 100-point sensory procedure.
notes: The article cannot distinguish the current and former Serbian scoring systems.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Serbian wine varietal label and sensory categories
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia targeted legal-label and sensory-score search
summary: No Hungarian Wikipedia treatment was recovered for the Serbian named-variety, vintage, smaller-area or multiple-variety percentages, the old 51% exception or the G.I./K.P.K. scoring systems.
notes: Absence in the requested corpus is not evidence against the Serbian legal texts.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — сорта 85%, берба и сензорно оцењивање вина
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language legal-label and sensory-score search
summary: No Serbian Wikipedia passage was recovered that reproduces the current articles 23, 24 and 30, traces the former 51% exception or distinguishes the present 100-point method from the earlier 20-point system.
notes: Current national rulebooks provide the operative local-language evidence.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Виноделие в Сербии
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia Serbian classification check
summary: Describes the broad 85% grape-origin rule for the PGI-like regional tier and two controlled-origin tiers, but not the separate label rules for variety, vintage and smaller units, the 51% history or either sensory scoring card.
notes: Its 85% regional-origin statement must not be substituted for the three distinct labelling provisions audited here.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Serbian wine 85% and sensory scoring
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia targeted legal-label and sensory-score search
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia material was recovered for the current Serbian percentage rules, historical 51% exception, official sensory scale or G.I. and K.P.K. minima.
notes: General Croatian or EU labelling rules cannot substitute for Serbian domestic provisions.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Articles 23, 24, 25 and 30
summary: Sets at least 85% for a named vintage and a single named variety, 100% collectively for several named varieties, and normally at least 85% from a named smaller area inside a GI specification; also states documentary, denominator, ordering and legacy exceptions.
notes: The three 85% rules have different conditions and exceptions, so they are not literally identical despite sharing a headline threshold.

title: Former SRJ/Serbian Rulebook on wine quality and other requirements
provenance: Historical text from Official List FRY 54/1999 and 39/2002 with later sectoral repeals
summary: Contains the former 51% traditional-variety exception for table wine with geographical origin and the old 20-point sensory card: colour 2, clarity 2, smell 4 and taste 12, with minima 15 and 16.5 for the earlier categories.
notes: These provisions explain older popular descriptions but do not override the current 2023/2024 labelling rule or current 100-point sensory method.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on procedures and methods of sensory evaluation of wine
provenance: Reproduction of Official Gazette RS 93/2015, applicable from 1 August 2016, Articles 23 and 31–35
summary: Requires at least three independent assessors for official work and defines a 100-point card with 20 visual, 30 olfactory, 30 gustatory and 20 gustatory-olfactory points, plus conformity assessment for GI, traditional term and variety.
notes: The act does not prescribe the category cutoffs itself; it directs classification to the separate wine-quality regulation.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on parameters and methods for analysis and quality determination of must and wine
provenance: Reproduction of Official Gazette RS 107/2014 and 72/2023, sensory method section
summary: Uses the positive-points system from 0 to 100 and sets minima of 39 for non-GI table wine, 59 for regional G.I., 79 for K.P.K. and 89 for K.G.P.K.; lists the current visual, olfactory, gustatory and gustatory-olfactory subcriteria.
notes: These are regulatory certification thresholds, not direct consumer ratings or linear conversions from the former 20-point system.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on recognition of designations for still wines
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 121/2012 through 18/2024, Article 13 and annual-control provisions
summary: Lists G.I. minima as 59/100 or 15/20 and controlled-origin minima as 79/100 or 16.5/20 depending on the scoring system, and links the category for a production year to sensory control alongside the designation specification.
notes: The paired numbers are thresholds of different scoring systems, not proportional equivalents; current methods and quality rules use the 100-point system.

title: English Wikipedia — Tamo daleko
summary: Describes Tamo daleko as a Serbian folk song associated with the First World War and 1916, and presents Đorđe Marinković as writer while noting the long authorship dispute. It contains no Serbian wine-labelling rules or evidence of physical back-label placement.
notes: The detailed designation, sweetness and optional-text conclusions come from current Serbian legislation; the winery's own page determines its recommendation wording.

title: German Wikipedia — Tamo daleko
summary: Characterises Tamo daleko as a traditional Serbian First World War song and treats the author as unknown, illustrating that public summaries do not agree on attribution. It supplies no Serbian label-law detail or Despotika package evidence.
notes: The disagreement is why the audit retains 'traditional/folk' only as genre or reception, not as proof of anonymous origin.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Tamo daleko
summary: Calls Tamo daleko a Serbian folk song and attributes its creation to an unnamed Serbian soldier, another variant of the disputed authorship history. It does not address Serbian wine designations, organic compliance, sweetness thresholds or labels.
notes: Used only for cross-language comparison, not to settle authorship.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Слово љубве
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language cultural check
summary: Identifies Slovo ljubve as Stefan Lazarević's poetic epistle or prose poem from the early fifteenth century, with 1404 or 1409 discussed. It contains no evidence about Dokaz's physical counterlabel or wine-labelling law.
notes: Independent Serbian cultural sources are also used for the work; winery recommendations come from Despotika itself.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Слово любви
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia title and date check
summary: Uses the Russian title Slovo lyubvi, attributes the work to Stefan Lazarević and places it in the first decade of the fifteenth century. It provides no Serbian wine-regulation detail or packaging photograph.
notes: The source validates the Russian cultural gloss, not the Despotika counterlabel claim.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Tamo daleko
summary: Describes Tamo daleko as a well-known traditional Serbian song from the First World War. It does not settle the competing authorship accounts and contains no national Serbian label-law or winery-package evidence.
notes: Used as one cross-language descriptor, with independent reporting retained for the authorship caveat.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Articles 2, 4, 22, 26–31 and Annex 4
summary: Permits optional information only within non-misleading and other legal constraints; sends organic expressions to separate organic-production rules; defines the still-wine and sparkling-wine sweetness vocabularies and restricts significant historic or territorial references.
notes: This act regulates much of the passage but is not the sole source for recognition definitions or organic certification.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on recognition of designations for still wines
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 121/2012 through 18/2024, Articles 6 and 19
summary: Allocates mlado and sopstvena proizvodnja to GI wine and arhivsko, rezerva/reserve and kasna berba from K.P.K. upward; defines the one-vintage March deadline, vineyard ownership/lease, colour-specific ageing and late-harvest sugar conditions.
notes: Arhivsko and rezerva are distinct regulated designations, not synonyms.

title: Serbia — Wine Law
provenance: Reproduction of the Serbian Wine Law, Article 36 category and additional-designation framework
summary: Lists mlado, sopstvena proizvodnja and the organic-grape formula among additional designations and places arhivsko/rezerva and late-harvest families within higher geographical-origin quality categories.
notes: More exact present definitions and labelling conditions are taken from the later consolidated rulebooks.

title: Serbia — Law on Organic Production
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 109/2025, Articles 19, 33 and certification/labelling provisions; applicable from 1 June 2026
summary: Requires organic wine to use organic raw materials and only authorised products and substances during oenological practices, processes and treatments; reserves organic terms for compliant products and establishes control, certification and labelling obligations.
notes: This is the operative organic statute on the audit date, replacing reliance on older summaries.

title: Vinarija Despotika — Dokaz 2020 product page
provenance: Current official winery product page, recommendation section and location metadata
summary: Places Dokaz in the Šumadijski rejon / Krnjevačko vinogorje and lists red-meat/roast/blue-fish food, 18 °C, Tamo daleko — Narodna pesma, and Slovo Ljubve — Despot Stefan Lazarević recommendations.
notes: The page verifies the exact recommendation content but shows no sufficiently clear back-label image to establish physical placement.

title: Hrvatska enciklopedija — Lazarević, Stefan
provenance: Croatian Encyclopaedia biographical entry by the Miroslav Krleža Institute of Lexicography
summary: Identifies Serbian despot Stefan Lazarević as the author of the epistle Slovo ljubve.
notes: Used with the Serbian cultural source for dating, and not for wine-label claims.

title: Politika — Kladovčanin autor pesme Tamo daleko
provenance: Politika report of 7 March 2008 on archive research and competing claims
summary: Reports documents linking lyrics and music to Đorđe Marinković, composition on Corfu in 1916 and Paris copyright registration in 1922, while reviewing rival attribution claims.
notes: Supports qualifying the conventional 'folk song' label rather than replacing it with a categorical settlement of authorship.

title: Manastir Manasija — Slovo ljubve despota Stefana Lazarevića
provenance: Manasija monastery cultural and literary presentation
summary: Describes Slovo ljubve as Stefan Lazarević's poetic epistle from the early fifteenth century, possibly 1409.
notes: Corroborates the cultural annotation independently of the winery.

title: English Wikipedia — Serbian wine
provenance: Required English Wikipedia non-GI label and quick-reading check
summary: Provides broad Serbian wine and regional context but does not describe evidenciona markica placement, trademark exceptions, imported GI labels, current retail shelf shares or a producer-and-variety reading algorithm.
notes: Current Serbian statutes, rulebooks and administrative statistics determine the findings.

title: German Wikipedia — Weinbau in Serbien
provenance: Required German Wikipedia non-GI and shelf check
summary: Contains no current treatment of the Serbian GI registration mark, its permissible placement, geographical names in brands, import exceptions, retail shelf proportions or consumer decision rules.
notes: Its older regional overview cannot validate the present legal or market claims.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Serbian non-GI wine labels and geographical trademarks
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia targeted legal and label search
summary: No sufficiently specific Hungarian Wikipedia result was found for Serbian mark placement, protected category codes, geographical trademarks on non-GI wine, imported GI treatment or retail shelf shares.
notes: Search absence neither proves nor disproves the Serbian rules.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — vino bez geografskog porekla, žig and evidenciona markica
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language targeted check
summary: No Serbian Wikipedia passage was recovered that specifies the legal category reservation, mark placement, prior-trademark exception, imported GI distinction, 2025 production share or retail reading heuristic.
notes: Primary Serbian legislation controls the legal conclusions.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Виноделие в Сербии
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia non-GI and reading-order check
summary: Offers only a broad description of Serbian wine regions and origin control; it does not document mark location, geographical brand-name prohibitions and exceptions, imported GI treatment, shelf composition or the proposed ten-second algorithm.
notes: The article cannot support an inference from one empty bottle neck.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Serbian non-GI wine, mark and geographical trademark
summary: No sufficiently specific Croatian Wikipedia evidence was found for current Serbian mark placement, use of GI names in trademarks, import treatment, shelf proportions or consumer reading order.
notes: General terminology is insufficient for these national legal distinctions.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on the appearance, content and display of the registration mark for wine with geographical origin
provenance: Reproduction of Official Gazette RS 67/2010, Articles 2–6
summary: Requires a mark on every individual original package of wine holding the Ministry's annual GI-use and release decision, defines the three category colours and requires placement that is conspicuous and legible without naming the bottle neck as mandatory.
notes: Its ministerial-decision definition concerns the Serbian registration-mark system and does not make the sticker a universal sign for imported GI wine.

title: Serbia — Wine Law
provenance: Reproduction of the Serbian Wine Law, Articles 31, 33–35 and 44
summary: Makes evidenciona markica mandatory for domestic GI wine, reserves G.I./K.P.K./K.G.P.K. for use with a geographical designation, forbids misleading or unauthorised geographical trade names and preserves only qualifying good-faith trademarks predating GI recognition.
notes: A missing required mark can be a violation; it does not logically reclassify a bottle as lawful non-GI wine.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Articles 4–8, 22–26
summary: Forbids non-GI packaging that imitates GI wine or uses a vineyard production area, protected designation or part of one; gives a narrowly formatted prior-trademark exception, preserves original imported GI categories, and lists mandatory and optional label information including conditional variety and vintage.
notes: The rule distinguishes a geographical product name from mandatory country of origin and producer address.

title: Ministry of Agriculture of Serbia — Green Book 2025, Book II
provenance: Official annual report on agriculture in the Republic of Serbia for 2025, printed pages 39–40
summary: Reports a 2025 declared-production split of 91% wine without GI, 4% G.I. and 5% combined K.P.K./K.G.P.K. in Winery Register volume.
notes: The report does not count retail SKUs, bottles, shelf space or sales and therefore cannot establish a shelf majority.

title: English Wikipedia — Serbian wine
summary: Gives broad regional and varietal context but does not document registration-mark colours and Cyrillic codes, the hierarchy of label geographies, Serbian 85% rules or whether berba must precede a vintage year.
notes: Current national rulebooks control all four findings.

title: German Wikipedia — Weinbau in Serbien
summary: Does not specify the Serbian mark's colour/category map, distinguish which geographical level appears on a label, state current variety/vintage thresholds or require the word berba.
notes: Older regional summaries are not a substitute for the 2023/2024 rulebook.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Serbian wine mark colour, vintage and berba
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia targeted label search
summary: No sufficiently specific Hungarian Wikipedia evidence was found for mark colours, region/rejon/vinogorje label levels, current percentage rules or berba typography.
notes: Search absence does not adjudicate the Serbian legal text.

title: Serbian Wikipedia search — evidenciona markica, berba and wine geography
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language targeted check
summary: No Serbian Wikipedia result was recovered that supplies the protected mark design, exact label-geography hierarchy, optional-data thresholds or a general requirement to write berba before the year.
notes: Primary Serbian regulations are decisive.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Виноделие в Сербии
summary: Mentions Serbian wine categories and regions only broadly; it does not establish the registration-mark design, all geographical label levels, current 85% conditions or the scope of the word berba.
notes: The Russian-language overview cannot validate the ten-second reading instructions.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Serbian wine mark, harvest year and vinogorje
summary: No sufficiently specific Croatian Wikipedia evidence was found for the colour code, category abbreviations, precise geography level, varietal/vintage conditions or berba placement.
notes: General cognate terminology does not establish Serbian legal requirements.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on the appearance, content and display of the registration mark for wine with geographical origin
provenance: Reproduction of Official Gazette RS 67/2010, Articles 6–9 and 11–12
summary: Maps green/red/purple and Cyrillic Г.И./К.П.К./К.Г.П.К. to the three categories and requires Cyrillic БЕРБА followed by the four-digit vintage on every mark; mark placement is conspicuous on the package, not tied to the main label's script.
notes: The protected mark template must not be generalised into a typography requirement for every producer label.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Articles 6, 22–25 and Annex 2
summary: Requires the recognised geographical designation on GI wine, lists region/rejon/vinogorje names, treats vintage and variety as optional with 85% or multiple-variety conditions, and imposes no general berba-before-year formula.
notes: Additional smaller or larger geography is conditional on the GI framework and specification.

title: Serbia — Wine Law
provenance: Reproduction of the Serbian Wine Law, Articles 6 and 34–35
summary: Defines a geographical indication through a region and controlled geographical origin through a rejon or vinogorje, with the three quality-category terms layered onto those recognised designations.
notes: The consumer-facing generic question should therefore ask for the geographical designation, not only vinogorje.

title: Prokupac — English Wikipedia
summary: Identifies Prokupac as a Serbian Vitis vinifera variety and mentions freshness and dark fruit, but gives none of the exact Blaufränkisch/Cabernet Franc/Shiraz/Pinot sequence, Syrah identity myth, Cabernet error frequency or Aleksić quotation.
notes: Useful only as baseline identity and broad wine-style context; it does not adjudicate the disputed analogies.

title: Prokupac — German Wikipedia
summary: Records Serbia, VIVC 9734 and unknown ancestry and describes spicy, fruit-driven, often alcoholic wines, but does not supply the book's comparison row, Syrah claim, claimed error frequency or Sangiovese attribution.
notes: Its unknown-ancestry statement must not be used to infer either relation or non-relation to Syrah.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Prokupac, Syrah and Kékfrankos
summary: No sufficiently specific Hungarian Wikipedia article or passage was found for Prokupac's proposed comparison set, genetic relation to Syrah, Cabernet expectation frequency or Aleksić quotation.
notes: Kékfrankos material alone cannot establish a comparison with Prokupac.

title: Прокупац — Serbian Wikipedia
summary: Provides viticultural and organoleptic descriptions of Prokupac, including refreshing wine, ruby colour and neutral aroma, but does not state the exact international-variety analogies, Syrah identity claim, Cabernet error frequency or Aleksić wording.
notes: The local-language article is descriptive but does not support the book's source-attribution claims.

title: Russian Wikipedia search — Prokupac and proposed analogues
summary: No Russian Wikipedia article or passage was found that documents Prokupac's exact analogy row, the identity myth, claimed most-common expectation error or Aleksić comparison; articles on the proposed analogue varieties do not bridge that gap.
notes: Independent descriptions of Blaufränkisch or Syrah are not evidence that tasters compare them with Prokupac.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Prokupac, Syrah and Blaufränkisch
summary: No sufficiently specific Croatian Wikipedia evidence was found for the proposed sensory sequence, Prokupac–Syrah identity story, Cabernet expectation frequency or Prokupac–Sangiovese attribution.
notes: The absence is recorded as a corpus gap, not as proof that the comparisons never circulate.

title: Caroline Gilby MW — Made in Serbia
provenance: JancisRobinson.com, 9 November 2017; named author and attributed expert views
summary: Reports Igor Luković's Pinot Noir plus Cabernet Franc analogy; Gilby instead sees Blaufränkisch/Kékfrankos or Kadarka and advises Pinot-like gentle, elegant handling rather than Cabernet-Sauvignon-style extraction, intensity and structure.
notes: The article separates the viewpoints and documents varied styles and blends; it does not claim a canonical four-variety row or measure the most frequent expectation error.

title: Prokupac, the King of Zupa
summary: States only that some are said to compare Prokupac with Shiraz, presenting the analogy as reported opinion rather than identity or consensus.
notes: The passive wording provides no named comparator and cannot establish the book's exact combined row.

title: Zvonko Herceg — Makedonski Syrah: Vino novog Starog sveta
summary: Reports that some, including Wine-Searcher, believe Prokupac might actually be Syrah because of stylistic and organoleptic similarity; it presents this as others' belief and gives no southern-Serbia location.
notes: This documents circulation, not truth, prevalence or geography of the belief.

title: VIVC passport — PROKUPAC
provenance: Vitis International Variety Catalogue, variety number 9734
summary: Registers PROKUPAC as a noir wine grape associated with Serbia under its own VIVC identifier.
notes: A separate passport establishes catalogue distinction from Syrah; the word passport alone should not be inflated into a full published pairwise kinship test.

title: VIVC passport — SYRAH
provenance: Vitis International Variety Catalogue, variety number 11748
summary: Registers SYRAH separately as VIVC 11748 and records the full marker-confirmed pedigree Mondeuse Blanche × Dureza.
notes: This refutes synonymy with Prokupac but does not by itself prove that no remote common ancestor can exist.

title: Tello et al. — The genetic characterization of grapevines prospected in old Serbian vineyards reveals multiple relationships between traditional varieties of the Balkans
summary: Identifies Prokupac as an ancient Serbian variety and founder of a lineage extending through four continuous generations of Balkan-related cultivars within a complex regional pedigree network.
notes: Syrah is not discussed in the study, so it supports the positive Balkan-network statement but only contextualises, rather than directly tests, a Prokupac–Syrah relationship.

title: TEMET
provenance: BalkanWines producer profile; original text credited to Tomislav Ivanović, Swedish translation by Paola Allegrini
summary: Attributes to Nebojša Aleksić the view that Prokupac has the potential to gain the same significance for Serbia that Sangiovese has for Tuscany.
notes: The accessible page is a translated profile rather than a transcript; its modal claim is potential future significance, not present parity or sensory resemblance.

title: English Wikipedia — Tamjanika and Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains
provenance: Required English Wikipedia check with linked cultivar article
summary: Places Tamjanika in the Muscat group and the linked Muscat Blanc article names Tamjanika as its Serbian synonym, distinguishes Muscat Ottonel and notes that Alsace Muscat can involve different family members; the Tamjanika page itself confusingly mixes white and dark-berry descriptions.
notes: Useful for nomenclature context, but the page's colour inconsistency makes primary genetic and institutional sources necessary.

title: German Wikipedia search — Tamjanika, Muscateller and Muscat Ottonel
summary: Finds material on the large Muscateller group and Tamjanika Crna, but no sufficiently precise German Wikipedia evidence that identifies the entire Serbian white Tamjanika group with Muscat à Petits Grains or resolves the exact Alsace comparison.
notes: The black Tamjanika entry is a different cultivar and cannot validate the white anchor.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — Tamjanika, Sárgamuskotály and Ottonel muskotály
summary: No sufficiently specific Hungarian Wikipedia passage was found that establishes the Serbian Tamjanika population's identity or the exact permitted and typical composition of Alsace Muscat.
notes: Hungarian names for the two Muscats do not by themselves connect a Serbian accession to either one.

title: Тамјаника — Serbian Wikipedia
summary: Says multiple Tamjanika forms exist and distinguishes white and black, but does not provide genetic identification with VIVC 8193 or reliable evidence for the Alsace Petits Grains/Ottonel comparison.
notes: The short page has internally awkward colour and origin claims and relies on sparse references, so it cannot control cultivar identity.

title: Мускаты — Russian Wikipedia
