notes: Companion URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vineyard. English conceptual separation corroborates the objects only; Serbian law and the Serbian article establish the local words.

title: German Wikipedia — Weintraube and Weinberg
summary: Defines Weintrauben as grapevine fruit clusters and Weinberg as agriculturally used viticultural land, but supplies no evidence about the Serbian–Russian cognate pair.
notes: Companion URL: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weinberg. The German two-word contrast is conceptual context, not a translation authority for Serbian.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Szőlő and vineyard terminology
summary: Uses szőlő broadly for the grapevine genus and fruit context and szőlőültetvény for a vineyard plantation, but does not discuss Serbian grožđe/vinograd or the Russian false friend.
notes: Companion URL: https://hu.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sz%C5%91l%C5%91_term%C5%91helyi_kataszter. Hungarian lexical organisation differs and cannot establish the Serbian mapping.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Грожђе and Виноград
provenance: Required Serbian-language encyclopedia direct lexical definitions
summary: Defines грожђе as the fruit of Vitis plants and виноград as agricultural land planted with grapevines and used for viticulture or grape production, directly confirming the book's Serbian-side distinction.
notes: Companion URL: https://sr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%92%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B3%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B4. The fruit article is weakly sourced, so the national law independently supplies the same sector usage.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Виноград (ягода) and Виноградник
provenance: Required Russian-language encyclopedia direct comparison-side definitions
summary: Defines Russian виноград as edible grape fruit and виноградник as a plot of land on which grapes are grown, directly establishing the Russian side of the false-friend contrast.
notes: Companion URL: https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%92%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B3%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BA. Russian polysemy may extend to plant or genus contexts, but the everyday fruit sense remains distinct from the land term.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Vinova loza and grape-harvest usage
summary: Uses grožđe for the grapevine fruit and vinograd or vinogradi for the planted cultivation area, corroborating the same lexical division in the neighbouring standard without proving Serbian–Russian reader difficulty.
notes: Companion URL: https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berba_gro%C5%BE%C4%91a. Serbian national usage is established separately by Serbian sources.

title: Viktoria Kaprielova — Translator's false friends in Russian and Serbian from the perspective of semantic-shift theory
provenance: Original research article in Slavistika XXVII/1 (2023), DOI 10.18485/slavistika.2023.27.1.16
summary: Defines Russian–Serbian false friends as formally similar words whose meanings diverged through asymmetric polysemy or cognate semantic development in the two closely related languages.
notes: The article's examples concern temporal vocabulary and do not list vinograd itself; application to vinograd is an explicit inference from the independently verified Serbian and Russian definitions.

title: Government of Serbia — Improving the legal framework for further development of Serbian winemaking
provenance: Official Government of Serbia report dated 21 May 2026
summary: Reports a ministry round table on the draft Law on Wine and Other Products of Grapes and Wine, confirming that the proposed replacement framework was still a draft on that date.
notes: This dated item alone cannot exclude adoption after 21 May; the official legal-information system accessed on 27 August supplies the current-law check.

title: English Wikipedia — Sparkling wine and Oak (wine)
summary: Defines sparkling wine through significant dissolved carbon dioxide and describes oak barrels as vessels used for wine fermentation or aging, with effects depending on contact, size, age and treatment. It contains no Serbian lexical derivation or direct translation authority for pena, hrast, bure or odležati.
notes: Companion URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_(wine). The article itself warns of incomplete inline citation, so national law, Serbian lexicography and OIV carry the exact conclusions.

title: German Wikipedia — Schaumwein and Barrique
summary: Treats Schaumwein as the German sparkling-wine concept and Barrique as an oak cask used for wine maturation, distinguishing small barriques from generic barrels and noting effects of newness, toast and use. It supplies no evidence for the Serbian word forms.
notes: Companion URLs: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrique and https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fass. German terminology corroborates the objects, not the Serbian-to-Russian translation.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Pezsgő and Barrique
summary: Covers Hungarian sparkling wine as pezsgő and defines barrique both as an oak barrel used for wine maturation and the corresponding method. It provides general concept comparison but no Serbian pena/penušav or hrast/bure morphology.
notes: Companion URL: https://hu.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrique. The verified-page status does not make it a Serbian lexical authority.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Penušavo vino, Бачва and Храст
provenance: Required Serbian-language encyclopedia direct terminology corpus
summary: Uses penušavo vino as the Serbian article title and defines it through carbon dioxide that makes the wine penušav. Separate articles define bure/bačva as a vessel, traditionally wooden and commonly used for wine, and hrast as Quercus; the wine article also shows the ordinary collocation hrastova burad for wine aging.
notes: Companion URLs: https://sr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B2%D0%B0, https://sr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%81%D1%82 and https://sr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%92%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE. These pages do not document historical morphology or label-law distinctions.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Игристое вино and Баррик (бочка)
summary: Supplies the full Russian category expression игристое вино and defines баррик as an oak barrel used for wine maturation. Generic barrel and oak pages corroborate бочка and дуб, but none establishes the Serbian source words or the exact scope of Serbian law.
notes: Companion URLs: https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BA_(%D0%B1%D0%BE%D1%87%D0%BA%D0%B0), https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%BE%D1%87%D0%BA%D0%B0 and https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%94%D1%83%D0%B1_(%D0%B4%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B0). Barrique is narrower than generic bure.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Pjenušac and Barrique
summary: Uses pjenušavo vino as the broad Croatian sparkling-wine phrase and pjenušac for a principal type; its Barrique page explicitly describes wine kept in oak barrels. This neighbouring standard corroborates the cognate vocabulary but cannot replace Serbian definitions or current Serbian product law.
notes: Companion URLs: https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrique and https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba%C4%8Dva. The Pjenušac article's production generalisations are not used for the Serbian legal distinction.

title: Matica Srpska six-volume dictionary — pena, penušav, hrast, hrastov, bure and odležati
provenance: Searchable digitisation of Rečnik srpskohrvatskoga književnog jezika, with original volume and page metadata
summary: Defines pena as a multitude of small bubbles, penušav as that which foams, hrast as the Quercus oak genus, hrastov as made of or relating to oak, and bure as a wooden barrel of varying size. Its wine-specific third sense of odležati is to gain better taste through longer standing.
notes: Companion entry URLs replace the final lemma with pena, hrast, hrastov, bure and odležati. The digitisation exposes scans and flags OCR damage in unrelated examples; the definitions used here are visually and structurally clear. It establishes a transparent word family, not a reconstructed Proto-Slavic etymology.

title: OIV International Code of Oenological Practices — Ageing in small capacity wooden containers
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine adopted oenological practice II.3.5.12.1
summary: Defines the process as aging suitable wine in wooden casks for a set period and explains controlled oxygenation and progressive release of wood substances; it lists common oak species and recommends traceability and container information.
notes: The OIV process definition corroborates the meaning of the Serbian phrase but does not translate Serbian. Its small-container recommendation is not evidence that every generic bure is a 225-litre barrique.

title: English Wiktionary — Serbo-Croatian penušav
provenance: Collaborative lexical entry used only as secondary grammar corroboration
summary: Glosses penušav as foamy and supplies the singular adjective paradigm penušav, penušava, penušavo, directly confirming that penušavo is the neuter nominative form used with vino.
notes: The entry contains no etymology section and is not relied on for historical derivation; Matica Srpska supplies the authoritative semantic evidence.

title: English Wikipedia — Natural wine and Wine label
provenance: Required English-language encyclopedia natural-wine and bottler-label corpus
summary: Says natural wine has no uniform definition and is usually associated with limited or no SO2, filtration and fining. The companion label article distinguishes producer and bottler and says that where they differ the label can identify wine bottled by one party for another. Neither article contains Serbian nefiltrirano, bez sumpora or punjeno u, and neither supports inferring another legal person from place alone.
notes: Companion URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_label. The current Natural wine page contains unstable and weakly sourced material outside the points used here; exact chemistry and Serbian label law come from primary sources.

title: German Wikipedia — Naturwein, Sulfite and Erzeugerabfüllung
provenance: Required German-language encyclopedia natural-wine, sulfite and estate-bottling corpus
summary: Describes Naturwein as not uniformly regulated, treats omission of filtration aids as characteristic and records disagreement over added sulfur. The Sulfite article says small quantities arise naturally during alcoholic fermentation, while Erzeugerabfüllung requires the same operation to grow, vinify, mature and bottle. These pages give useful comparative concepts but no Serbian phrase, Serbian contract-bottling rule or Serbian trend count.
notes: Companion URLs: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfite and https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erzeugerabf%C3%BCllung. Their German and EU context cannot be transplanted into Serbian labelling law.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Kálium-metabiszulfit and targeted natural-wine/bottler searches
summary: Explains that potassium metabisulfite is added to must or wine and releases SO2, but supplies no endogenous-fermentation evidence and no definition of natural wine. Targeted searches recovered no Hungarian article relevant to Serbian nefiltrirano, bez sumpora, punjeno u, Serbian bottler identification or growth of the Serbian natural-wine scene.
notes: For C2513-C2515 and the exact Serbian lexical claims, this is explicitly no relevant material; the national rule, peer-reviewed microbiology and Serbian producer usage carry those conclusions.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Винарство and targeted natural-wine/label searches
summary: Discusses sulfur dioxide and metabisulfite as winemaking additions and describes ordinary filtration-related production context, but does not define natural wine, distinguish no added from zero total sulfites, document yeast-produced SO2, or explain nefiltrirano and bez sumpora as label expressions. Targeted searches found no Serbian Wikipedia treatment of punjeno u, bottler identity or the Serbian trend claim.
notes: The page is weakly sourced and contains imported generalisations, so it is not used for the exact conclusions. Current Serbian law and direct Serbian usage are decisive.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Натуральное вино and Винная этикетка
provenance: Required Russian-language encyclopedia translation-side natural-wine and label corpus
summary: Associates natural winemaking with refusal of filtration and minimal or no added sulfur dioxide and acknowledges the lack of a generally recognised international definition. The label article lists producer and place of bottling as separate information. Neither article establishes the Serbian source phrases, the yeast mechanism, Serbian trend, or the legal inference from a different bottling place.
notes: Companion URL: https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%92%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%8D%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B5%D1%82%D0%BA%D0%B0. The natural-wine article has conspicuous sourcing and terminology problems, so it is only comparative corroboration.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Kalijev metabisulfit and targeted natural-wine/bottler searches
summary: Explains that the enological additive potassium metabisulfite releases sulfur dioxide and is used in must and wine. Targeted Croatian searches recovered no dedicated article defining natural wine, documenting endogenous wine sulfites, or explaining Serbian nefiltrirano, bez sumpora, punjeno u, bottler identity and the Serbian growth trend.
notes: For the bottling claims and the exact Serbian expressions this is explicitly no relevant material. Neighbouring Croatian vocabulary cannot replace current Serbian rules.

title: Capece et al. — Biotechnological Approach Based on Selected Saccharomyces cerevisiae Starters for Reducing the Use of Sulfur Dioxide in Wine
provenance: Microorganisms 8(5), 738 (2020), DOI 10.3390/microorganisms8050738, public full text in PubMed Central
summary: Explicitly distinguishes wine made without SO2 addition from wine with zero sulfites and states that wine cannot be completely sulfite-free because yeasts naturally produce SO2 during fermentation. It reports strain- and must-dependent endogenous amounts and experimentally produces acceptable no-SO2-added wine.
notes: This supports the book's mechanism, while also showing why «without sulfur» is an imprecise label. It does not define Serbian words or natural wine as a legal category.

title: OIV — Review of practices for the reduction of SO2 doses used in winemaking
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine technical review and good-practice guidance
summary: States that besides being added, sulfur dioxide is produced by yeasts during alcoholic fermentation, potentially up to 100 mg/l depending on strain and must composition, and distinguishes total, free, bound and molecular SO2. It also records the 10 mg/l total-SO2 labelling threshold in the EU context and sets out reduction rather than presumed zero-content practices.
notes: OIV supplies the international technical synthesis; Serbia's current rule separately confirms the same 10 mg/l allergen threshold and exact local label terms.

title: Maurer — Babba and current wine range
provenance: Official website of Serbian natural-wine producer Oszkár Maurer
summary: The Babba product description uses the explicit sequence «Nefiltrirano, nepročišćeno, bez dodatog sumpora», directly separating unfiltered, unfined and no-added-sulfur claims and demonstrating the more precise Serbian expansion that the book's shortened bez sumpora omits.
notes: A producer page establishes its wording and practice claim, not independent chemical verification, a universal natural-wine definition or a national frequency trend.

title: MICHELIN Guide — Natural wines in Serbia: an increasing interest in sustainability
provenance: 2022 feature created by the MICHELIN Guide in collaboration with the National Tourism Organisation of Serbia, based substantially on producer interviews
summary: Describes natural wine as a still-niche low-intervention sector and reports unfiltered/unfined practice. Interviewees say producer numbers increase year by year, interest had exploded over the preceding three or four years, and more young Serbian consumers were becoming curious; the article concludes that interest was growing across the country.
notes: The claims are attributable and useful for direction, but collaboration with the tourism body and reliance on two producers mean this is not an independent census or time series.

title: Osservatorio Balcani Caucaso Transeuropa — Oskar Maurer and Serbia's natural wine revolution
provenance: Registered independent regional publication, Ian Bancroft feature dated 13 August 2024
summary: Describes Serbia's natural-wine movement through minimal intervention, limited or absent added sulfites and unfiltered wines; states there is no real legal definition, names several Serbian producers, and reports greater expert attention and recognition beyond Serbia.
notes: The article is interview-led and does not count producers across years, so it corroborates a growing scene but cannot quantify «становится всё больше». Its headache statement is not used.

title: English Wikipedia — Wine cellar and Winery
provenance: Required English-language encyclopedia cellar-versus-winery corpus and targeted Negotinske Pivnice search
summary: Defines a wine cellar as a room for storing wine and a winery as a wine-producing building, property or business, independently illustrating why cellar, winery and winemaker are different referents even when usage can move between facility and enterprise. It contains no Serbian podrum or pimnica, no evidence for the frequency of idemo u podrum, and no useful Negotin-specific architecture.
notes: Companion URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winery. These broad English categories cannot by themselves establish a Serbian metonymy or regional term.

title: German Wikipedia — Weinkeller and Kellerei
provenance: Required German-language encyclopedia cellar-versus-winery corpus and targeted Negotinske Pivnice search
summary: Defines Weinkeller as wine storage space and Kellerei as an enterprise for producing, storing, bottling and selling wine or other alcoholic drinks. This comparative distinction supports the place-versus-enterprise caution but supplies no Serbian podrum or pimnica, no colloquial-frequency evidence and no Negotin-specific construction evidence.

Targeted searches found no treatment of Serbian podrum, pimnica, the exact colloquial sentence or Negotinske Pivnice architecture.

The Negotinske article defines complexes of wine cellars; Rajačke gives pivnice ili pimnice, while Negotinske and Štubičke record mixed stone, timber, frame, brick and mud construction and different settlement forms.

Article quality varies; UNESCO and the research paper carry the architectural conclusion.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Винодельческое хозяйство and targeted wine-cellar search
provenance: Required Russian-language encyclopedia target-translation and winery corpus
summary: Defines a winery as a wine-producing enterprise and lists aging cellars as characteristic parts of it, confirming in the target language that a cellar is not automatically the enterprise or the winemaker as person. Targeted searches recovered no dedicated reliable page establishing Serbian podrum, pimnica, the exact colloquial example or Negotin construction details.
notes: The winery page itself is flagged as under-cited and is used only as comparative translation-side context.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Vinski podrum and Vinarija
provenance: Required Croatian-language neighbouring encyclopedia cellar-versus-winery corpus and targeted Serbian-term search
summary: Defines vinski podrum as a room for storing and maturing finished wine, while Vinarija begins with the broader equation vinarija ili vinski podrum for a wine-production, storage and transfer facility. This neighbouring usage corroborates semantic extension to a facility but not Serbian colloquial frequency. Targeted searches found no Croatian treatment of Serbian pimnica or Negotin architecture.
notes: Companion URL: https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinarija. Croatian usage is comparative evidence and cannot replace direct Serbian sources.

title: Tehnologija hrane — Vinarija
provenance: Serbian food-technology reference article published 29 December 2017
summary: Defines vinarski podrum as any room in which wine is kept and vinarije as large wine cellars equipped for industrial production, storage and distribution; later it uses the parenthetical equivalence vinarija (podrum). This directly supports the technical facility extension while retaining the literal room sense.
notes: The article uses a mixed Serbian/Croatian technical register and does not measure ordinary conversational frequency or validate the exact sentence idemo u podrum.

title: Hrvatski jezični portal — pòdrum
provenance: Current searchable Croatian lexical database, used as neighbouring-language corroboration only
summary: Gives the primary meaning as a room partly or wholly below ground level and secondary senses including an alcoholic-drink shop or a type of restaurant. It confirms that the cognate word has metonymic extensions, but does not list winery as a dictionary sense and cannot establish Serbian frequency.
notes: Direct Serbian encyclopedia and usage examples remain primary for the Serbian claim; Croatian lexical evidence is not silently transferred across standards.

title: English Wikipedia — House wine, Vintage and Harvest (wine)
provenance: Required English-language encyclopedia hospitality and vintage/harvest corpus with targeted Serbian-term search
summary: Defines house wine as generally inexpensive wine served in restaurants, often without producer, origin or variety details, and notes service by glass, carafe or bottle; this is a restaurant category, not a claim of household production or exemption from regulation. Vintage describes both grape picking and wine made wholly or primarily from one specified year and records an 85% rule for EU-labelled vintage. It supplies no Serbian kućno vino or berba definition, Serbian certification status, kafana frequency or retail-shelf measurement.
notes: Companion URLs: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vintage ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvest_(wine). The international 85% comparison corroborates but does not replace current Serbian law.

title: German Wikipedia — Hauswein and Jahrgang (Wein)
provenance: Required German-language encyclopedia house-wine and vintage corpus with targeted Serbian-term search
summary: Distinguishes an older private-use sense of Hauswein from the hospitality sense of an unspecified open wine served in restaurants, hotels and inns; restaurant house wine may change and is selected by the venue. Jahrgang states that a labelled vintage may contain a small other-year share and gives a minimum 85% same-year rule. Neither article defines Serbian kućno vino or berba, determines certification, or measures Serbian restaurant and shop frequency.
notes: Companion URL: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jahrgang_(Wein). German lexical history is comparative evidence, not a Serbian definition.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Bor (ital) and targeted house-wine/vintage search
provenance: Required Hungarian-language encyclopedia wine corpus and targeted kućno vino, házi bor, house-wine, vintage and harvest search
summary: The general wine article illustrates and discusses grape harvest and acknowledges blends from more than one vintage, but targeted searches recovered no useful definition of a restaurant house wine, no Serbian kućno vino or berba, no Serbian 85% label condition, and no evidence about certification, kafana prevalence or shop rarity.
notes: Hungarian material contributes only broad wine context; direct Serbian law, usage and lexicography carry the conclusions.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Вино and targeted кућно вино search
provenance: Required Serbian-language encyclopedia wine/vintage corpus and direct exact-term search
summary: The wine article uses godina berbe and explains that non-vintage wines can combine multiple harvests, supporting the year-versus-multi-year distinction but not the Serbian 85% rule. An incidental airport-lounge article uses kućno vino as a bar offering, which is compatible with hospitality usage but supplies no definition. No Serbian Wikipedia article establishes that kućno means homemade or uncertified, quantifies kafana/shop frequency, or gives a lexical analysis of berba.
notes: Incidental companion URL: https://sr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B4%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%BC%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8_%D1%81%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD. It appears in a broad translated context and is corroborative only.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Винтаж (виноделие) and targeted house-wine search
provenance: Required Russian-language target-translation vintage corpus and targeted Serbian house-wine search
summary: Defines винтаж as wine, spirits or harvest of a specified year and therefore helps explain the target-language harvest/vintage distinction. Its unsourced blanket statement that European vintage material is 100% conflicts with the current Serbian 85% rule and with stronger comparative material, so it is not used for the threshold. Targeted searches found no relevant Serbian kućno vino or berba definition and no certification or market-frequency evidence.
notes: The legal conclusion follows the current Serbian rulebook, not this page's overly broad European assertion.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Berba grožđa, Vino and Kupaža
provenance: Required Croatian-language neighbouring encyclopedia harvest and vintage-label corpus with targeted house-wine search
summary: Directly treats berba grožđa as grape harvesting, the general wine page uses godište berbe as a normal wine descriptor, and Kupaža states a Croatian minimum of 85% from the labelled harvest year. This neighbouring corpus corroborates the dual harvest/vintage frame and percentage caution but does not define Serbian kućno vino, establish Serbian certification, or measure Serbian kafana and retail frequency.
notes: Companion URLs: https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vino ; https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kupa%C5%BEa. Croatian law is comparative only; Serbia's own current rulebook is decisive.

title: Serbia — Wine Law
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 41/2009 and 93/2012, especially Articles 4, 10, 17, 27–30 and 46–50
summary: Exempts a natural person's wine only when produced for personal needs and experimental wine only when not marketed; commercial producers must enter the Business and Wine Registers. Before filling, labelling and marketing, wine undergoes mandatory quality testing and sensory assessment by authorised structures. End-consumer wine normally requires prescribed original packaging, while bulk sale is narrowly allowed at the producer's own winery and registered wine events and prohibited in hospitality establishments. The law also uses berba grožđa for the harvesting operation.
notes: The statute regulates testing, registration, packaging and GI controls rather than creating one universal certificate called certification for every wine. Kućno vino itself is not a statutory category; poured wine in a restaurant need not mean unlawful bulk circulation because it may be poured from compliant original packaging.

title: Hrvatski jezični portal — bèrba
provenance: Current searchable Croatian lexical database, used as neighbouring-language corroboration
summary: Defines berba as large-scale picking and gathering, the time when fruits are picked, and, usually with a year designation, the time when the grapes used to make a wine were harvested. It directly records both the harvesting action/time and year-associated wine sense in the neighbouring standard.
notes: Because this is Croatian, direct Serbian statutory usage and Serbian Wiktionary examples are retained rather than silently transferring the entry across standards.

title: Serbian Wiktionary — berba
provenance: Serbian Wiktionary entry drawing examples from dialectological sources
summary: Lists berba grožđa and examples of people coming to or being in berba, plus harvesting corn, directly supporting Serbian use for the work or event of harvesting.
notes: The short crowdsourced entry does not fully define the label-year sense; the rulebook and Croatian dictionary supply that separately.

title: Restoran Paša and Reka — current wine/drinks menus
provenance: Current first-party Serbian restaurant menu pages
summary: Paša lists Kućno vino in white, rosé and red at 1 l, 0.25 l and 0.15 l within its Serbian wine card; Reka lists Kućno vino — točeno, belo, 1 l. These are direct current hospitality examples, not evidence of household manufacture, certification status, national frequency or retail rarity.
notes: Companion URL: https://reka.co.rs/pice/. Menu wording and prices can change; access date is therefore material.

title: Vino & Fino — Na Salašu 137 izabrana najbolja vina od sile
provenance: Serbian specialist wine-and-gastronomy magazine report dated 28 April 2025
summary: Reports that Sila was the first draft house wine served when restaurant Salaš 137 opened 29 years earlier and remained in its offer. This identifies kućno vino with a restaurant-selected varietal wine and independently supports hospitality usage, but does not quantify the national market or state certification status.
notes: The historical continuity is reported by the venue context and not independently audited here; the source is useful chiefly for the semantic category.

title: Wine Style — Restoran Šaran
provenance: Serbian wine-and-lifestyle restaurant report originally dated 8 May 2012, page updated 25 November 2018
summary: Says Vinarija Jelić made a white and red Premium blend specifically for Šaran, served by the glass and in carafes, and later calls it Premium kućno vino podruma Jelić in a 0.25 l bottle. It directly shows that house wine may be producer-identified, specially commissioned and bottled rather than anonymous household wine.
notes: One restaurant case does not establish general frequency, retail rarity or legal compliance of all products.

title: Podrum Pevac — Roze vino KOKODA
provenance: Current first-party Serbian winery product presentation
summary: Presents the product as Cabernet Franc, suvo roze vino berba 2022, directly attesting the idiomatic berba-plus-year ordering in current Serbian consumer-facing wine text.
notes: A product webpage demonstrates usage, not a legally mandatory layout or a representative sample of physical bottle labels; the 85% meaning comes from the national rulebook.

title: English Wikipedia — Sweetness of wine
provenance: Required English-language encyclopedia sweetness-classification corpus with targeted Serbian-variety search
summary: Explains that perceived sweetness depends on sugar together with acidity, alcohol and tannin, and gives the still-wine sequence dry, medium dry, medium sweet and sweet with the 4/9, 12/18 and 45 g/l boundaries and acidity conditions. It contains no representative evidence for the sweetness distribution of Serbian Smederevka or Grašac.
notes: The comparative international table closely matches Serbia's current Annex 4, but the national rulebook remains decisive for Serbian label wording and limits.

title: German Wikipedia — Geschmacksangabe (Wein)
provenance: Required German-language encyclopedia wine-sweetness corpus with targeted Serbian-variety search
summary: Distinguishes subjective sweetness from analytical values and defines trocken, halbtrocken, lieblich and süß with the same residual-sugar and acidity-dependent boundaries used in the comparable European system. It supplies no Serbian suvo lexicography and no market sample for Smederevka or Grašac.
notes: German labels are comparative evidence only; their terms do not replace the Serbian expressions in the national rulebook.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Bor (ital)
provenance: Required Hungarian-language encyclopedia wine-sweetness corpus with targeted Serbian-variety search
summary: Lists száraz, félszáraz, félédes and édes in increasing sugar order and gives the comparable 4/9, 12/18 and 45 g/l frame, confirming that the dry and medium-dry categories include acidity-conditioned extensions. It has no evidence for how often Serbian Smederevka or Grašac is dry.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Грузијска вина and targeted sweetness search
provenance: Required Serbian-language encyclopedia exact-descriptor usage and Serbian-variety frequency search
summary: Uses the Serbian descriptors suvo, polusuvo and poluslatko for specific wines, confirming ordinary category vocabulary, but does not reproduce the current Serbian residual-sugar thresholds or analyse the four-term ladder. Targeted searches recovered no representative Smederevka or Grašac sweetness-frequency evidence.
notes: The page concerns Georgian wines and cannot establish Serbian market frequencies; the national rulebook supplies the Serbian four-category definition.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Вино and Сладость и сухость напитка
provenance: Required Russian-language target-translation and sweetness-classification corpus
summary: Uses сухое, полусухое, полусладкое and сладкое and explains the analytical dry and medium-dry boundaries, while the companion article stresses that acidity can mask perceived sweetness. It supplies no representative evidence for Serbian Smederevka or Grašac and does not control Serbian label law.
notes: Companion URL: https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A1%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D1%8C_%D0%B8_%D1%81%D1%83%D1%85%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D1%8C_%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%BF%D0%B8%D1%82%D0%BA%D0%B0. Russian classification language is useful for translation, not Serbian frequency.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Predložak:Vinarstvo and targeted sweetness search
provenance: Required Croatian-language neighbouring encyclopedia category-order and Serbian-variety search
summary: The viticulture template lists suho vino, polusuho vino, poluslatko vino and slatko vino in that order under wine sweetness, directly corroborating the neighbouring terminology and sequence. It gives no numerical definitions and no Serbian Smederevka or Grašac frequency evidence.

title: English Wikipedia — Varietal and Classification of wine
provenance: Required English-language encyclopedia varietal-wine and named-variety-label corpus
summary: Defines varietal wine as made primarily, not necessarily exclusively, from a single named grape variety and distinguishes variety for the vine or grape from varietal for the wine. It gives an 85% minimum for a single variety displayed in the EU and states that several displayed varieties must collectively make up 100%, but does not reproduce Serbia's registration, evidence, sensory or denominator conditions.
notes: Companion URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classification_of_wine. Serbian law, not the EU summary, controls the domestic rule.

title: German Wikipedia — Rebsorte and targeted Sortenwein search
provenance: Required German-language encyclopedia grape-variety and Serbian label search
summary: Defines Rebsorte as a variety of cultivated grapevine from whose fruit wine is produced and therefore supplies a direct comparative cultivar concept. Targeted searches found no reliable page defining Serbian sortno vino or reproducing Serbia's single- and multiple-variety label conditions.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Világfajta szőlők and targeted Serbian varietal-wine search
summary: Notes the increasing use of grape-variety names as wine names and discusses internationally distributed grape varieties, providing only broad varietal-label context. It gives no Serbian sortno vino definition, 85% rule or domestic documentary and sensory conditions.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Вранац (грожђе) and targeted sortno vino search

summary: Uses sorta vinove loze and sorta grožđa for a grape cultivar, directly supporting the core meaning of sorta. Targeted searches found no Serbian Wikipedia definition of sortno vino and no passage reproducing the current 85%, registration, evidence, sensory, exclusion or multiple-variety rules.
notes: The current Serbian rulebook supplies the operative meaning and conditions of the label phrase.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Саперави and targeted Serbian varietal-wine search
summary: Calls Saperavi a grape variety and says it is used for both сортовые and купажные wines, supporting the Russian distinction between varietal and blended wine. It neither defines Serbian sortno vino nor supplies the Serbian 85% and associated conditions.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Kujundžuša and Vinova loza
provenance: Required Croatian-language neighbouring cultivar and varietal-wine corpus
summary: Uses sortno vino for wine from Kujundžuša, while the companion vine article uses sorta vinove loze for grape cultivars, corroborating the neighbouring lexical pair. Neither page defines a Serbian percentage threshold or the Serbian no-geographical-origin, evidence and multiple-variety conditions.
notes: Companion URL: https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinova_loza. Croatian usage is comparative only.

title: OURS Vinoteka — Smederevka
provenance: Current Serbian specialist retailer's educational cultivar profile
summary: Says Smederevka most often gives a light dry white wine and separately lists residual sugar as most often dry, directly supporting commonness of the style while stopping short of almost always or a measured market share.

title: Vinarija Čoka — Ždrebac Smederevka 1 l
provenance: Current first-party Serbian winery product declaration
summary: Identifies Ždrebac Smederevka as suvo belo vino made from Smederevka, providing a direct current Serbian dry example.
notes: One producer label establishes existence, not national frequency; the page showed the item out of stock at access.

title: Erdevik Winery — Geronimo
provenance: Current first-party Serbian winery portfolio and technical declaration
summary: Lists Geronimo from Serbia and Fruška Gora as dry white wine from Graschatz/Grašac, with 1.80 g/l residual sugar, providing a direct dry Grašac example.
notes: A single estate wine cannot establish how nearly universal the dry style is.

title: Vino & Fino — Grašac: jedna sorta, a toliko različitih vina!
provenance: Serbian specialist wine-magazine report dated 26 May 2024 from the third Grašac festival
summary: Reports about thirty Grašac producers and stylistic diversity, ending with Fruškogorski Vinogradi's Tri sunca as an exceptionally sweet Grašac whose production is exported. This directly supplies a sweet varietal counterexample but not a frequency denominator.
notes: Festival coverage is broad usage evidence but not a systematic census; the precise regulatory sweetness category of Tri sunca is not stated.

title: Vino & Fino — Tri trofeja za Srbiju na jubilarnom BIWC-u
provenance: Serbian specialist wine-magazine report dated 30 May 2026 on the Balkans International Wine Competition
summary: Identifies Salaš Gnezdo's Serbian Gnezdo Belo 2025, a Grašac and Sauvignon Blanc blend, as the best medium-dry wine category winner. It demonstrates a current non-dry wine containing Grašac, though not a pure Grašac bottling.
notes: Because this is a blend, it limits the broad wording about wines with Grašac but is not a monovarietal counterexample.

title: Luding — Balkanika Smederevka Poluslatko, Vino Kalem
provenance: Current international retailer product record for a Serbian producer
summary: Lists Balkanika Smederevka Poluslatko as a Serbian white semi-sweet still wine from the Smederevka grape and producer Vino Kalem, providing a direct varietal counterexample to an exclusively dry reading.
notes: Retail availability varies and the record is commercial; it proves the product and style, not their market share.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine and specified other wine products
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Articles 22 and 24–26 and Annex 4 Part B
summary: Makes sweetness wording optional for still and related wines and defines suvo at no more than 4 g/l or 9 g/l under the acidity condition, polusuvo above the applicable dry maximum through 12 or conditionally 18 g/l, poluslatko above that maximum through 45 g/l, and slatko above 45 g/l. For one named variety it requires at least 85%, registration for Serbian wine and specified denominator exclusions; several named varieties must collectively be 100% and appear in descending order. For qualifying Serbian wine without geographical origin, Article 25 requires administrative evidence and sensory confirmation and permits the phrase sortno vino after the country and/or variety names.
notes: The 85% threshold means one named variety need not be the only grape; sortno vino is regulated label wording, not a guarantee of 100% monovarietal composition.

title: English Wikipedia — Cuvée
summary: Explains that cuvée derives from cuve and has several wine meanings. On labels it generally denotes a specific blend or batch and is unregulated; in some regions, especially outside France, it specifically means a multi-variety blend, while in Champagne it also names the first 2,050 litres of juice from a marc.
notes: The article directly refutes a universal one-to-one equivalence with mixture of varieties. It does not define Serbian kupaža.

title: German Wikipedia — Cuvée
summary: Distinguishes usages by language: in French a cuvée can be any separately bottled wine, including a blend or a single-site wine, and in Champagne it can mean first-press must; in German-speaking usage Cuvée is commonly a synonym for a blended wine assembled from varieties, sites or separate lots.
notes: The page shows why a locally common synonym cannot be universalised as the French meaning or as the exact Serbian lexical definition.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia — Bor (ital)
summary: Lists cuvée or vegyes bor as wine made from several grape varieties. This corroborates one widespread regional use of cuvée as a varietal blend but supplies neither the broader French meanings nor a definition of Serbian kupaža.
notes: A short classification list is comparative usage evidence, not authority for all cuvée labels.

title: Serbian Wikipedia — Вино and targeted kupaža/cuvée search
provenance: Required Serbian-language encyclopedia wine and exact-term search
summary: Provides a broad Serbian wine context, but targeted searches recovered no reliable Serbian Wikipedia definition of kupaža and no article distinguishing cuvée as batch, selection, blend or Champagne press fraction.
notes: The absence makes specialist Serbian lexicography, current wine usage and international oenological standards necessary for both claims.

title: Russian Wikipedia — Ассамбляж (виноделие)
summary: Defines купажирование as mixing finished wines from the same or different grape varieties and notes its use even for monovarietal wines assembled across vineyards or lots. A companion sparkling-wine article uses кюве for the assembled base wine, but Russian Wikipedia gives no general rule that every cuvée is identical to Serbian kupaža.
notes: Companion URL: https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9F%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B8%D0%B7%D0%B2%D0%BE%D0%B4%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE_%D0%B8%D0%B3%D1%80%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%B2%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B0. Neither page is a Serbian lexical authority.

title: Croatian Wikipedia — Kupaža
summary: States that blending may combine different varieties, different vintages, different sites of the same variety, and different tanks or barrels from the same vintage. It directly demonstrates that the cognate kupaža is broader than mixture of varieties, while offering no definition of cuvée.
notes: Croatian terminology is strong comparative evidence but the Serbian conclusion is also checked against Serbian specialist usage.

title: OIV International Code of Oenological Practices — Blending and mixing or preparation of the cuvee
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine adopted oenological practice II.3.5.3
summary: Defines the operation as blending different wines and calls it blending and mixing or preparation of the cuvee. Its objectives concern the desired analytical, sensory, qualitative, geographical and price characteristics rather than a necessary difference of grape variety.
notes: The OIV standard is conceptual rather than a translation dictionary and therefore does not make the two Serbian/French label words lexically interchangeable in every context.

title: CANU — Leksikon vinogradarstva i vinarstva Crne Gore: Kupaža
provenance: Montenegrin Academy of Sciences and Arts specialist viticulture and winemaking lexicon
summary: Defines kupaža as mixing several wines from the same or different grape varieties and says kuve has a similar, not identical, meaning. It further records cuvée as Champagne first-press must, a sparkling-wine composition, a specific blend, a selection from vats or a blend across vintages.
notes: The lexicon is Montenegrin rather than a Serbian national dictionary, but it directly covers the shared specialist vocabulary and explicitly distinguishes the scopes.

title: Vino.rs — 10 najboljih kupaža Srbije
provenance: Serbian specialist wine article published 11 August 2016
summary: Defines kupaža as the process of joining different varieties, different wines, vintages or even wine styles, then supplies Serbian examples. This is direct living Serbian specialist usage broader than a mere mixture of varieties.
notes: The article is editorial rather than normative and includes evaluative rankings not used for the lexical conclusion.

title: Vinarija Zvonko Bogdan — Cuvée No.1
provenance: Current first-party Serbian winery label and product presentation
summary: Uses Cuvée No.1 as the current name of a Serbian wine, directly confirming that the French word appears in Serbian label and portfolio practice.
notes: The product name proves usage, not a universal lexical equivalence with kupaža or a fixed composition across vintages.

title: English Wikipedia — Oak (wine)
summary: Describes oak barrels as vessels for wine fermentation or aging, identifies 225 litres as the common Bordeaux barrel and 228 litres as the Burgundy style, and stresses that barrel size, age, origin and treatment change the result.
notes: The article supplies the comparative object and cautions against inferring barrel details from a bare aging phrase; it does not translate Serbian odležalo.

title: German Wikipedia — Barrique
summary: Defines a barrique as an oak cask used especially for maturing wine, usually 225 litres in the Bordeaux measure while noting 228-litre Burgundy usage and variation. It separately discusses maturation, newness, toast and repeated use.

notes: Odležalo is the neuter singular past form agreeing with vino; exact container information must come from an accompanying phrase such as u bariku.

title: Vinski vodič — Barik (barrique)

summary: The article places Fruškogorsko vinogorje beneath an old Sremski rejon, Župsko beneath the former Kruševac subregion and Smederevsko beneath the former Belgrade subregion. This supports the broad idea that the three names are below a higher level, but the hierarchy is obsolete relative to the 2015/2024 rules and the article does not establish a formal centre, popularity causation or current label wording.
notes: The local-language encyclopedia cannot override the amended zoning rule or the current packaging and labelling rulebook.

title: Russian Wikipedia review — Фрушка гора, Жупа, Смедерево и географическое происхождение
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia combined B0703 geography and label review
summary: The article broadly distinguishes Serbian wines without GI, regional GI and controlled-origin categories and links Smederevka to Smederevo, but it gives no current rejon/vinogorje list, no Aleksandrovac-centre rule, no comparative name-recognition evidence and no exact current requirement for the recognised designation alongside other label text.
notes: Broad category prose is insufficient to identify the official geographical field on a current Serbian bottle.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — Fruška gora, Župa, Smederevo and Serbian wine regions
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia combined B0703 geography and label search
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia article was found that establishes the current Serbian Srem/Tri Morave/Belgrade nesting, a formal Aleksandrovac centre, comparative fame of popular versus official names, the cause of their usage or the current Serbian GI-label wording.
notes: The negative search result is recorded without treating it as a contradiction of current Serbian law.

title: Vino.rs — Miodrag Mija Radovanović: 30 godina prve moderne privatne srpske vinarije
provenance: 11 November 2020 direct specialist interview with founder Miodrag Mija Radovanović
summary: The introduction calls Podrum Radovanović the first private winery registered in Serbia after Yugoslavia's breakup. Radovanović rejects a literal hundred-year lag, names the lack of old vineyards as a basic deficiency, describes the postwar split between vineyard and cellar work under a quantity-led state model, and dates his own small-cellar start to 1990 and own-label release to 1992.
notes: The 'first' wording is the publication's framing rather than an attached exhaustive registry, and 'lack of old vineyards' is one of several deficiencies discussed rather than a statement that technical ability is irrelevant.

title: Danas — Prošle godine proizvedeno 30 miliona litara: Brz napredak srpskog vinarstva
provenance: 7 September 2022 sector report quoting PKS data and Serbian winery operators
summary: States that 30 million litres were produced in the previous year and that this was the three-year average, while PKS put possible Serbian wine-production capacity at 70 million litres and roughly twice current output. A winery operator says subsidies mainly target small and starting wineries and can cover up to 70% of equipment, which supports an incentive but not easy or durable market entry.
notes: Because the article is dated September 2022, 'previous year' means 2021; its wording does not establish a calendar-2022 production result or an audited inventory of installed capacity.

title: Biznis i finansije — Kvalitet naših vina ne zaostaje za svetskom konkurencijom, ali problem je u količinama
provenance: 15 March 2026 sector feature citing PKS figures and a Serbian oenologist
summary: Repeats an average annual Serbian wine output around 30 million litres and possible capacity around 70 million, while an interviewed oenologist says many small wineries lack their own raw-material base and that consistent quality is difficult without vineyards. It provides current sector context but no winery-level capacity census or national grape-purchase prevalence rate.
notes: The feature postdates the book's 2022 framing and should not be used to retroactively redefine the reference year; 'many' does not prove ubiquitous buying from cooperants.

title: Vino.rs — Vinski bum u Srbiji između privida i stvarnosti
provenance: 3 November 2025 specialist market feature based on PKS/RZS/APR tables and distributor interviews
summary: Reports a rise in registered wineries and attributes part of it to vineyard and equipment subsidies, but interviewees describe financial problems and ownership changes after initial enthusiasm, undermining any simple claim of easy durable entry. It separately reports rising consumer popularity of sparkling wine, which is not the same series as PKS production growth.
notes: The source gives commentary and selected headline series rather than licensing costs, survival cohorts or a complete sparkling-production time series.

title: Euronews Srbija — Vina iz 112 vinarija u Srbiji sa oznakom geografskog porekla
provenance: 4 January 2025 report quoting the Serbian Chamber of Commerce (PKS)
summary: PKS says Serbian sparkling-wine production had grown over the preceding several years, more wineries were choosing the category and quality was increasing, while production remained far behind still wine. No annual sparkling volume or growth-rate series is supplied.
notes: The wording supports the book's attribution but not a quantified trend or a claim that sparkling is already a large share of Serbian output.

title: English Wikipedia review — current Serbian wine industry, Radovanović and sparkling wine
provenance: Required English Wikipedia combined B0705 current-industry and history review
summary: The article gives broad Serbian wine history and an older regional and vineyard overview, but not the Green Book 2025 register figures, the paragraph's mixed-source problem, Radovanović's interview wording, a documented three-part old-vine causal history, the PKS 70/30 estimate, national grape-purchase prevalence, entry-barrier evidence or a current sparkling-production series.
notes: Its broad historical statements cannot substitute for the dated ministry report, direct interview or attributed PKS figures.

title: German Wikipedia review — heutige serbische Weinbranche, Radovanović und Schaumwein

summary: The German article offers general historical and production context but does not contain the 2025 registered-producer and declared-volume definitions, Radovanović's 1990-first claim and old-vine answer, a sourced complete causal chain, the dated PKS capacity comparison, an utilisation measure, national cooperant-purchase prevalence, market-entry metrics or recent sparkling output data.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia search — szerb borászat, Radovanović, kapacitás and pezsgő

summary: The local-language article supplies broad viticulture history and older classifications, but not the Green Book 2025 definitions, the mixed-source error, a documented first-private-winery registry, Radovanović's exact interview answer, the full three-cause claim, current PKS capacity figures, a national purchase or entry study, or recent sparkling-production measurements.
notes: Local-language relevance does not overcome obsolete scope or absent citations for the paragraph's current numbers and causal inferences.

title: Russian Wikipedia review — современная винная отрасль Сербии, Радованович и игристые
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia combined B0705 current-industry and history review
summary: The article provides general history, varieties and quality categories but not the official 2025 register count and declared volume, source comparability, Radovanović's first/1990 status or quoted old-vine diagnosis, the exact multi-period causal chain, PKS possible capacity, utilisation, cooperant-buying prevalence, entry ease or a current sparkling-production trend.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — srpsko vinarstvo, Radovanović, kapacitet and pjenušac
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia combined B0705 current-industry search
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia treatment was found that establishes the 2025 register figures, Radovanović's pioneering role and interview, the paragraph's compound historical causation, the dated PKS capacity ratio, ubiquitous grape purchasing, easy entry or quantified recent sparkling-wine production growth.
notes: The absence is recorded as a coverage finding, not as counterevidence to the non-Wikipedia sources.

title: Pravilnik o rejonizaciji vinogradarskih geografskih proizvodnih područja Srbije — consolidated 2015/2024 text
provenance: Fresh article-by-article audit of the consolidated text citing Službeni glasnik RS 45/2015 and 18/2024
summary: Defines region, rejon, vinogorje, localitet/potes and oases; applies viticultural status up to 800 metres plus listed higher areas; and enumerates three regions, 22 rejon and 77 vinogorje. The current lists use Severno-srednje banatski rejon and Rejon Negotinska Krajina, place Podgorsko vinogorje under Pocersko-Valjevski rejon and retain two Metohija rejon.
notes: This is a public consolidated republication rather than the official publisher interface; the legal identifiers and embedded official-register pages permit checking the 2015 original and 2024 amendment.

title: Vinski Vodič — Rejonizacija vinogradarskih geografskih proizvodnih područja Srbije
provenance: Serbian wine-sector zoning overview reproducing the current hierarchy, altitude rule and complete rejon list
summary: States that Serbia has three regions, 22 rejon and 77 vinogorje and that the rejonized territory includes the country up to 800 metres plus listed higher areas. Its lists independently reproduce seven Vojvodina, 13 Central Serbia and two Kosovo and Metohija rejon with the current names.
notes: It is a secondary specialist overview; disputed details and effective dates are resolved against the legal text.

title: INAO — Cahier des charges Côtes du Rhône Villages, dénomination géographique complémentaire Nyons
provenance: Official INAO proposed specification showing commune-based and intra-appellation geographic delimitation
summary: Defines an appellation geographic area through named communes and a complementary geographic denomination with its own delimited scope. It illustrates why a French commune can be a useful reading aid but is not a universal legal equivalent of Serbian vinogorje: appellation specifications determine whether whole communes, parts or additional denominations apply.
notes: One French appellation specification demonstrates variability rather than establishing a general one-to-one conversion between Serbian and French legal units.

title: Грамота.ру — поиск термина «виногорье»
provenance: Targeted Russian dictionary and usage check for a one-word equivalent of Serbian vinogorje
summary: The targeted check did not yield an authoritative dictionary entry defining a Russian legal equivalent of Serbian vinogorje. Search usage nevertheless includes the direct borrowing «виногорье», so absence of a fully equivalent established term is plausible but the categorical claim that no one-word analogue exists is not lexicographically provable from this corpus.
notes: A negative dictionary search is a corpus limitation, not proof that a word or translation has never been used.

title: Nacionalni program poljoprivrede Srbije 2010–2013
provenance: Serbian national agricultural programme republished from the official legal corpus
summary: Its viticulture baseline gives approximately 135,000 hectares under vineyards in 1955 and describes the long subsequent contraction. This independently supports the historical magnitude but not a like-for-like comparison with the 2025 bearing-vineyard estimate or Vineyard Register area.
notes: Territory and statistical definitions must be retained when comparing the historical programme with present-day ministry and RZS figures.

title: Petrović, Krstić and Stanišić — Analysis of Production Potential and Competitive Position of Serbia on the International Wine Market
provenance: Economics of Agriculture 62(3), 2015, pages 813–829, citing Serbian Statistical Office historical data
summary: Reports that Serbian vineyard area remained above 100,000 hectares during the 1980s before later decline. The article supports the order of magnitude but relies on an older statistical source and does not harmonise those figures with current territorial coverage or register methodology.
notes: The secondary citation should not be turned into an exact continuous series without consulting the underlying RZS tables and definitions.

title: Vinski Vodič — Vinarija Milijan Jelić, Pocersko-Valjevski rejon
provenance: Serbian wine-sector directory entry classified under Pocersko-Valjevski rejon
summary: Places Vinarija Milijan Jelić in the Pocersko-Valjevski rejon and identifies its Valjevo-area location; the regulatory list further nests Podgorsko vinogorje in that rejon. This shows the estate is outside the book map's nine selected rejon, not outside the official vinogorje system.
notes: The producer address identifies the cellar; exact vineyard-parcel coordinates would be needed for a parcel-by-parcel boundary audit.

title: Vino.rs — Najbolje vino Srbije 2017
summary: Names Milijan Jelić as the 2017 Serbian Winery of the Year in the publication's annual selection. It is direct evidence of a high annual distinction, but it is an organiser-specific editorial result rather than a universal national ranking.
notes: The result concerns the winery category and should not be presented as a top-three bottle placement.

title: Vino.rs — Najbolje vino Srbije 2018
summary: Ranks Milijan Jelić Kameničanka 2013 third in the local and new-variety red-wine category. This is a documented top-three result in a named category, not third place among every Serbian wine released that year.
notes: Category, vintage and organiser are essential qualifiers.

title: Vino.rs — Najbolja vina Srbije 2023
summary: Places Morange 2018 first in the orange-wine category, Kameničanka 2019 third among local-variety reds and Vinarija Milijan Jelić third in the winery selection. It confirms multiple high results in 2023 while also showing that bottle and winery categories are distinct.
notes: Together with 2017 and 2018 this supports repeated appearances, but the publication does not define the book's frequency word «regularly».

title: European Commission — Kosovo Report 2024
provenance: European Commission enlargement report describing Kosovo institutions, government, municipalities and legal implementation
summary: Discusses the Government of Kosovo, Kosovo institutions, mayors and application of Kosovo law as the operating governance framework. It supports the de facto institutional-control statement but does not resolve recognition or sovereignty, which the EU document explicitly treats under a status-neutral framework where required.
notes: The report's reference year is 2024; it should be paired with a source on the continuing UN framework and Serbia's non-recognition rather than used as a sovereignty ruling.

title: UNMIK — Mandate
provenance: Official United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo mandate page
summary: States that UNMIK was established by UN Security Council Resolution 1244 and that its current objectives include promoting security, stability and respect for human rights in Kosovo. The continuing mandate qualifies any simple description of an uncontested national administration.
notes: A continuing UN mission does not mean UNMIK performs all day-to-day government functions; de facto local institutions must be described separately.

title: Idealno.rs — Stone Castle Cuvee crveno vino 0,75 l
provenance: Current Serbian price-comparison product page and offer history
summary: Shows no current offers for the indexed Stone Castle wine and reports its last availability on 30 November 2017. This supports low visibility for one producer and SKU in indexed Serbian e-commerce, not a census of all Belgrade retail, restaurants or direct imports.
notes: Price aggregators can miss merchants and offline channels, and one product cannot represent every wine from the two Metohija rejon.

title: Al Jazeera Balkans — Kosovsko vino uskoro na tržištu Srbije
provenance: 25 April 2015 report on planned Stone Castle entry into the Serbian market
summary: Documents a concrete effort to place Kosovo-produced Stone Castle wine on the Serbian market in 2015. It establishes historical market interest and makes an absolute timeless absence claim untenable, but it does not measure current Belgrade availability.
notes: The article predates the current audit by more than a decade and is used only as historical context.

title: English Wikipedia review — Serbian wine zoning, vineyard area and regional lists
provenance: Required English Wikipedia combined B0706–B0713 wine-geography review
summary: The article provides broad wine history and older area figures and identifies important places such as Fruška Gora and Župa, but its regional material is based on obsolete schemes and it does not reproduce the consolidated 2015/2024 hierarchy, 77 vinogorje, the 800-metre effective date, Green Book definitions, the book-map count, Milijan Jelić placements or the current exact rejon names.
notes: Current counts, names and nesting are resolved from the Serbian regulation; encyclopedia gaps neither prove nor disprove retailer availability or a lexical absolute.

notes: Older aggregate areas are not comparable with current ministry series without matching territorial and statistical definitions.

notes: The negative result is recorded as a corpus gap and does not count as counterevidence to Serbian legal and primary sources.

It also does not establish that Russian lacks every one-word rendering of vinogorje.

title: Croatian Wikipedia search — srpska vinska rejonizacija, vinogorje and vineyard area
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia combined B0706–B0713 wine-geography search
summary: No Croatian Wikipedia article was found that gives the current Serbian three/22/77 scheme, units below vinogorje, effective altitude-rule date, dual 2025 area measures, book-map comparison, Milijan Jelić location and annual results, or complete present-day rejon names for the three regions.
notes: The search gap is not evidence against the current Serbian regulation or specialist ranking pages.

title: English Wikipedia review — Kosovo governance, disputed status and wine-market evidence
provenance: Required English Wikipedia combined B0713 governance and market review
summary: Describes Kosovo as a partially recognised state with its own governing institutions and Serbia's claim and non-recognition, supporting the need to separate de facto governance from disputed status. It contains no inventory of Kosovo wines in Belgrade retail, restaurants or imports and cannot establish near-absence from that market.
notes: The status summary is secondary and paired with EU and UN primary institutional sources; market silence is not proof of absence.

title: German Wikipedia review — Kosovo-Verwaltung, Statusstreit und Weinmarkt
provenance: Required German Wikipedia combined B0713 governance and market review
summary: Explains Kosovo's institutions, declaration of independence, partial recognition and Serbia's contrary position, broadly corroborating the de facto/legal-status distinction. It gives no current evidence on availability of Metohija wines in the Belgrade market.
notes: National-language framing varies across encyclopedia editions, so neutral wording relies on the common factual intersection and primary institutional documents.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia review — Koszovó intézményei, vitatott státusza and wine-market gap
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia combined B0713 governance and market review
summary: Provides general context on Kosovo's own institutions, contested independence and recognition. It does not document the range, sales or absence of Kosovo and Metohija wines in Belgrade channels.
notes: The article is used only as an encyclopedia cross-check, not as a market census or final authority on sovereignty.

title: Serbian Wikipedia review — Косово и Метохија, фактичка управа и тржиште вина
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language combined B0713 governance and market review
summary: Presents Kosovo and Metohija through Serbia's constitutional and non-recognition position while also describing post-1999 institutions and international presence. Its framing reinforces the need for explicit attribution and neutrality; it provides no comprehensive evidence on current Belgrade availability of wines from the territory.
notes: The national framing is not treated as a standalone resolution of status, and lack of retail discussion is not evidence of no sales.

title: Russian Wikipedia review — Республика Косово, фактическое управление и рынок вина

summary: Describes the Republic of Kosovo, its institutions, partial recognition, Serbia's non-recognition and the continuing dispute. It does not supply retailer, restaurant, distributor or import data for wines on the Belgrade market.
notes: The common de facto-control facts are separated from the article's legal and geopolitical wording; market absence remains unproven by encyclopedia coverage.

title: Croatian Wikipedia review — Kosovo, stvarna uprava, sporni status and wine market
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia combined B0713 governance and market review
summary: Provides general context on Kosovo's institutions, independence, recognition and Serbia's position, supporting a qualified de facto-governance formulation. It offers no evidence for the near-absence of Kosovo wines across the current Belgrade market.
notes: Cross-language agreement supports the factual distinction, while primary EU and UN sources anchor current institutional wording.

title: Терруары Сербии — опубликованный раздел источников и внутренняя разметка ссылок
provenance: Direct inspection of the audited book, its endnotes and all .srcref href targets
summary: The source section says the book was finished in July and all online sources were accessed on 6 August, while S10 records 9 August. All in-text source links target the common #istochniki fragment; endnote numbering jumps S8 to S10, and several later notes besides S8 print no web address.
notes: Browser Back normally restores the prior history position, but there are no per-note anchors; the record audits internal consistency rather than supplying external factual corroboration.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on recognition of designations for still wines
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 121/2012, 102/2014, 78/2015, 94/2017, 48/2022 and 18/2024, Article 13
summary: Recognises K.P.K. and K.G.P.K. for the same controlled geographical designation and lists alternative sensory minima of 59/100 or 15/20 for G.I. and 79/100 or 16.5/20 for controlled origin, with annual category tied to control results.
notes: The consolidated host is not the official Gazette; related current sensory rules show why the 100-point values should be stated alongside the retained 20-point alternatives.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on packaging, declaration and labelling of still wine and specified products
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 55/2023 and 18/2024, Articles 23, 24 and 30
summary: Sets the 85% conditions for one named variety, a vintage and a qualifying smaller geographical unit and requires several named varieties to constitute 100% collectively, subject to specified evidence, denominator exclusions and exceptions.
notes: The endnote is a fair shorthand but not a complete substitute for the operative conditions in each article.

title: Ministry of Agriculture of Serbia — Green Book 2025, Book II
summary: Reports 17.4 thousand hectares of bearing vineyards in the broad series, roughly 6.9 thousand hectares in the predominantly commercial Vineyard Register, 521 market-oriented Winery Register producers, 27.2 million litres declared and the variety-area order. It gives 91% non-GI, 4% G.I. and 5% combined K.P.K./K.G.P.K. volume and a separate 2024 producer-series value of 504.
notes: The area populations differ, and the 9% figure is a declared production-volume share rather than a share of wineries, labels or retail sales.

title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Negotinske Pivnice, Tentative List 5537
provenance: Tentative List submission by the Permanent Delegation of Serbia, submitted 15 April 2010
summary: Dates documentary evidence of the wine-cellar settlements to the mid-nineteenth century and the mainly surviving buildings to the second half of the nineteenth and first half of the twentieth century.
notes: Tentative-list inscription is not inscription on the World Heritage List, and UNESCO notes that the nominating state is responsible for the submitted content.

title: VIVC passport 8899 — Pamid
provenance: Vitis International Variety Catalogue, Julius Kühn-Institut
summary: The canonical Pamid passport includes Crvena Slankamenka and Drenak in its published synonym tradition, establishing the narrow catalogue statement while leaving local-name homonymy possible.
notes: Automated retrieval is restricted; passport number and synonymy are cross-checked against catalogue-derived records and peer-reviewed Serbian germplasm research.

title: Tello et al. — Genetic characterization of grapevines prospected in old Serbian vineyards
summary: Identifies Parmak Cerven among the sampled old Serbian vines and maps Drenak to Parmak Cerven in the discussion, demonstrating that Drenak usage is not unique to catalogue Pamid synonymy.
notes: The main article does not fully expose the exact accession-level field label for the single Parmak Cerven sample; that detail should be tied to supplementary data if quoted literally.

title: van Leeuwen et al. — Recent advancements in understanding the terroir effect on aromas in grapes and wines
summary: Reviews climate, soil and plant interactions and treats soil effects chiefly through water availability, nitrogen status and rooting-related vine response rather than direct transmission of a soil type into a wine aroma.
notes: The endnote's separate soil thermal-balance phrase is not a central mechanism developed in this specific cited review and needs a separate source if retained.

title: Peter Dry / AWRI — Terroir: it’s the rocks that matter
provenance: Australian Wine Research Institute technical conference presentation
summary: Distinguishes geology, vine mineral nutrition and sensory minerality, says most rock minerals are tasteless or insoluble at relevant levels and rejects a literal rock-to-glass taste pathway.
notes: A presentation rather than a peer-reviewed experiment; it supports the conceptual correction and should be cited by author and title, not only by domain.

title: University of California IPM — Grape Phylloxera
provenance: University of California Statewide Integrated Pest Management Program
summary: States that grape phylloxera prefers heavy clay soils and is not a pest on sandy soils, providing a citable agronomic formulation for strong practical suppression.
notes: The practical phrase does not prove biological impossibility in every sandy profile or establish the rootstock status of a particular Serbian vineyard.

title: Tasmania NRE — Import Risk Analysis: Grape Phylloxera
summary: Describes sandy soils as less conducive to phylloxera and associated with slow population growth rather than absolute immunity, qualifying the stronger practical shorthand in extension guides.
notes: This source also demonstrates that stable online technical references are available for the endnote.

title: DWWA 2026 official results API — Serbia
provenance: Official country-filter endpoint; book records a 9 August 2026 snapshot
summary: The dated snapshot contains 146 Serbian medal records: 3 Platinum, 7 Gold, 58 Silver and 78 Bronze.
notes: Live result sets can change, so the query date must remain attached to the count.

title: AgroFin / PKS — Serbian wines won 149 DWWA 2026 medals
provenance: Report reproducing the Serbian Chamber of Commerce statement of 21 June 2026
summary: Reports 149 medals: 3 Platinum, 7 Gold, 60 Silver and 79 Bronze and names the three Platinum wines.
notes: The three-record difference from the later API snapshot is unresolved in the public sources.

title: Decanter — DWWA 2026 Platinum winners: Serbia
summary: Lists Matalj Kremen Kamen, Aleksandrović Kameničarka Prokupac and Deurić La Rem Chardonnay as Serbia's three 97-point Platinum winners.
notes: The list resolves the Platinum names but not the 146-versus-149 total-medal discrepancy.

title: Decanter — DWWA 2020 results announced
summary: Says Serbia received its first Platinum medal since the 2014 competition, directly preserving continuity with a prior top-tier Serbian result rather than describing 2020 as unqualified first-ever success.
notes: The formulation reflects Decanter's own handling of the award-system name change.

title: Decanter — DWWA 2014 Central and Eastern European Red Regional Trophy
summary: Records Janko Zavet Stari 2011 from Serbia as the 2014 Regional Trophy winner, the earlier highest-tier result referenced by Decanter in 2020.
notes: The 2014 award was called Regional Trophy, so it should not be silently renamed Platinum; the taxonomy change must be explained.

title: CEVVIN — Autohtone i regionalne sorte vinove loze Srbije
summary: Provides the publication identity and inventory tables: Kadarka 11.60 ha; Kreaca 31.69 ha on 37 parcels; Marselan 20.21 ha on 24 parcels. The following Župski Bojadiser row contains 40 parcels.
notes: The table is a 2019 publication-era commercial-vineyard inventory and should not be labelled a current 2026 census.

title: National Library of Serbia — CIP bibliographic record for Autohtone i regionalne sorte vinove loze Srbije
summary: Confirms the title, authorship/editorial record, Niš publication context, 2019 date and ISBN 978-86-912489-1-8.
notes: The catalogue validates publication identity but not every numerical table or the underlying register observation date.

title: Darko Jakšić, ed. — Sorta vinove loze Bagrina
summary: Catalogues the 164-page Bagrina monograph; the cited research section describes 21 2022 microvinifications and sensory work involving CREA-VE Asti.
notes: Exact pages and blinding protocol require direct inspection of the monograph rather than inference from the catalogue landing page.

title: Vino.rs — Bagrina kakvu nismo poznavali
provenance: On-site report from the 2023 Bagrina project conclusion and tasting
summary: Reports inspection of 13,110 vines, selection of 21 plants or genotypes, microvinifications and CREA-VE involvement, with wide sensory and acidity variation.
notes: The journalistic account does not independently demonstrate a blind protocol or the monograph's exact page span.

title: RHMZ Serbia — Negotin station climate normals
provenance: Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia official station page
summary: Gives 2109.2 sunshine hours and 87 clear days for 1981–2010 and 2035.9 hours and 77.0 clear days for 1961–1990.
notes: The page does not define or report the promotional claim of 265 sunny days, so that number is not a comparable official normal.

title: Vino.rs — Manastir Bukovo: S verom u vino
provenance: Independent Serbian wine reportage based on a visit and interviews
summary: Dates Bukovo's modern Crna Tamjanika revival planting to 2009 and describes the certified planting material associated with Negotin, supporting an external source for that planting and a conservation role.

summary: The Velika Drenova nursery says it maintains a Crna Tamjanika mother planting and presents it as unique in Serbia.

provenance: 4 January 2025 report attributing sector figures to PKS
summary: States that the dated 2024 snapshot had 497 registered market wine producers, 112 with geographical-origin designations covering 450 wines.

title: Danas — Prošle godine proizvedeno 30 miliona litara: Brz napredak srpskog vinarstva
summary: Attributes a possible production capacity of 70 million litres to PKS and says about 30 million litres were produced in the previous year and as the three-year average.

title: Public Serbian wine-sector annual-turnover calculation search
provenance: Targeted review of ministry, statistics, chamber and business materials for annual wine-sector turnover methodology
summary: No authoritative open calculation was recovered that defines the sector population, period and price basis and supplies reproducible arithmetic for annual Serbian wine-industry turnover.
