title: Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans — Albedo of a water surface
provenance: Peer-reviewed aircraft, mast and ship irradiance measurements
summary: Shows dependence of water-surface albedo on solar altitude, spectrum, atmospheric transmittance, cloud and wind, supporting low high-Sun values and strong low-Sun increase while rejecting a universal constant.
notes: The study contains no site-specific Danube vineyard slope radiometry or universal reflected-ray direction claim.

title: Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans — Observation and Parameterization of Broadband Sea Surface Albedo
summary: Finds little clear-sky high-Sun variation but strong albedo growth at large solar zenith angles, with cloud, wind, waves and water vapour affecting the relationship.
notes: Sea-surface observations establish general physics, not the irradiance received by a particular freshwater-river vineyard.

title: NOAA NESDIS — Sunglint
summary: Explains that sunglint is specular reflection received when source, surface and receiver angles align, so the strong direction changes with geometry and surface orientation rather than always pointing sideways or away from a slope.
notes: The explainer establishes geometry but does not quantify vineyard-canopy photosynthetically active radiation.

title: Effects of an Inter-Row Reflective Ground Film on grape berry development and composition
provenance: Controlled vineyard reflective-ground-film field study, Horticulturae 11(9), 2025
summary: Places reflective film on the vineyard ground in the inter-row zone and measures changes in canopy light and berry ripening or composition, confirming the endnote's description of the experimental configuration.
notes: A close, deliberately reflective material is not a quantitative analogue for a distant water surface; the study cannot resolve the Danube mechanism without local geometry and radiometry.

title: English Wikipedia combined review — Serbian wine, Pamid, phylloxera, albedo and source-note claims
provenance: Required English Wikipedia combined B0714–B0751 review
summary: Provides broad Serbian-wine, Pamid, phylloxera and albedo context through the main and companion articles, but does not document this book's dates or anchors, exact 2023/2024 Serbian rules and 2025 register definitions, full endnote bibliographies, DWWA snapshot conflict and award-taxonomy history, CEVVIN table rows, Bagrina panel protocol, Negotin station normals, Bukovo propagation chain, sector-turnover search or site-specific Danube radiometry.

summary: Supplies older Serbian-wine context and a Pamid synonym list including Crvena Slankamenka and Drenak, plus general Reblaus and Albedo physics. It lacks the book's internal chronology/navigation, current Serbian legal percentages and scoring details, 2025 statistical populations, exact source metadata and inventory rows, DWWA dated conflict and historical taxonomy, Bagrina method, official Negotin normals, Bukovo source chain, reproducible turnover evidence and a Danube-vineyard light model.

title: Negotinske Pivnice — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
provenance: Tentative List submission by the Permanent Delegation of Serbia, reference 5537
summary: Records submission on 15 April 2010 and explicitly identifies the property as a Serbian Tentative List entry. It says reliable initial construction dates are unavailable, gives second-half nineteenth to first-half twentieth-century ranges and reports different present building, cellar, distillery and use counts for Rajac, Rogljevo and Štubik.
notes: UNESCO states that Tentative List content remains the State Party's responsibility; the entry is not an inscription on the World Heritage List and its inventories must be date- and unit-qualified.

title: Participatory Urban Design for Touristic Presentation of Cultural Heritage Sites: The Case of Negotinske Pivnice
summary: Provides an independent cultural-heritage inventory and, for Rajac, reports 169 buildings, 166 cellars and three distilleries, demonstrating that counts depend on the unit and survey framing and do not map one-to-one onto the UNESCO dossier's building/cellar totals.
notes: The paper does not turn one inventory into a timeless total; figures should retain location, date and counted-object definition.

title: Ministry of Agriculture of Serbia — Green Book 2025, Book II
provenance: Official 2025 annual report, Book II, printed pages 37–40 and associated charts
summary: Supplies 2025 Vineyard and Winery Register measures, cultivar and colour shares, 521 market-oriented producers and 27.2 million litres of declared production, while also printing multi-year producer and area series. It separately identifies broad bearing-vineyard area and predominantly commercial registered area, proving why unlike denominators must not be mixed but also disproving the claimed uniqueness of one comparable year.
notes: Every reuse must name the register or statistical series and preserve whether the measure is area, producer count or declared production volume.

title: CEVVIN — Autohtone i regionalne sorte vinove loze Srbije
summary: The title and author pages identify Darko Jakšić, Ivan Bradić, Milan Beader, Radoslav Milić and Miloš Ristić and the Niš 2019 edition. Cultivar chapters provide planted-area ranks and distributions by altitude, exposition and slope, and the full PDF is openly downloadable.
notes: The figures are tied to the publication's commercial-vineyard inventory rather than a live 2026 register; page and chart citations remain necessary.

title: National Library of Serbia — CIP record for Autohtone i regionalne sorte vinove loze Srbije
summary: Independently confirms the title, five-author record, Niš publication context, 2019 date and ISBN 978-86-912489-1-8.
notes: The catalogue validates identity and authorship, not the underlying vineyard census or every table.

title: Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia — Vinski atlas
summary: The official edition identifies the Vinski atlas author team as Darko Jakšić, Dragoslav Ivanišević, Marina Brbaklić Tepavac and Violeta Đokić, not the five authors of CEVVIN's 2019 cultivar book.
notes: The PDF is large but publicly downloadable from RZS; an official PDF is preferable to an unattributed Issuu copy.

title: Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia — Vinogradarski atlas
summary: The official edition identifies Dragoslav Ivanišević, Darko Jakšić and Nada Korać as the Vinogradarski atlas authors, a third and different author group.
notes: The bibliographic identity directly contradicts 'the same authors' and supplies an authorised full-text route outside Issuu.

title: Targeted search for authorised full Issuu editions of both Serbian atlases
provenance: Exact-title, author and site:issuu.com searches for Vinski atlas and Vinogradarski atlas
summary: No direct official Issuu URL establishing complete authorised versions of both works was recovered, while official RZS PDFs were available.
notes: This bounded negative result does not prove that no Issuu upload exists; it shows that the book's access claim is uncitable as written.

title: Wine Style — Uopšteno o W.S.
provenance: Magazine's official history and publication-frequency page
summary: States that Wine Style has appeared five times a year beginning in October 2006.
notes: The current site footer and archive corroborate continuity; this page does not by itself prove that every tasting used one invariant template.

title: Wine Style — Degustacije archive
provenance: Magazine's official public tasting archive and retrieved Kovačević/Cilić entries
summary: Retrieved tasting entries identify wine, vintage, variety, area, producer and alcohol and then describe colour, nose and palate, confirming a recurring structured presentation for the named examples.
notes: The geographic field is an editorial area/origin label unless separately checked against the Serbian legal zoning hierarchy.

title: Wine Style — Vinarija Temet: Anatomija srpskih vinarija
summary: Identifies Temet in the Anatomy series and preserves Broj 74 and author Aleksandar Duković along with structured wine entries, showing that exact issue and author metadata exist externally even though the audited book does not map every borrowed description to them.
notes: The page supports the magazine example and exposes the book's claim-to-source mapping gap rather than a universal metadata gap at Wine Style.

title: Терруары Сербии — source section, warning popovers and internal provenance audit
provenance: Direct inspection of the audited publication, links, map markup and all local unverified-warning identifiers
summary: The publication names source families but does not retain a unique Wine Style article for every tasting, exact Telegram/vc posts for the five scene observations, a per-price seller/date ledger, map input dataset or a per-logistics verification ledger. Repository inspection finds only four dedicated unverified-warning popovers, and the map/card system represents nine rejons. B0779 says no country-filtered DWWA result is open although S10 elsewhere cites the official API.
notes: This record audits internal completeness and consistency; it is not external corroboration of prices, taste, map coordinate origins or source credentials.

title: Wine Style — Antologija srpskih vinarija
summary: Describes a Serbian-English publication of more than 250 pages and promotes it as the most complete and accurate overview; currently lists 2,400 dinars and sales through Delfi, Laguna, Vulkan and wine outlets.
notes: The completeness superlative is publisher advertising, not an independent comparative finding; price and outlets are date-sensitive.

title: Wine Style — 3D FlipBook catalogue
provenance: Publisher's public flipbook index listing Antologija srpskih vinarija
summary: Lists a dedicated Antologija srpskih vinarija flipbook entry on the public site, so an absolute claim of no free access requires an actual dated page-count and viewer test.
notes: The crawler did not establish that every book page is readable; existence of a viewer shell is not proof of complete lawful free access.

title: Wine Style — Antologija srpskih vinarija: Virtus
provenance: Official excerpt, issue 76, by Aleksandar Duković and Vuk Tripković
summary: Explicitly says it reproduces the Virtus text from Antologija srpskih vinarija and supplies both authors, directly confirming that individual chapters are openly published online.
notes: One excerpt proves partial access, not completeness of the flipbook or of the book's winery coverage.

title: Сербия и вино — @serbianwine
provenance: Public channel address named in the book
summary: Establishes the named channel and handle but, without exact post URLs and dates, does not identify the sources of the five observations or independently verify the author's full professional biography.
notes: Channel existence is not evidence that every attributed observation appears there or that the unnamed vc.ru author is the same person.

title: Search for the cited Nadezhda vc.ru Serbian wine guide and exact observations
provenance: Exact-name, domain and quoted-term searches across vc.ru and the public web
summary: No unambiguous guide URL, author identity or passage set was recovered for sparkling Tamjanika, spritzer, Dragojlović, price points and the phrase župski prokupac.
notes: This is a bounded discovery failure, not proof that the guide or posts never existed; the remedy is direct citation metadata.

title: Serbia — Law on Organic Production
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 109/2025, applicable from 1 June 2026
summary: Reserves organic terms for compliant production and establishes control, certification and labelling obligations, illustrating why a producer's informal claim is not equivalent to current certification evidence.
notes: A winery-level audit still requires the actual valid certificate, scope, control body and date rather than inference from the general law.

title: CEVVIN — Kreaca cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking public cultivar profile
summary: Provides an open agronomic and wine profile for Kreaca, including late ripening, lower sugar accumulation, neutral berry taste and a harmonious drinkable wine characterization, directly refuting the absolute absence of open descriptions.
notes: The profile is institutional and useful but not an independent multi-vintage sensory panel; the book may still accurately note a scarcity of modern independent tastings if it defines that narrower corpus.

title: Vino.rs — Bagrina kakvu nismo poznavali
provenance: Report from the CEVVIN Bagrina project conclusion and tasting
summary: Reports inspection of 13,110 vines, selection of 21 plants/genotypes, microvinifications, CREA-VE involvement and wide sensory/acidity variation, supplying public Bagrina evidence beyond a Matalj product page even though the monograph remains central.
notes: The journalistic account is not a substitute for full monograph tables and does not by itself prove a blind panel.

title: Терруары Сербии — audit of price and visit-source traceability
provenance: Direct inventory of all price, opening, visit and location statements against the published source apparatus
summary: The publication does not expose a row-level 2025 retail dataset with seller, date, bottle size and archived listing, nor a dated verification ledger for every visit and opening statement. This prevents reproduction of both the claimed price collection and the universal location-only editorial convention.
notes: Absence from the published corpus does not prove that private working notes never existed; it means readers and auditors cannot verify the process.

title: Search for authoritative open Serbian wine-area boundary polygons
provenance: Targeted Serbian and English searches of zoning publications, open-data and GIS terms for rejon/vinogorje shapefiles
summary: The search recovered textual rules, static official maps and project mapping but no authoritative openly downloadable national polygon layer for all current wine rejons and vinogorje.
notes: This bounded result cannot exclude a non-indexed ministry, cadastre or project GIS; the book should say only that none was found in the stated search.

title: Pravilnik o rejonizaciji vinogradarskih geografskih proizvodnih područja Srbije — consolidated 2015/2024 text
provenance: Consolidated reproduction citing Official Gazette RS 45/2015 and 18/2024
summary: Defines and enumerates the current three regions, 22 rejons and 77 vinogorje and describes territorial units in legal text and maps. It establishes the current denominator and legal hierarchy but does not furnish the book with a documented open polygon dataset.
notes: This is a public consolidated republication rather than the official Gazette interface; legal identifiers should remain attached.

title: Serbia — current packaging, declaration and labelling rule for still wine and specified products
provenance: Official Serbian Legal Information System consolidated act record
summary: The current act's final provisions identify superseded earlier wine-quality and labelling instruments, allowing the old Pravilnik o kvalitetu i drugim zahtevima za vino to be distinguished from the 2012 designation-recognition rule.
notes: The official interface requires JavaScript; title, act identity and repeal context were cross-checked with the public consolidated text.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on recognition of designations for still wines
provenance: Consolidated reproduction of Official Gazette RS 121/2012, 102/2014, 78/2015, 94/2017, 48/2022 and 18/2024
summary: Shows that the 121/2012 and 102/2014 citation sequence belongs to the rule on conditions and procedures for recognising designations for still wines, not to Pravilnik o kvalitetu i drugim zahtevima za vino.
notes: The full amendment sequence and exact title should replace the book's conflated citation.

title: Serbia — Rulebook on the appearance, content and display of the registration mark for wine with geographical origin
summary: Identifies the evidenciona markica instrument as a separate rulebook published in Official Gazette RS 67/2010 and specifies its scope and mark design.

title: Vino.rs — Svet vina / Serbian wine-region overview
summary: Repeats the three-region, 22-rejon and 77-vinogorje scheme and attributes the developed presentation to the 2015 Vinski atlas, not to an identified 2013–2014 SERSA or Vinopedia edition.

notes: The overview does not itself expose every Serbian medal row; the official API supplies the country-filtered dataset.

title: DWWA 2026 official results API — Serbia

title: Терруары Сербии — тематическая библиография, палитра почв и дата редакции
provenance: Direct inspection of B0781–B0785, CSS custom properties and source-note dates in the audited repository
summary: B0781 lists source families without article-level metadata. The base palette contains eleven hex colours; standard sRGB D65 to CIELAB plus CIEDE2000 yields the smallest pair as Chernozem #403B32 versus Crnica #1C2023 at about 12.2800, while Sand versus Loess is about 13.3926. The title says July 2026 although the source section records 6 and 9 August checks.
notes: The computed result concerns the published base palette; dark-theme overrides and viewing conditions require separate reporting. This record audits internal state rather than external soil colours.

title: Poljoprivredni fakultet Novi Sad — Voćarstvo i vinogradarstvo
provenance: Official University of Novi Sad Faculty of Agriculture department history
summary: States that the Sremski Karlovci institute and Novi Sad Faculty of Agriculture were integrated in 1972 and that the institute became a faculty organisational unit, clarifying the historical rather than current standalone institutional label.
notes: The book still needs the actual author, title, date and issuing organisational unit for every institute-derived claim.

title: CIE — ISO/CIE 11664-6:2022 CIEDE2000 Colour-Difference Formula
provenance: International Commission on Illumination official standard page
summary: Defines CIEDE2000 as an extension of CIELAB intended to improve correlation between numerical values and the relative perceived size of colour differences, and makes clear that colour spaces and viewing/reference conditions matter.
notes: The full normative formula is a seven-page standard; the audit calculation uses standard sRGB D65 conversion and default weighting factors.

title: Frontiers — Soil and climate risk mapping for grape phylloxera
provenance: Peer-reviewed open-access review and risk model
summary: Reviews the association of phylloxera with lower sand fractions and its rarity in very sandy soils while retaining temperature, moisture and experimental caveats, supporting reduced suitability rather than universal immunity.
notes: A soil called sandy without measured particle-size distribution is insufficient to infer practical absence of the pest.

title: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources — Grapes: soils, berry size and irrigation
summary: Explains how soil depth, texture, root zone, irrigation and fertility jointly govern vine water status, berry size and vegetative growth; excessive water can promote canopy growth, but no single soil name fixes wine style.
notes: General grape guidance, not a controlled Serbian sand, loess, Chernozem or Prokupac trial.

title: Atmosphere — Vojvodina loess coverage
provenance: Peer-reviewed regional study citing Serbian loess literature
summary: Reports that loess and loess-like sediments cover more than 60% of Vojvodina, a large majority but not a demonstrated ‘almost all’ of the province.
notes: The percentage joins loess with loess-like material and therefore needs that denominator wording retained.

title: Scientific Reports — Provenance of late Pleistocene loess in central and eastern Europe
summary: Finds mixed local and regional Danube/Carpathian-basin sources and predominantly western glacial-period winds, contradicting a simple equation of loess transport with the modern Košava airflow.
notes: A modern named wind cannot be projected across multiple Pleistocene depositional phases without dedicated atmospheric evidence.

title: FAO — Lecture notes on the major soils of the world: Chernozems
provenance: Food and Agriculture Organization world-soil reference
summary: Describes Chernozems as dark, humus-rich, well-structured, moisture-holding and naturally fertile soils, supporting the definition but not a universal negative vineyard outcome or an erosion requirement.
notes: Natural reference profiles may contain more organic matter than cultivated Serbian sites.

title: IVES — Effect of vigour and cluster number on wine parameters
provenance: Field study of vigour, crop load and grape/wine responses
summary: Shows that vigour and cluster number matter but sugar, anthocyanin and tannin responses vary by season and treatment; it does not support a universal ‘fertile or unthinned soil equals empty, loose or simple wine’ rule.
notes: Not a Serbian soil-type experiment; used for the general management mechanism and its limits.

title: Contribution to the knowledge of soils formed on limestone on Ozren Mountain
summary: Measures limestone Calcomelanosol with high humus, fine-earth water-holding capacity, porosity and permeability while retaining the importance of shallow profile and skeletal setting.
notes: Ozren forest and meadow profiles do not establish wine texture or the effect of crop thinning in Banat vineyards.

title: Spektrum Lexikon der Geowissenschaften — Pararendzina
summary: Defines Pararendzina on loose carbonate-rich parent material including marl, supporting the soil-parent link while not imposing one fixed temperature, moisture or pH profile on every site.
notes: Marl composition remains a continuum and must be measured for a particular vineyard.

title: IVES — Soil temperature, water and nitrogen effects on vine development
summary: Demonstrates that soil temperature, water and nitrogen affect vine phenology and ripening but vary within soil groups; a parent-material or taxonomic label alone does not determine warming or harvest timing.
notes: Bordeaux evidence for general mechanism, not direct Serbian marl or Vertisol measurements.

title: USGS — Carbonate-rock aquifers and fractured limestone
provenance: United States Geological Survey hydrology overview
summary: Documents the wide range from dense low-transmission carbonate rock to dissolution-enlarged connected fractures that store and transmit substantial water, with overlying regolith also controlling flow.
notes: Aquifer-scale evidence supplies the physical mechanism; vine-root-zone storage still requires site measurements.

title: IVES — Radiative and thermal effects on fruit ripening induced by soil colour
provenance: Vineyard experiment with contrasting surface-cover colours
summary: Shows that white, red and dark surface materials change reflected radiation, fruit-zone microclimate and grape response; colour and material properties, not the words limestone or stone alone, determine the effect.
notes: White pumice in the experiment is not Serbian limestone and does not justify the phrase ‘reflects heat’.

title: FAO AGRIS — granite-gneiss parent material and soil variability
provenance: Peer-reviewed soil toposequence study indexed by FAO AGRIS
summary: Finds deep to very deep granite-gneiss-derived profiles ranging from well to somewhat poorly drained and pH 5.8–8.9, directly demonstrating that crystalline parent rocks do not imply one shallow acidic fast-draining soil.
notes: The non-Serbian setting establishes possible range, not local frequency; a Serbian map is still needed for ‘usually’.

title: FAO — Major soils of the world: Cambisols
summary: Describes many Cambisols as medium-textured, structurally stable, porous and well drained while explicitly recognising numerous exceptions, and therefore supports only a qualified ‘balanced profile’ shorthand.
notes: It does not make Serbian gajnjača exactly synonymous with one WRB unit or Russian brown forest soil.

title: IUSS WRB 2022 — Vertisol and vertic diagnostics
provenance: Official World Reference Base for Soil Resources, fourth edition with correction
summary: Defines Vertisols through abundant shrink-swell clay, wide cracks, wedge aggregates and slickensides, supporting the core smonica description but not an automatic ripening delay or tannin outcome.
notes: A vernacular smonica label still needs an actual profile diagnosis for exact WRB classification.

title: University of California ANR — Grapes: soil depth, drainage and root restriction
summary: Explains deep grape rooting potential while identifying hardpan, stratified layers and rock as restrictions; rootable depth is a whole-profile property rather than a direct consequence of visible gravel.
notes: Rootstock and vine age add further variation and must be measured locally.

title: FAO — Fluvisols: hydromorphic soils of alluvial flood plains
provenance: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization soil reference
summary: Describes stratified recent alluvial soils ranging from coarse to fine, acid to alkaline and nutrient-rich to poor, often but not invariably fertile, flat and groundwater- or flood-influenced.
notes: Fluvisol parent material may include deposits broader than strict geological alluvium; lacustrine facies should be named separately.

title: Journal of Experimental Botany — elevated temperature and organic-acid degradation in ripening grape
summary: Shows stage-dependent effects of day and night warming on malate degradation during ripening, supporting a qualified cool-berry effect but not the blanket preservation of all organic acids or aroma precursors.
notes: No single Serbian cultivar or night-temperature threshold is established.

title: PLOS One — vineyard canopy versus standard weather-station temperature
summary: Demonstrates material differences between canopy/berry-zone and standard weather-station temperature, supporting the card's insistence on direct plant-zone measurements.
notes: Canopy temperature is not identical to berry temperature; both may be needed for a mechanistic claim.

title: International Journal of Climatology — Contributing factors to Koshava wind characteristics
summary: Finds Košava usually concentrated in the cold part of the year and driven by pressure-gradient gap-flow conditions, supporting a seasonal maximum but not an exclusive October–April season.
notes: Abstract-level evidence does not itself quantify every warm-season event or vineyard effect.

title: Grapes Extension — Wind Damage to Grapevines
provenance: University guidance reviewed by Cornell and Texas A&M specialists
summary: Documents shoot and leaf damage, fruit rubbing, trellis risk and possible flowering/fertilisation effects from strong growing-season wind, refuting a categorical no-effect inference when Košava occurs during vegetation.
notes: It does not quantify the effect of Košava on a specific Serbian vineyard or vintage.

title: CEVVIN — Prokupac cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar and register profile
summary: Documents Prokupac names, late ripening, thick blue-black skin, refreshing red/ruby wine, astringency under longer extraction and leading Serbian planting areas, supporting old local identity and a variable structural profile.
notes: The page does not establish a securely dated medieval origin or a universal descriptor list.

title: PSSS — Kakav je prokupac kao grožđe, a kakav kao vino
provenance: Serbian Agricultural Advisory and Expert Service author republished by Dobro Jutro
summary: Describes Prokupac as medium/high-vigour and productive and recommends permeable, loose, stony-gravelly, moderately fertile soils, supporting the management concern but not automatic carbon diversion from crop to leaves.
notes: No paired fertility treatment or measured canopy-to-crop allocation is published.

title: SerbianWine.rs — Tamjanika: Serbia’s Aromatic White Wine
summary: Treats white Tamjanika as Serbia's intensely aromatic Muscat Blanc expression and lists jasmine, elderflower, orange blossom, citrus, grape, peach and herbs; it also explains that floral-fruit aroma can suggest sweetness in a dry wine.
notes: Editorial guide, not a genetic passport, historical primary record or rank study.

title: Tamjanika.rs — Grožđe tamjanika
provenance: Serbian specialist narrative explicitly discussing uncertainty
summary: Calls derivation from tamjan the most logical theory and says approximately 500 years in Serbia is often mentioned without clear evidence; it also warns that multiple local clones and imported Muscat forms can pass under the name Tamjanika.
notes: Useful because it exposes rather than resolves the traditional claims; it is not a peer-reviewed etymology or archival study.

title: Food Chemistry — effects of wine volatiles on taste and astringency perception
summary: Finds that wine volatiles can alter taste judgments and that congruent fruit aroma can increase perceived sweetness in dry wine without a corresponding sugar addition.
notes: The experiment is not Tamjanika-specific and does not remove the roles of residual sugar, alcohol and acidity.

title: CEVVIN — Bagrina cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar/register profile
summary: Defines Bagrina as an old Balkan white-wine cultivar with reddish skin and its largest Serbian commercial concentration in Negotinska Krajina; displayed synonyms include Bagrina crvena/Bagrina roșie.
notes: The exact book form Crvena Dinka is not supplied by this strongest displayed source.

title: Darko Jakšić, ed. — Sorta vinove loze Bagrina
provenance: CEVVIN, Niš, 2023, 164 pp., sensory section pp. 130–147
summary: Reports 21 2022 microvinifications and a broad, variable set including apple, peach, flowers and occasional honey, mint and spice with sample differences in acidity and bitterness.
notes: The public catalogue identifies the work; page-level sensory details derive from the cited monograph, not marketing copy.

title: CEVVIN — Začinak cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking technical/register profile
summary: Calls Začinak's must partly coloured and the cultivar a bojadiser, describes very dark extract-rich wine and use for colour correction, directly contradicting ‘light juice’ and exclusive skin-only colouring.
notes: It does not publish the distribution of blend percentages across commercial wines.

title: Vino.rs — Konačno pravi Bukovski Cuvée na Grand Tastingu
summary: Reports Bukovski Cuvée 2021 as 68% Prokupac, 25% Začinak and Četereška, providing a current named counterexample to a claimed single-digit Začinak norm.
notes: One prominent example disproves the safe absolute but does not establish the market-average percentage.

title: CEVVIN — Kreaca cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar/register profile
summary: Defines Kreaca as a Balkan regional/autochthonous white concentrated in South Banat, with soft juicy neutral berry, late ripening, lower sugar accumulation and harmonious drinkable wine; Temišvarka is absent from its displayed synonyms.
notes: Regional concentration does not demonstrate exclusive origin in the city of Vršac.

title: Vitis International Variety Catalogue — Kreaca passport 6477
provenance: Julius Kühn-Institut VIVC identity reflected in linked catalogue lists
summary: Uses Kreaca as the identity and lists Banat Riesling/Banati Rizling/Banatski Rizling in the catalogue-derived synonym set; Temišvarka is not present in the accessible specialist cross-checks.
notes: Absence cannot prove that a local folk name never existed, but it blocks presenting it as established without a primary source.

title: Vinogradar, vinogradar–rasadničar, podrumar — Kreaca profile
provenance: Lazar Avramov et al., Zadružna knjiga, Belgrade, 1964
summary: Places Kreaca chiefly in South Banat and in the third ripening epoch, gives modest sugar/alcohol and calls its wine drinkable and harmonious, supporting the technical shorthand with a dated historical baseline.
notes: Yugoslav-era figures and classifications are not current legal specifications.

title: Swisslion-Takovo — Banatski rizling 1L
provenance: Current official product page for Vinarija Drašković
summary: Uses Banatski Rizling as a current product name and lists seven varieties, including Kreaca, Italian Riesling, Rhine Riesling, Župljanka, Smederevka, Rkatsiteli and Chasselas.
notes: The product name must not be mistaken for a declaration that the blend is varietal Kreaca.

title: CEVVIN — Smederevka cultivar profile
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking cultivar/register profile
summary: Describes an old widely grown Balkan/Serbian high-yielding, very late white, capable of high must acidity under high yield and light drinkable wine; it does not supply the exact 7 g/L plus 10.5% pair or ‘king of spritzer’ phrase.
notes: Its displayed analytical value is must acidity in a specific production context, not the book's paired finished-wine analysis.

title: Ivanova-Petropulos et al. — Influence of variety and vintage on Smederevka and Vranec wines
provenance: Original six-vintage physicochemical study using OIV methods
summary: For Smederevka 2018–2023 reports alcohol 10.21–11.0% and total acidity 4.8–7.2 g/L, supporting the broad profile but not a specifically paired 10.5% and about 7 g/L record.
notes: North Macedonian wine series; not automatically representative of all Serbian Smederevka.

title: Rubin — Smederevka
summary: Publishes a Smederevka at 10.5% alcohol and describes freshness but gives no paired total-acidity measurement.
notes: The page's anti-bot state limits current direct extraction; the indexed primary product fact was preserved in the earlier audit.

title: Magyar Bor — Kadarka
summary: Describes Kadarka as pale, elegant, fresh, low-tannin and light to medium-bodied, with low anthocyanins, red berries, cherry and fresh spice, supporting the style while separating pale colour from a simplistic thin-skin cause.
notes: Promotional national source; rot mechanism and Serbian expression require separate evidence.

title: Frontiers in Plant Science — genetic characterization of old Serbian grapevines
summary: Identifies Prokupac as founder of a multigenerational lineage and separately finds Serbian Kadarka parent-offspring related to Heunisch Weiss, without reporting direct Prokupac–Kadarka parentage.
notes: Broad Balkan genetic relationships should not be rewritten as a specific parentage.

title: GuildSomm — Grow Welschriesling/Graševina/Grašac
provenance: Specialist synthesis by Caroline Gilby MW
summary: Explains the Grašac/Graševina/Welschriesling name family, probable grašak association and modern Serbian name revival aimed at distancing the cultivar from Rhine Riesling confusion and mass-market Italian Riesling.
notes: The pea derivation is specialist interpretation, not a demonstrated historical-linguistic proof.

title: Ministry of Agriculture — Green Book 2025, Book II
provenance: Official Serbian Ministry report based on the Vineyard Register, chart 46
summary: Gives Merlot 12%, Cabernet Sauvignon 10%, Chardonnay 9% and Grašac 8% in commercial grape-production vineyards at end-2025, making Grašac second among whites and fourth overall in that stated population.
notes: The register population does not include every household, abandoned or unregistered vine in Serbia.

title: wein.plus — Gewürztraminer
summary: Calls Gewürztraminer by far the most common Traminer form but warns that shared names across Savagnin Rose and Traminer prevent definitive cultivar identity from the bare regional name; broad wine literature supports rose, lychee and spice.
notes: Only openly visible text was used; no premium or obscured material was accessed.

title: Montenegrin Academy of Sciences and Arts — Vranac
provenance: Authoritative national-academy cultivar entry by Vesna Maraš
summary: Documents Crmnica origin, spread into central Serbia, full body, intense ruby colour, blackberry, blueberry and dried spice plus multiple styles, supporting the core geography and structure while not making every descriptor invariant.
notes: Does not itself prescribe decanting or the exact chocolate/cinnamon sequence.

title: Hrvatski jezični portal — vranac
provenance: Croatian lexical database and dictionary entry
summary: Defines vranac as a horse with a vran, black coat, directly supporting the South Slavic lexical meaning behind the wine-grape name.
notes: ‘Stallion’ is a common intensification; the ordinary noun is simply a black-coated horse.

title: Bordeaux.com — How to serve wine
summary: Recommends assessing how a wine opens before decanting and notes that young structured wines generally tolerate air better than old fragile bottles, supporting only a conditional young-Vranac recommendation.
notes: General red-wine guidance, not a Vranac-specific controlled test.

title: University of Belgrade Faculty of Agriculture — Župski bojadiser
provenance: Official profile by the institution that bred the cultivar
summary: Gives coloured juice, extract-rich intensely coloured refreshing quality wine, colour-correction use and additional juice/pigment applications, directly contradicting the absolute ‘not for taste’ wording.
notes: The page does not quantify current varietal bottlings or usual blend percentages.

title: CEVVIN — Župski bojadiser
provenance: Serbian Centre for Viticulture and Winemaking register-derived profile
summary: Confirms coloured juice and refreshing wine used primarily for colour, along with current commercial-area ranking and regional distribution.
notes: Primary use for colour is compatible with, but not identical to, absence of independent sensory interest.

title: English Wikipedia combined review — Serbian wine glossary, soils, Košava and cultivars
provenance: Required English Wikipedia combined B0780–B0809 review
summary: Serbian wine and companion pages supply broad soil, phylloxera, loess, climate, Welschriesling, Gewürztraminer, Vranac and other cultivar context. They do not reproduce the book's source bibliography, CIE palette calculation or date chronology, and lack authoritative Serbian technical coverage for several local soils and grapes; current institution, Green Book rank, genetic, analytical and blend-percentage findings therefore rely on primary and specialist sources.
notes: General encyclopedia statements are not used to infer deterministic soil-to-wine effects or replace current Serbian registries.

title: German Wikipedia combined review — Weinbau in Serbien, Böden and Rebsorten
provenance: Required German Wikipedia combined B0780–B0809 review
summary: German pages give useful definitions for Sandboden, Löss, Rendzina, limestone, granite, Cambisol, Vertisol, Welschriesling and Gewürztraminer and broad Serbian-wine history. They do not establish the internal CIE/date claims, exact Serbian soil terminology, current cultivar rank, Temišvarka, Začinak blend norms, paired Smederevka analysis or Župski Bojadiser's technical potential.
notes: Cross-language taxonomy is treated cautiously and does not force one-to-one equivalence with Serbian vernacular soils.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia combined search — Serbian terroir, soils, Kadarka and regional cultivar names
provenance: Required Hungarian Wikipedia combined B0780–B0809 review
summary: Hungarian pages are particularly useful for homoktalaj, lösz, continental climate, Kadarka, Olaszrizling and Tramini regional context. They contain no reproducible evidence for the book's source list, CIE computation, editorial date, Serbian local-soil correlations, current 2025 rank, Kreaca/Začinak/Bagrina/Smederevka specifics or Župski Bojadiser.
notes: Targeted-search silence documents corpus limits and is neither proof nor disproof of specialist Serbian findings.

title: Serbian Wikipedia combined review — виноградарство, земљишта, кошава и сорте
provenance: Required Serbian Wikipedia local-language combined B0780–B0809 review
summary: Serbian pages provide local terminology for soils, Kalkomelanosol, Smonica, Košava, Tamjanika, Prokupac and Vranac and explicitly allow summer Košava, but coverage and citations are uneven for specialist cultivar identities and current statistics. They do not supply the internal bibliography/CIE/date audit, current Green Book 2025 rank, Temišvarka evidence, Začinak percentage distribution, the paired Smederevka analysis or a full Bojadiser profile.
notes: Local-language relevance does not override CEVVIN, official reports, genetics or the publication's own internal state.

title: Russian Wikipedia combined review — виноделие Сербии, почвы, климат и сорта
provenance: Required Russian Wikipedia combined B0780–B0809 review
summary: Russian pages give broad Serbian wine, loess, Chernozem, Rendzina, alluvium, Welschriesling, Gewürztraminer and Vranac context and directly connect vranac with voronoy. They do not resolve the internal source/date/CIE claims, exact Serbian soil correlations, current 2025 cultivar ranking, disputed local synonyms, blend percentages, Smederevka analytical provenance or Bojadiser's official technical profile.
notes: Broad Russian equivalents are not treated as exact one-to-one Serbian taxonomic translations.

title: Croatian Wikipedia combined search — srpsko vino, tla, košava and regional varieties
provenance: Required Croatian Wikipedia combined B0780–B0809 review
summary: Croatian pages contribute general soil, limestone, alluvium, Graševina, Traminac and Vranac context plus regional language, but do not provide the book's internal audit evidence or robust specific treatment of Serbian Bagrina, Začinak, Kreaca, Smederevka, current Grašac rank and Župski Bojadiser. The vranac dictionary meaning is therefore checked against a dedicated language portal rather than inferred only from wine pages.
notes: Search silence and short local articles are recorded as limitations, not negative evidence against primary Serbian sources.

title: American Meteorological Society — Continentality
provenance: Glossary of Meteorology maintained by the American Meteorological Society
summary: Defines continentality as the degree of landmass influence, opposite oceanicity, and identifies temperature range as a measure, with annual range the convenient conventional form while daily range may be considered separately.
notes: The existence of daily-range usage does not justify defining the whole concept solely as hot days and cold nights without annual or maritime context.

title: wein.plus — Bagrina
summary: Defines Bagrina as a white cultivar of the Romania–Serbia/Hungary border and historical Banat and directly lists Crvena Dinka/Červená Dinka and Braghina forms among its synonyms.
notes: Only openly visible public text was used; regional distribution should not be converted into exclusive origin.

title: Frontiers in Plant Science — genetic characterization of old Serbian grapevines
summary: Identifies Serbian-collected Bagrina samples as Braghina Rosie and reports fifteen matching accessions, independently supporting the wider synonym/identity complex.
notes: The result concerns genotyped accessions and should not be extrapolated to every vine carrying a folk name without identification.

title: Gorjanović et al. — Serbian aromatized wine Bermet: antioxidant activity
provenance: Journal of the Serbian Chemical Society 85(4), peer-reviewed open article
summary: Defines Fruška Gora Bermet as red or white aromatized wine made with herb, fruit and spice extracts, documents strong producer variation and uses wormwood within an experimental multi-botanical recipe.
notes: The analysed commercial recipes remained secret; the experimental formula cannot prove one universal ingredient count or principal herb.

title: Vinarija Vinum — Bermet crveni
provenance: Current official Sremski Karlovci producer page
summary: Describes a sweet red Bermet based on Frankovka with 22 kinds of fruit and spices and recommends 16–18°C with Karlovci kuglof, providing a concrete recipe-count and service example.
notes: One producer example supports neither a universal 20-plus rule nor a universal chilled-dessert temperature.

title: Decanter — DWWA 2026 results revealed
provenance: Official Decanter World Wine Awards results publication
summary: Publishes the dated DWWA scale, judging panel and Serbian Platinum results, exemplifying organiser evidence that can verify competition medals and their exact award taxonomy.
notes: It cannot prove that unrelated producer first-place claims are absent from every other competition or register.

title: Maps of Power — Studenica Monastery
provenance: Austrian Academy of Sciences historical-geography project citing medieval critical editions
summary: Presents a reconstructed later-witness fragment with the Rasina estate village list and an obligation to bring necessary wine to Studenica, supporting transmitted vineyard/wine evidence while requiring textual attribution.
notes: The database is not the lost original and does not make every modernized village identification equally secure.

title: RTK — Pisani tragovi od povelje Stevana Nemanje
provenance: Regional cultural-history retelling citing a local encyclopedia
summary: Gives a shorter modern village list than the scholarly reconstructed fragment, directly illustrating variation among transmitted or retold enumerations.
notes: A regional media retelling is evidence of variant reception, not a substitute for a critical manuscript edition.

title: Politika — Duga tradicija uzgoja vinove loze u Negotinskoj Krajini
provenance: National historical feature citing regional records
summary: Connects Negotin exports to France and other markets with the western European phylloxera crisis and the Danube port at Radujevac, supporting substantial demand and trade context.
notes: It does not provide primary customs proof for the exact two-million-litre or Napoleon-price numbers.

title: Wine Routes in Vojvodina Province, Northern Serbia
summary: Reports more than 10,000 hectares of Vršac vineyards by the late nineteenth century and supplies independent evidence for the region's large scale; its synthesis also shows why period units and dates must be retained.
notes: The article does not itself authenticate every owner, yield or cellar-capacity number and is not a metrological primary source for all forms of juger.

title: Oregon State University — How to scout grape phylloxera in vineyards
provenance: Oregon State University Extension viticulture and entomology guidance
summary: Describes phylloxera as an aphid-like root-feeding insect and explains susceptible own-rooted vines and resistant rootstocks, while documenting that own-rooted vineyard contexts still exist.
notes: A scouting guide supports the modern biology and management mechanism, not a precise country-by-country percentage of nineteenth-century destruction.

title: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources — Rootstock selection
provenance: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources technical guidance
summary: Explains American-derived grape rootstocks and selection for phylloxera, vigour, drought, rooting and soil-lime conditions, emphasizing scion, site and management interactions.
notes: Trait tables do not establish a universal wine-quality ranking between grafted and own-rooted vines.

title: OIV — White wine with maceration
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine code of oenological practices
summary: Defines white wine with maceration through fermentation of white must in prolonged contact with grape pomace, anchoring the orange/amber method and distinguishing it from ordinary early pressing.
notes: The definition sets a process category but does not require tea, nut or any fixed sensory descriptor.

title: Pre-fermentative skin contact in white winemaking — review and experiment
provenance: Peer-reviewed open-access study of white-grape skin contact and extraction
summary: Shows that non-orange white winemaking can use short pre-fermentation skin contact and that time, temperature and cultivar affect phenolics, aroma and colour rather than creating a universal linear result.
notes: One experimental design should not be converted into fixed maceration results for all grape varieties.

title: Comité Champagne — Blending Champagne
summary: Explains blending wines from varieties, crus and years to construct balance and house style, directly supporting the broad technical meaning of assemblage.
notes: Champagne practice is a strong example but not a universal legal definition of varietal wine.

title: OIV — International standard for the labelling of wines
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine labelling standard
summary: Provides the international reference framework under which a single-variety indication may use an 85% threshold, demonstrating that varietal labelling need not mean a chemically pure 100% single-grape wine.
notes: National or appellation rules may impose different or stricter requirements and must be checked for a named wine.

title: Bordeaux.com — Aging wine in barrels
summary: Identifies the Bordeaux barrel/barrique as 225 litres and explains extraction and controlled oxygen interaction during oak ageing, with stronger wood contribution from new cooperage.
notes: It does not standardize how every producer calculates a declared percentage of new oak or prove that used barrels contribute only oxygen.

title: Oak barrel maturation: a review of wood–wine interactions
provenance: Peer-reviewed open-access review of oak compounds, toasting, extraction and oxygen
summary: Reviews oak species, seasoning, grain, toast, barrel age and reuse as interacting controls on aroma compounds, ellagitannins and oxygen exposure; extraction diminishes over fills rather than becoming zero.
notes: Compound and sensory outcomes cannot be mapped to one toast label or new-oak percentage without cooperage and wine details.

title: Cornell University — study of wine aeration and decanting
provenance: Cornell eCommons academic research on exposure of wine to air
summary: Examines how aeration changes wine chemistry and sensory response, supporting bottle- and time-dependent effects rather than a universal immediate chemical softening of tannin.
notes: Service recommendations still require the condition, style and age of the individual bottle.

title: Comité Champagne — Maturation on lees
summary: Explains bottle maturation on lees, yeast autolysis, minimum ageing periods and the development of textural and mature aromatic complexity in Champagne.
notes: Champagne-specific minimums and descriptors should not be imposed unchanged on every still sur-lie wine.

title: Comité Champagne — Bottling and second fermentation
summary: Documents tirage and secondary fermentation in the same bottle later sold after maturation, riddling and disgorgement, providing the canonical traditional-method sequence.
notes: The page establishes process and time, while relative cost versus tank production remains scale-dependent.

title: IVES — leaf-to-fruit ratios in grapevine: a systematic review
provenance: IVES Open Science peer-reviewed synthesis of source–sink balance and crop manipulation
summary: Synthesizes variable responses of ripening and composition to leaf area, crop load and thinning across cultivars and environments, contradicting universal fertile-site and poor-soil rules.
notes: Effects require measured crop load and canopy function; no fixed pool of sugar, acid and colour is simply divided among bunches.

title: Australian Wine Research Institute — managing canopy and disease pressure
provenance: Australian Wine Research Institute technical guidance
summary: Links canopy density and management with airflow, drying, spray penetration and fungal-disease risk around grape clusters.
notes: The ideal degree of exposure varies with weather, cultivar and training system.

title: Vineyard row orientation and slope effects on grape microclimate
provenance: Peer-reviewed open-access field study of vineyard solar exposure and microclimate
summary: Quantifies how orientation and site geometry alter intercepted radiation and canopy or berry conditions, supporting the general aspect mechanism while showing dependence on latitude, angle and time.
notes: Row orientation and slope aspect are related but distinct variables and must not be conflated in a site description.

title: Iron chlorosis responses of grapevine under calcareous conditions
summary: Explains reduced iron availability and chlorosis risk under alkaline, calcareous or bicarbonate conditions and shows genotype/rootstock-dependent responses.
notes: Soil pH alone is not a complete diagnostic; bicarbonate, active lime, water and rootstock matter.

title: OIV — Definition of vitivinicultural terroir
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine resolution
summary: Defines terroir through collective knowledge of interactions between an identifiable physical and biological environment and applied vitivinicultural practices that confer distinctive characteristics.
notes: The resolution does not say that every cellar choice weighs equally with site, nor that terroir is a literal flavour of soil.

title: Pravilnik o rejonizaciji vinogradarskih geografskih proizvodnih područja Srbije
provenance: Public consolidated text citing Službeni glasnik RS 45/2015 and 18/2024
summary: Defines region, rejon, vinogorje, localitet/potes and oases and enumerates their nesting, proving that vinogorje is below rejon but can have smaller named units beneath it.
notes: The legal viticultural unit is not an administrative equivalent of a French commune.

title: Comité Champagne — Disgorgement
summary: Explains neck freezing, opening the temporary closure and ejection of the frozen lees plug by internal bottle pressure, followed by topping and dosage; also describes manual disgorgement without freezing.
notes: The frozen plug is not pushed by the final cork, which is inserted later.

title: Comité Champagne — Dosage
provenance: Official Comité Champagne production-method and sweetness-category explanation
summary: Describes topping after disgorgement with dosage liquid and gives sweetness categories, including brut nature as no added sugar with less than 3 g/L residual sugar.
notes: No added sugar does not mean chemically zero total sugar, and topping wine can still replace disgorgement loss.

title: INAO — Clairette de Die ancestral method specification
provenance: French national origin-and-quality institute appellation specification
summary: Documents an ancestral sparkling method in which ongoing primary fermentation continues in bottle and retains carbon dioxide, anchoring the one-fermentation mechanism behind pét-nat.
notes: A protected Clairette de Die specification is not a universal requirement that every pét-nat remain cloudy or undisgorged.

title: IVES — controlled 30 L microvinification trials
provenance: IVES Open Science experimental winemaking study
summary: Uses replicated small 30-litre lots to compare controlled winemaking conditions, illustrating microvinification as an experimental scale rather than a rigid universal volume boundary.
notes: Other published protocols use smaller or larger volumes, and vessel geometry can itself affect the outcome.

title: Own-rooted versus grafted grapevines — systematic evidence review
provenance: Peer-reviewed open-access review of paired rootstock and own-rooted comparisons
summary: Reviews direct comparisons of own-rooted and grafted vines, finding site- and combination-dependent effects on vine function and wine composition but no universal wine-quality superiority.
notes: The evidence directly contradicts ‘nothing to compare’ while leaving individual site effects open.

title: Austrian Wine — Leithaberg including Ruster Ausbruch DAC
provenance: Official Austrian Wine Marketing Board regional and legal-category guide
summary: Identifies Ruster Ausbruch DAC as a protected Rust-origin nobly sweet wine corresponding broadly to Trockenbeerenauslese and made from grapes grown in the Free City of Rust.
notes: The modern DAC does not by itself define every historical Habsburg or Karlovci use of the word Ausbruch.

title: Sima P. Lazić — Vinogradarstvo i vinarstvo Fruške Gore, Ausbruch and Bermet
provenance: Matica srpska 1982 monograph in public transcription
summary: Documents historical Fruška Gora sweet wines, suškovo vino, samotok, suvarak material, natural and artificial grape drying and varied Bermet technologies and recipes.
notes: The monograph shows that suvarak is not safely interchangeable with every finished-wine name and that current recipes should not be projected backward.

title: Hungarian National Archives — Historical land measures
provenance: Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár reference table citing Bogdán István's historical metrology
summary: Lists katasztrális hold/Katastraljoch as 1,600 square öl and distinguishes variable regional hold measures, providing the authoritative base for the approximately 0.5755-hectare conversion.
notes: A historical Serbian source must still be checked to ensure its jutro means the cadastral unit rather than another local measure.

title: CEVVIN — Probus
provenance: Center for Viticulture and Enology of Serbia cultivar profile
summary: Gives Kadarka × Cabernet Sauvignon parentage, 1983 recognition, blue-black berries and intensely coloured wine for Probus.
notes: The exact breeding-centre institutional name is better supplied by the university and international register than by shorthand ‘Novi Sad institute’.

title: CEVVIN — Sila
provenance: Center for Viticulture and Enology of Serbia cultivar profile
summary: Identifies Sila as Ružica/Kevedinka × Chardonnay from the Sremski Karlovci breeding programme and describes its harmonious, refreshing wine profile and current commercial presence.
notes: The profile does not make ‘medium-bodied’ a fixed analytical class or Ausbruch a defining use.

title: VIVC — PETRA passport
provenance: Vitis International Variety Catalogue, Julius Kühn-Institut
summary: Records PETRA as a Serbian blanc cultivar from KUNBARAT × PINOT NOIR, with breeders connected to the Sremski Karlovci/Novi Sad programme.
notes: The passport establishes identity, not the frequency or purpose of its use in sweet blends.

title: Vina Srbije — Ausbruch, Vinarija Milutinović
provenance: Public Serbian producer and product directory
summary: Lists Sila, Petra and Beli Burgundac in a current Milutinović Ausbruch and describes late harvest, suvarak and botanicals, proving one specific modern Karlovci blend and terminology use.
notes: A single product cannot define the whole Ausbruch category or the ordinary vinification of either cultivar.

title: Vino.rs — Legendarna vina: Banatski rizling
provenance: Serbian specialist retrospective with former chief enologist Aleksandar Ivkov
summary: Documents the historical mass-market Vršac wine, its changing reputation and current Drašković continuation, including a modern seven-variety formula rather than an immutable four-grape recipe.
notes: Some historical quantities are oral recollection; a product name in use is not proof of exclusive trademark registration.

title: Vino & Fino — Rkaciteli će se od sada gajiti i u Francuskoj
summary: Calls Rkatsiteli a very old Georgian cultivar, dates notable Serbian presence to the 1970s and highlights cold tolerance and high acidity.
notes: It does not establish bloc-wide planting motives, a national age map, the near-absence of new vines or intrinsic flavour neutrality.

title: CEVVIN — Slankamenka / Grupa Plovina
provenance: Center for Viticulture and Enology of Serbia cultivar inventory
summary: Uses the official Serbian group spelling Plovina, includes Slankamenka Crvena forms and describes a very old Balkan cultivar producing harmonious, drinkable, thin and lower-alcohol wine.
notes: The institutional grouping does not by itself prove that every folk-named accession is genetically identical Pamid.

title: Frontiers in Plant Science — genetic characterization of old Serbian grapevines
summary: Genotyped old Serbian vines and identified 29 samples as Pamid, commonly prospected under Plovdina or Lisičina field names.
notes: The published study does not independently tie those Pamid samples to the named Leposavić producer site.

title: CEVVIN — Tamjanika crna
provenance: Official Serbian cultivar and commercial-vineyard profile
summary: Reports Tamjanika crna as a separately tracked dark cultivar and places it thirty-fifth by represented commercial vineyard area in the cited inventory.
notes: The rank belongs to the survey denominator and date, not an eternal all-vine national order.

title: Slow Food Ark of Taste — Black Tamjanika Wine
summary: Documents rare traditional Black Tamjanika wine in Negotinska Krajina and its pronounced aromatic Muscat character.
notes: General aromatic character does not guarantee berry and spice descriptors in every vintage or identify the cultivar without genetics.

title: National Tourism Organisation of Serbia — Authentic from Serbia
summary: Defines classic Serbian sarma with sauerkraut leaves, minced meat, rice and spices and separately notes summer vine-leaf sarma, demonstrating both the canonical form and the wider category.
notes: The page does not prescribe a unique wine pairing from acidity and fat alone.

title: National Tourism Organisation of Serbia — All the flavors of the south
provenance: Official national Serbian tourism guide to Leskovac cuisine
summary: Presents Leskovac as Serbia's iconic barbecue centre and translates vešalica specifically as pork loin while listing mućkalica among the regional grill dishes.
notes: The tourism page establishes regional identity and the pork cut but does not standardize every restaurant's mućkalica or Leskovački voz format.

title: DIAM — Our guarantees
provenance: Official DIAM closure technology and analytical guarantee page
summary: Describes supercritical-CO₂ cleaning of cork granules, controlled permeability and a releasable-TCA guarantee at the stated analytical threshold.
notes: A closure guarantee addresses closure-derived TCA and consistency, not all possible pre-bottling, microbial, oxidation or storage faults.

title: Whole-bunch and stem inclusion in red winemaking — review
provenance: Peer-reviewed open-access review of whole-cluster and stem chemistry and sensory effects
summary: Reviews rachis/stem inclusion effects on tannin, astringency, acidity and green or herbal aromas and emphasizes cultivar, maturity, inclusion rate and extraction conditions.
notes: The source does not make bitterness automatic for every visually unripe stem.

title: English Wikipedia combined review — final wine glossary and Serbian historical terms
provenance: Requested English Wikipedia comparison corpus across dedicated pages and targeted search
summary: Provides broad definitions for phylloxera, grafting, maceration, blending, barrels, sparkling methods, terroir, food and major grapes, while many Serbia-specific cultivars, local historical numbers and producer claims are absent or thin.
notes: Wikipedia context was compared with primary and specialist sources and was not used to turn missing coverage into proof of falsehood.

title: German Wikipedia combined review — Weinbegriffe, Reblaus and Balkan varieties
provenance: Requested German Wikipedia comparison corpus across dedicated pages and targeted search
summary: Offers strong general technical coverage for Reblaus, Unterlage, Maischestandzeit, Barrique and sparkling-wine terms and some Central European measures or grapes, but sparse coverage of Serbian microhistory and new cultivars.
notes: German-language terminology helps expose overbroad absolutes but does not independently verify Serbia-specific rankings, recipes or producer records.

title: Hungarian Wikipedia combined review — borászati fogalmak, katasztrális hold and regional grapes
provenance: Requested Hungarian Wikipedia comparison corpus across dedicated pages and targeted search
summary: Adds Central European terminology for phylloxera, barrels, sweet-wine traditions and historical land measures, with uneven or absent entries for most Serbian-created cultivars and local legends.
notes: The corpus is useful for katasztrális hold and regional names but cannot establish every exact historical conversion or Serbian product composition.

title: Serbian Wikipedia combined review — вински појмови, историја и домаће сорте
provenance: Requested Serbian Wikipedia comparison corpus across dedicated pages and targeted search
summary: Supplies the closest local-language context for Bermet, Serbian wine history, food and terminology but remains incomplete for manuscript criticism, regulatory hierarchy, experimental viticulture and several locally bred cultivars.
notes: Local-language proximity does not make unsourced exact numbers, rankings, producer claims or tasting descriptors independent evidence.

title: Russian Wikipedia combined review — винодельческие термины, история Сербии и сорта
provenance: Requested Russian Wikipedia comparison corpus across dedicated pages and targeted search
summary: Provides Russian definitions for general viticulture and sparkling-wine vocabulary and broad Serbian wine context, while many Serbian proper names, fine zoning distinctions and exact historical claims are absent.
notes: Russian lexical convenience, including rough analogies, was not treated as legal equivalence or primary historical documentation.

title: Croatian Wikipedia combined review — vino, Bermet, regional food and grape terminology
provenance: Requested Croatian Wikipedia comparison corpus across dedicated pages and targeted search
summary: Adds neighbouring South Slavic usage for Bermet, wine methods, Balkan grapes and food, while coverage of Serbian zoning, breeding records and exact historical statistics remains incomplete.
notes: Cross-border shared terms help detect false exclusivity but do not make Croatian traditions identical to Serbian products or regulations.

title: eGastro — Otkrijte tajne leskovačkog roštilja
provenance: Regional gastronomy feature quoting a named restaurant's service format
summary: Describes Leskovački voz as a sequence of distinct grill components—filled pljeskavica followed by skewers, sausages and a mućkalica ‘carriage’—rather than one homogeneous mixed dish.
notes: This is one restaurant's realization of the traditional idea, so exact components are not universal; it supports the train-like succession rather than a fixed recipe.

title: Matalj Vinarija — current wines index
provenance: Official producer website current wines index
summary: The current official wines index lists Dušica Rosé and links an official product page, but the accessible index provides neither a vintage nor a varietal composition.
notes: This supports current portfolio presence only; it cannot resolve the 2024 blend or percentages.

title: Matalj Vinarija — Dušica Rosé official product page
provenance: Official producer product page reached from the current wines index
summary: The product URL was live but exposed only a verification challenge at review time, with no readable vintage-specific technical sheet or composition.
notes: Access failure is not evidence for either composition; a producer technical sheet or bottle label for vintage 2024 remains necessary.

title: ICPDR — The future of the Danube River Basin
provenance: International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River climate-adaptation assessment
summary: The basin-wide assessment describes projected warming and winter hydrological change in the Danube basin, but provides no paired present-day shore-versus-inland temperature or frost observations for a Serbian vineyard.
notes: It is relevant climate context, not proof that the Danube moderates winter frost immediately beside a particular Serbian bank; a local station-pair or vineyard microclimate study is still required.

title: OIV International Code of Oenological Practices — Maceration
provenance: International Organisation of Vine and Wine normative oenological definition
summary: Defines maceration as contact between the solid and liquid parts of grapes for a more or less extended period to dissolve phenolic compounds, aromas and their precursors; the duration is adapted to the intended objective rather than a universal ceiling.
notes: The definition supports the corrected non-absolute time wording; it does not prescribe a universal rosé duration or replace bottle- or method-specific technical data.

title: Правно-информациони систем РС / Службени гласник — Правилник о рејонизацији виноградарских географских производних подручја Србије
provenance: Official Legal Information System of the Republic of Serbia, official-gazette record for the zoning rulebook (SG RS 45/2015, amended 18/2024)
summary: Official record for the Serbian zoning rulebook governing names and boundaries of viticultural geographical production areas. Its current official text is the controlling legal source for Subotički rejon and the separate Severnometohočki and Južnometohočki rejons.
notes: The official interface requires JavaScript; the official-gazette record, not the earlier third-party transcription, controls the legal classification.

title: Правно-информациони систем РС / Службени гласник — Правилник о начину паковања, декларисања и обележавања вина
provenance: Official Legal Information System of the Republic of Serbia, Službeni glasnik RS 55/2023, ministerial rulebook
summary: Official record for the current Serbian wine labelling rulebook. The crop-year provision makes the year optional and conditions its use on at least 85% of the product being made from grapes harvested in that year, with the prescribed administrative evidence.
notes: The official PIS/gazette record controls the legal conclusion; use of berba before a year is a separate current-language observation, not a mandated label position.

title: Decanter World Wine Awards 2026 — Producer: Erdevik
provenance: Official Decanter World Wine Awards results database, producer result page
summary: Official DWWA 2026 result identifies Erdevik Marlon Delon Cabernet Sauvignon-Merlot 2017, Serbia, Srem, Fruška Gora, as Gold with 95 points.
notes: Exact competition-primary confirmation for producer, wine, vintage, competition year and Gold medal; it replaces reliance on a national announcement for this award fact.

CIVP / Vins de Provence — Elaboration of Rosé
provenance: Conseil Interprofessionnel des Vins de Provence, regional wine-body technical explanation
summary: Описывает мацерационный метод розе Прованса с выдержкой сусла 2–20 часов при 16–20 °C и последующим отделением после достижения желаемого цвета. Отличает прямое прессование без предварительной мацерации и saignée.
notes: Прямая поддержка регионального примера конкретного метода. Не доказывает универсальную длительность всех розе, сербскую норму или абсолютный верхний предел. Поиск и чтение выполнены 2026-09-05.
